ध्यायेदात्मानमव्यक्तं परात्परतरं विभुमट् ॥
1.33.m: In the eight-spoked lotus of the heart, twelve finger-breadths wide, / one should meditate on the unmanifest Self, higher than the highest, the omnipresent Lord.

1.33.s:
dhyānaṃ sadbhinirgaditaṃ pratyayasyaikatānatā /
dhyānaṃ kṛtvā muhurttaṃ vā paraṃ mokṣaṃ labhennaraḥ //
1.33.d:
ध्यानं सद्भिनिर्गदितं प्रत्ययस्यैकतानता ।
ध्यानं कृत्वा मुहुर्त्तं वा परं मोक्षं लभेन्नरः ॥
1.33.m: Through meditation sins are destroyed; through meditation one obtains liberation; / through meditation Hari is pleased; through meditation all aims are achieved.

1.33.s:
dhyānātpāpāni naśyanti dhyānānmokṣaṃ ca vindati /
dhyānātprasīdati hariddharyānātsarvārthasādhanam //
1.33.d:
ध्यानात्पापानि नश्यन्ति ध्यानान्मोक्षं च विन्दति ।
ध्यानात्प्रसीदति हरिद्धर्यानात्सर्वार्थसाधनम् ॥
1.33.m: Whatever form of Mahāviṣṇu [one chooses], upon that one should meditate with concentrated mind; / pleased in spirit by that meditation, Hari indeed grants liberation.

1.33.s:
yadyadrūpaṃ mahāviṣṇostattaddhyāyetsamāhitam /
tena dhyānena tuṣṭātmā harirmokṣaṃ dadāti vai //
1.33.d:
यद्यद्रूपं महाविष्णोस्तत्तद्ध्यायेत्समाहितम् ।
तेन ध्यानेन तुष्टात्मा हरिर्मोक्षं ददाति वै ॥
1.33.m: One should make the mind unwavering upon the object of meditation, O best of the virtuous, / so that meditation, the object of meditation, and the state of the meditator completely vanish.

1.33.s:
acañcalaṃ manaḥ kuryāddhyeye vastuni sattama /
dhyānaṃ dhyeyaṃ dhyātṛbhāvaṃ yathā naśyati nirbharam //
1.33.d:
अचञ्चलं मनः कुर्याद्ध्येये वस्तुनि सत्तम ।
ध्यानं ध्येयं ध्यातृभावं यथा नश्यति निर्भरम् ॥
1.33.m: Then immortality arises from the enjoyment of the nectar of knowledge; / from unbroken meditation comes the realization of non-difference.

1.33.s:
tato 'mṛtatvaṃ bhavati jñānāmṛtaniṣevaṇāt /
bhavennirantaraṃ dhyānādabhedapratipādanam //
1.33.d:
ततो ऽमृतत्वं भवति ज्ञानामृतनिषेवणात् ।
भवेन्निरन्तरं ध्यानादभेदप्रतिपादनम् ॥
1.33.m: Joined with supreme bliss as if in deep sleep, with the senses ceased, / standing steady like a lamp in a windless place—this is called samādhi.

1.33.s:
suṣutpivatparānandayuktaścoparatendriyaḥ /
nirvātadīpavatsaṃsthaḥ samādhirabhidhīyate //
1.33.d:
सुषुत्पिवत्परानन्दयुक्तश्चोपरतेन्द्रियः ।
निर्वातदीपवत्संस्थः समाधिरभिधीयते ॥
1.33.m: In the state of samādhi the yogin does not hear, does not see, / does not smell, does not touch, and speaks nothing at all, O best of the virtuous.

1.33.s:
yogī samādhyavasthāyāṃ na śṛṇoti na paśyati /
na jighrati na spṛśati na kiñcadvakti sattama //
1.33.d:
योगी समाध्यवस्थायां न शृणोति न पश्यति ।
न जिघ्रति न स्पृशति न किञ्चद्वक्ति सत्तम ॥
1.33.m: The Self, however, is spotless, pure, the embodiment of being, consciousness, and bliss, / released from all adjuncts; to yogins it shines unwavering.

1.33.s:
ātmā tu nirmalaḥ śuddhaḥ sañcidānandavigrahaḥ /
sarvopādhivinirmukto yogināṃ bhātyacañcalaḥ //
1.33.d:
आत्मा तु निर्मलः शुद्धः सञ्चिदानन्दविग्रहः ।
सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्तो योगिनां भात्यचञ्चलः ॥
1.33.m: Though devoid of qualities, the supreme God seems possessed of qualities through ignorance; / but upon the destruction of ignorance, [the Self] remains established as it was before.

1.33.s:
nirguṇo 'pi paro devo hyajñānādguṇavāniva /
vibhātyajñānanāśe tu yathāpūrvaṃ vyavasthitam //
1.33.d:
निर्गुणो ऽपि परो देवो ह्यज्ञानाद्गुणवानिव ।
विभात्यज्ञाननाशे तु यथापूर्वं व्यवस्थितम् ॥
1.33.m: The supreme light, immeasurable in essence, seems possessed of māyā to the illusory; / upon its destruction, the spotless Brahman reveals itself to the wise.

1.33.s:
paraṃ jyotirameyātmā māyāvāniva māyinām /
tannāśe nirmalaṃ brahma prakāśayati paṇḍitaṃ //
1.33.d:
परं ज्योतिरमेयात्मा मायावानिव मायिनाम् ।
तन्नाशे निर्मलं ब्रह्म प्रकाशयति पण्डितं ॥
1.33.m: One alone and without a second, supreme light, taintless, / existing as the inner ruler within all beings.

1.33.s:
ekamevādvitīyaṃ ca paraṃ jyotirnirañjanam /
sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāmantaryāmitayā sthitam //
1.33.d:
एकमेवाद्वितीयं च परं ज्योतिर्निरञ्जनम् ।
सर्वेषामेव भूतानामन्तर्यामितया स्थितम् ॥
1.33.m: Smaller than the small, greater than the great, the eternal Self is the cause of the entire universe; / the foremost among knowers of knowledge behold it, higher than the highest, supremely pure.

1.33.s:
aṇoraṇīyānmahato mahīyānsanātanātmākhilaviśvahetuḥ /
paśyanti yajjñānavidāṃ variṣṭāḥ parātparasmātparamaṃ pavitram //
1.33.d:
अणोरणीयान्महतो महीयान्सनातनात्माखिलविश्वहेतुः ।
पश्यन्ति यज्ज्ञानविदां वरिष्टाः परात्परस्मात्परमं पवित्रम् ॥
1.33.m: Arranged in the division of letters from "a" to "kṣa", / the ancient, beginningless Person is sung of as Śabdabrahman.

1.33.s:
akārādikṣakārāntavarṇabhedavyavasthitaḥ /
purāṇapuruṣo 'nādiḥ śabdabrahmeti gīyate //
1.33.d:
अकारादिक्षकारान्तवर्णभेदव्यवस्थितः ।
पुराणपुरुषो ऽनादिः शब्दब्रह्मेति गीयते ॥
1.33.m: Completely pure, imperishable, eternal, full, dwelling in the midst of ether, / bliss, spotless and tranquil, it is sung of as the supreme Brahman.

1.33.s:
viśuddamakṣaraṃ nityaṃ pūrṇamākāśamadhyagam /
ānandaṃ nirmalaśāntaṃ paraṃ brahmeti gīyate //
1.33.d:
विशुद्दमक्षरं नित्यं पूर्णमाकाशमध्यगम् ।
आनन्दं निर्मलशान्तं परं ब्रह्मेति गीयते ॥
1.33.m: Yogins behold within the heart the eternal supreme Self; / changeless, unborn, pure, it is sung of as the supreme Brahman.

1.33.s:
yogino hṛdi paśyanti parātmānaṃ sanātanam /
avikāramajaṃ śuddhaṃ paraṃ brahmeti gīyate //
1.33.d:
योगिनो हृदि पश्यन्ति परात्मानं सनातनम् ।
अविकारमजं शुद्धं परं ब्रह्मेति गीयते ॥
1.33.m: I shall describe another meditation, listen, O best of sages, / which is like a shower of nectar for men scorched by the heat of worldly existence.

1.33.s:
dhyānamanyatpravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva muni sattama /
saṃsāratāpatatpānāṃ sudhāvṛṣṭisamaṃ nṛṇām //
1.33.d:
ध्यानमन्यत्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्व मुनि सत्तम ।
संसारतापतत्पानां सुधावृष्टिसमं नृणाम् ॥
1.33.m: One should remember Nārāyaṇa, supreme bliss, residing in the praṇava, / whose form is sound, incomparable, standing above the half-mora.

1.33.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ parānandaṃ smaretpraṇavasaṃsthitam /
nādarupamanaupamyamarddhamātroparisthitam //
1.33.d:
नारायणं परानन्दं स्मरेत्प्रणवसंस्थितम् ।
नादरुपमनौपम्यमर्द्धमात्रोपरिस्थितम् ॥
1.33.m: The letter "a" has the form of Brahmā; the letter "u" possesses the form of Viṣṇu; / the letter "m" is the form of Rudra; the half-mora consists of the supreme.

1.33.s:
akāraṃ brahmaṇo rupamukāraṃ viṣṇurupavat /
makāraṃ rudrarupaṃ syādardhdamātraṃ parātmakam //
1.33.d:
अकारं ब्रह्मणो रुपमुकारं विष्णुरुपवत् ।
मकारं रुद्ररुपं स्यादर्ध्दमात्रं परात्मकम् ॥
1.33.m: Three morae are declared, presided over by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva; / their combination, O brāhmaṇa, awakens [knowledge of] the supreme Brahman.

1.33.s:
mātrāstistraḥ samākhyātā brahmaviṣṇu śivādhipāḥ /
teṣāṃ samuccayaṃ vipra parabrahmaprabodhakam //
1.33.d:
मात्रास्तिस्त्रः समाख्याता ब्रह्मविष्णु शिवाधिपाः ।
तेषां समुच्चयं विप्र परब्रह्मप्रबोधकम् ॥
1.33.m: The signified is the supreme Brahman; the signifier is said to be the praṇava; / the connection between signified and signifier between the two, O twice-born, is figurative.

1.33.s:
vācyaṃ tu paramaṃ brahma vācakaḥ praṇavaḥ smṛtaḥ /
vācyavācakasaṃbandho hyupacārāttayordvijā //
1.33.d:
वाच्यं तु परमं ब्रह्म वाचकः प्रणवः स्मृतः ।
वाच्यवाचकसंबन्धो ह्युपचारात्तयोर्द्विजा ॥
1.33.m: Reciting the praṇava daily, they are freed from all sins; / united with its practice, they attain supreme liberation.

1.33.s:
japantaḥ praṇavaṃ nityaṃ mucyante sarvapātakaiḥ /
tadabhyāsena saṃyuktāḥ paraṃ mokṣaṃ labhanti ca //
1.33.d:
जपन्तः प्रणवं नित्यं मुच्यन्ते सर्वपातकैः ।
तदभ्यासेन संयुक्ताः परं मोक्षं लभन्ति च ॥
1.33.m: Reciting the praṇava mantra, which consists of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, / one should meditate within oneself on the spotless radiance equal to ten million suns.

1.33.s:
japaṃśca praṇavaṃ mantraṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivātmakam /
koṭisūryasamaṃ tejo dhyāyedātmani nirmalam //
1.33.d:
जपंश्च प्रणवं मन्त्रं ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवात्मकम् ।
कोटिसूर्यसमं तेजो ध्यायेदात्मनि निर्मलम् ॥
1.33.m: Either in the form of a śālagrāma stone or in the form of an image, / or whatever object removes sin, upon that one should meditate in the heart.

1.33.s:
śālagrāmaśilārupaṃ pratimārupameva vā /
yadyatpāpaharaṃ vastu tattadvā cintayeddhṛdi //
1.33.d:
शालग्रामशिलारुपं प्रतिमारुपमेव वा ।
यद्यत्पापहरं वस्तु तत्तद्वा चिन्तयेद्धृदि ॥
1.33.m: This Vaiṣṇava knowledge which has been told to you, O lord of sages— / having known this, the foremost yogin attains supreme liberation.

1.33.s:
yadetaddaiṣṇavaṃ jñānaṃ kathitaṃ te munīśvara /
etadviditvā yogīndro labhate mokṣamuttamam //
1.33.d:
यदेतद्दैष्णवं ज्ञानं कथितं ते मुनीश्वर ।
एतद्विदित्वा योगीन्द्रो लभते मोक्षमुत्तमम् ॥
1.33.m: Whoever either hears this or recites it with a concentrated mind, / freed from all sins, attains the world of Hari.

1.33.s:
yastvetacchṛāṇuyādvāpi paṭhedvāpi samāhitaḥ /
sa sarvapāpanirmukto harisālokyamānpuyāt //
iti śrībṛnnāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde yoganirupaṇaṃ nāma trayastriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.33.d:
यस्त्वेतच्छृआणुयाद्वापि पठेद्वापि समाहितः ।
स सर्वपापनिर्मुक्तो हरिसालोक्यमान्पुयात् ॥
इति श्रीबृन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे योगनिरुपणं नाम त्रयस्त्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.33.m:
Thus ends the thirty-third chapter, named the Exposition of Yoga, in the first quarter of the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

Nārada said: / All the limbs of yoga have been fully explained, O great sage; / now too, O omniscient one, tell me what I ask.

1.34.s:
nārada uvāca
samākhyātāni sarvāṇi yogāṅgāni mahāmune /
idānīmapi sarvajña yatpṛcchāmi taducyatām //
1.34.d:
नारद उवाच
समाख्यातानि सर्वाणि योगाङ्गानि महामुने ।
इदानीमपि सर्वज्ञ यत्पृच्छामि तदुच्यताम् ॥
1.34.m: It was spoken by you that yoga succeeds only for those with devotion; / and he with whom the Lord of all is pleased has eternal devotion.

1.34.s:
yogobhaktimatāmeva sidhyatīti tvayoditam /
yasya tuṣyati sarveśastasya bhaktiśca śāśvatam //
1.34.d:
योगोभक्तिमतामेव सिध्यतीति त्वयोदितम् ।
यस्य तुष्यति सर्वेशस्तस्य भक्तिश्च शाश्वतम् ॥
1.34.m: In what manner the Lord of all, the God of gods, Janārdana, is pleased, / tell me that, O omniscient sage, ocean of compassion.

1.34.s:
yathā tuṣyati sarveśo devadevo janārdanaḥ /
tanmamākhyāhi sarvajña mune kāruṇyavāridhe //
1.34.d:
यथा तुष्यति सर्वेशो देवदेवो जनार्दनः ।
तन्ममाख्याहि सर्वज्ञ मुने कारुण्यवारिधे ॥
1.34.m: Sanaka said: / Worship Nārāyaṇa, the supreme God, the embodiment of being, consciousness, and bliss, / with your whole being, O brāhmaṇa, if you desire liberation.

1.34.s:
sanaka uvāca
nārāyaṇaṃ paraṃ devaṃ saccidānandavigraham /
bhaja sarvātmanā vipra yadi muktimabhīpsasi //
1.34.d:
सनक उवाच
नारायणं परं देवं सच्चिदानन्दविग्रहम् ।
भज सर्वात्मना विप्र यदि मुक्तिमभीप्ससि ॥
1.34.m: Enemies do not harm him, the planetary forces do not afflict him, / and demons do not cast their gaze upon a man devoted to Viṣṇu.

1.34.s:
ripavastaṃ na hiṃsanti na bādhante grahāścatam /
rākṣasāśca na cekṣante naraṃ viṣṇuparāyaṇam //
1.34.d:
रिपवस्तं न हिंसन्ति न बाधन्ते ग्रहाश्चतम् ।
राक्षसाश्च न चेक्षन्ते नरं विष्णुपरायणम् ॥
1.34.m: He whose devotion to the God of gods, Janārdana, is firm / has blessings come to fruition; those endowed with devotion are superior to others.

1.34.s:
bhaktardṛḍhā bhavedyasya devadeve janārdane /
śreyāṃsi tasya sidhyanti bhaktimanto 'dhikāstataḥ //
1.34.d:
भक्तर्दृढा भवेद्यस्य देवदेवे जनार्दने ।
श्रेयांसि तस्य सिध्यन्ति भक्तिमन्तो ऽधिकास्ततः ॥
1.34.m: Those feet of men are fruitful which walk to the house of Viṣṇu; / those hands should be known as fruitful which are devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu.

1.34.s:
pādau tau saphalau puṃsāṃ yau viṣṇugṛhagāminau /
tau karau laphalau jñeyau viṣṇupūjāparau tu yau //
1.34.d:
पादौ तौ सफलौ पुंसां यौ विष्णुगृहगामिनौ ।
तौ करौ लफलौ ज्ञेयौ विष्णुपूजापरौ तु यौ ॥
1.34.m: Those eyes of men are very fruitful which behold Janārdana; / that tongue is praised by the virtuous which is dedicated to the name of Hari.

1.34.s:
te netre suphale puṃsāṃ paśyato ye danārdanam /
sā jihvā procyate sadbhirharināmaparā tu yā //
1.34.d:
ते नेत्रे सुफले पुंसां पश्यतो ये दनार्दनम् ।
सा जिह्वा प्रोच्यते सद्भिर्हरिनामपरा तु या ॥
1.34.m: Truth, truth, again truth, raising my arm it is proclaimed: / there is no truth equal to the guru, and there is no deity higher than Keśava.

1.34.s:
satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyamuddhṛtya bhujamutyate /
tattvaṃ gurusamaṃ nārita nata devaḥ keśavātparaḥ //
1.34.d:
सत्यं सत्यं पुनः सत्यमुद्धृत्य भुजमुत्यते ।
तत्त्वं गुरुसमं नारित नत देवः केशवात्परः ॥
1.34.m: I speak the truth, I speak what is beneficial, I speak the essence again and again: / in this worthless worldly existence, worship of Hari is the truth.

1.34.s:
satyaṃ vacmihitaṃ vācmi sāraṃ vacmi punaḥ punaḥ /
asāre 'smiṃsta saṃsāre satyaṃ harisamarcanam //
1.34.d:
सत्यं वच्मिहितं वाच्मि सारं वच्मि पुनः पुनः ।
असारे ऽस्मिंस्त संसारे सत्यं हरिसमर्चनम् ॥
1.34.m: Having severed the exceedingly firm snare of worldly existence, which produces great delusion, / with the axe of devotion to Hari, become exceedingly happy.

1.34.s:
saṃsārapāśaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ mahāmohapradāyakam /
haribhaktikuṭāreṇa cchittvātyantasukhī bhava //
1.34.d:
संसारपाशं सुदृढं महामोहप्रदायकम् ।
हरिभक्तिकुटारेण च्छित्त्वात्यन्तसुखी भव ॥
1.34.m: That mind is [truly a mind] which is joined to Viṣṇu; that speech which is devoted to him; / those ears, praised by the world, which are filled with the essence of stories about him.

1.34.s:
tanmanaḥ saṃyutaṃ viṣṇau sā vāṇī yatparāyaṇā /
te śrotre tatkathāsārapūrite lokavandite //
1.34.d:
तन्मनः संयुतं विष्णौ सा वाणी यत्परायणा ।
ते श्रोत्रे तत्कथासारपूरिते लोकवन्दिते ॥
1.34.m: Bliss, imperishable, devoid of the three states as well, / constantly worship the God dwelling in the midst of ether, O Nārada.

1.34.s:
ānandamakṣaraṃ śūnyamavasthātritayairapi /
ākāśamadhyagaṃ devaṃ bhaja nārada saṃtatam //
1.34.d:
आनन्दमक्षरं शून्यमवस्थात्रितयैरपि ।
आकाशमध्यगं देवं भज नारद संततम् ॥
1.34.m: Whose place or essential nature can never / be indicated, O tiger among sages, or seen by those with unrefined minds.

1.34.s:
sthānaṃ na śakyate yasya svarupaṃ vā kadācana /
nirdeṣṭuṃ muniśārdūla draṣṭuṃ vāpyakṛtātmabhiḥ //
1.34.d:
स्थानं न शक्यते यस्य स्वरुपं वा कदाचन ।
निर्देष्टुं मुनिशार्दूल द्रष्टुं वाप्यकृतात्मभिः ॥
1.34.m: When it is endowed with all the sense-organs, / then that eternal inner ruler is called waking by the virtuous.

1.34.s:
samastaiḥ karaṇairyukto vartte 'sau yadā tadā /
jāgradityucyate sadbhirantaryāmī sanātanaḥ //
1.34.d:
समस्तैः करणैर्युक्तो वर्त्ते ऽसौ यदा तदा ।
जाग्रदित्युच्यते सद्भिरन्तर्यामी सनातनः ॥
1.34.m: When, joined with the inner organs, it roams at will, / that Self, when free from slumber, is called dreaming.

1.34.s:
yadāntaḥ karaṇairṃyuktaḥ svecchayā vicaratyasau /
svapannicyucyate hyātmā yadā svāpavivarjitaḥ //
1.34.d:
यदान्तः करणैर्ंयुक्तः स्वेच्छया विचरत्यसौ ।
स्वपन्निच्युच्यते ह्यात्मा यदा स्वापविवर्जितः ॥
1.34.m: When that Self is not endowed with external sense-organs, nor with inner organs, / formless, and free from merit and demerit,

1.34.s:
na bāhyakaraṇairyukto na cāntaḥ karaṇaistathā /
asvarupo yadātmāsau puṇyāpuṇyavivarjitaḥ //
1.34.d:
न बाह्यकरणैर्युक्तो न चान्तः करणैस्तथा ।
अस्वरुपो यदात्मासौ पुण्यापुण्यविवर्जितः ॥
1.34.m: released from all adjuncts, bliss, devoid of qualities, all-pervading, / the God consisting of supreme Brahman is sung of as asleep [in deep sleep].

1.34.s:
sarvopādhivinirmukto hyānando nirguṇo vibhuḥ /
parabrahmamayo devaḥ suṣutpa iti gīyate //
1.34.d:
सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्तो ह्यानन्दो निर्गुणो विभुः ।
परब्रह्ममयो देवः सुषुत्प इति गीयते ॥
1.34.m: This universe of the moving and unmoving consists of thought alone; / it is as fickle as lightning, O best of brāhmaṇas; therefore worship Janārdana.

1.34.s:
bhāvanāmayametadvai jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam /
vidyudvilolaṃ viprendra bhaghaja tasmājjanārdanam //
1.34.d:
भावनामयमेतद्वै जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
विद्युद्विलोलं विप्रेन्द्र भघज तस्माज्जनार्दनम् ॥
1.34.m: Non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, and non-possession— / he in whom these abide, with him alone the Lord of the worlds is pleased.

1.34.s:
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmacaryāparigrahau /
vartate yasya tasyaiva tuṣyate jagatāṃ patiḥ //
1.34.d:
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहौ ।
वर्तते यस्य तस्यैव तुष्यते जगतां पतिः ॥
1.34.m: With one who is endowed with compassion for all beings and devoted to honoring brāhmaṇas, / the Lord of the universe, the crusher of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, is pleased.

1.34.s:
sarvabhaghūtadayāyukto viprapūjāparāyaṇaḥ /
tasya tuṣṭo jagannātho madhukaiṭabhamarddanaḥ //
1.34.d:
सर्वभघूतदयायुक्तो विप्रपूजापरायणः ।
तस्य तुष्टो जगन्नाथो मधुकैटभमर्द्दनः ॥
1.34.m: Jagannātha, the slayer of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, is pleased with him / who is full of compassion for all beings and devoted to honouring brāhmaṇas.

1.34.s:
satkathāyāṃ ca ramate satkathāṃ ca karoti yaḥ /
satsaṅgo nirahaṃ kārastasya prīto ramāpatiḥ //
1.34.d:
सत्कथायां च रमते सत्कथां च करोति यः ।
सत्सङ्गो निरहं कारस्तस्य प्रीतो रमापतिः ॥
1.34.m: The husband of Ramā is delighted with him / who takes delight in noble tales and tells noble tales, who keeps good company, and is free from egoism.

1.34.s:
nāmasaṃkīrttanaṃ viṣṇo kṣuttṛṭpraskhalitādiṣu /
karoti satataṃ yastu tasya prīto hyadhokṣajaḥ //
1.34.d:
नामसंकीर्त्तनं विष्णो क्षुत्तृट्प्रस्खलितादिषु ।
करोति सततं यस्तु तस्य प्रीतो ह्यधोक्षजः ॥
1.34.m: Adhokṣaja is pleased indeed with him / who constantly chants Viṣṇu's names when hungry, thirsty, slipping, and the like.

1.34.s:
yātu nārīpatiprāṇā patipūjāparāyaṇā /
tasyāstuṣṭo jagannātho dadāti svapadaṃ mune //
1.34.d:
यातु नारीपतिप्राणा पतिपूजापरायणा ।
तस्यास्तुष्टो जगन्नाथो ददाति स्वपदं मुने ॥
1.34.m: With the woman whose husband is her life and who is devoted to serving her husband, / Jagannātha is pleased, O sage, and gives his own abode.

1.34.s:
asūyārahitā ye tu hyahaṅkāravivarjitāḥ /
devapūjāparāścaiva teṣāṃ tuṣyati keśavaḥ //
1.34.d:
असूयारहिता ये तु ह्यहङ्कारविवर्जिताः ।
देवपूजापराश्चैव तेषां तुष्यति केशवः ॥
1.34.m: Keśava is pleased with those / who are free from malice, rid of egoism, and devoted to worshipping the gods.

1.34.s:
tasmācchṛṇuṣva devarśe bhajasvaṃ satataṃ harim /
mā kuruṣva hyahaṅkāraṃ vidyullolaśriyā vṛthā //
1.34.d:
तस्माच्छृणुष्व देवर्शे भजस्वं सततं हरिम् ।
मा कुरुष्व ह्यहङ्कारं विद्युल्लोलश्रिया वृथा ॥
1.34.m: Therefore listen, O divine sage! Constantly worship Hari; / do not become arrogant in vain over fortune as unsteady as lightning.

1.34.s:
śarīraṃ mṛtyusaṃyuktaṃ jīvitaṃ cāti cañcalam /
rājādibhirdhanaṃ bādhyaṃ sampadaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgurāḥ //
1.34.d:
शरीरं मृत्युसंयुक्तं जीवितं चाति चञ्चलम् ।
राजादिभिर्धनं बाध्यं सम्पदः क्षणभङ्गुराः ॥
1.34.m: The body is bound to death, and life is exceedingly fickle; / wealth can be seized by kings and others, and fortunes crumble in a moment.

1.34.s:
kiṃ na paśyasi devarṣe hyāyuṣārddhaṃ tu nidrayā /
hataṃ ca bhojanādyaiśca kiyadāyuḥ samāhṛtam //
1.34.d:
किं न पश्यसि देवर्षे ह्यायुषार्द्धं तु निद्रया ।
हतं च भोजनाद्यैश्च कियदायुः समाहृतम् ॥
1.34.m: Do you not see, O divine sage, that half of one's life is destroyed by sleep, / and how much of life is consumed by eating and the like?

1.34.s:
kiyadāyurbālabhāvātkiyadvṛthā /
kiyadviṣayabhogaiśca kadā dharmānkariṣyati //
1.34.d:
कियदायुर्बालभावात्कियद्वृथा ।
कियद्विषयभोगैश्च कदा धर्मान्करिष्यति ॥
1.34.m: How much of life is spent in childhood, how much in vain, / and how much in the enjoyment of sense objects! When will one practice righteousness?

1.34.s:
bālabhāve ca vārddhakyena ghaṭetācyutārcanam /
vayasyeva tato dharmānkuru tvamanahaṅkṛtaḥ //
1.34.d:
बालभावे च वार्द्धक्येन घटेताच्युतार्चनम् ।
वयस्येव ततो धर्मान्कुरु त्वमनहङ्कृतः ॥
1.34.m: Worship of Acyuta cannot be accomplished in childhood or in old age; / therefore, while still in your youth, practice righteousness, free from egoism.

1.34.s:
mā vināśaṃ vraja mune magnaḥ saṃsāragahvare /
varurvināśanilayamāpadāṃ paramaṃ padam //
1.34.d:
मा विनाशं व्रज मुने मग्नः संसारगह्वरे ।
वरुर्विनाशनिलयमापदां परमं पदम् ॥
1.34.m: Do not perish, O sage, sinking into the pit of worldly existence; / the body is an abode of ruin, the supreme seat of misfortunes.

1.34.s:
śarīraṃ bhoganilayaṃ malādyaiḥ paridūṣitam /
kimarthaṃ śāśvatadhiyā kuryātpāpaṃ naro vṛthā //
1.34.d:
शरीरं भोगनिलयं मलाद्यैः परिदूषितम् ।
किमर्थं शाश्वतधिया कुर्यात्पापं नरो वृथा ॥
1.34.m: The body is an abode of pleasures, tainted by impurities and the like; / why should a person commit sin in vain thinking it to be eternal?

1.34.s:
āsārabhūte saṃsāre nānāduḥ khasamanvite /
viśvāso nātra karttavyo niścitaṃ mṛtyusaṃkule //
1.34.d:
आसारभूते संसारे नानादुः खसमन्विते ।
विश्वासो नात्र कर्त्तव्यो निश्चितं मृत्युसंकुले ॥
1.34.m: In this worthless worldly existence, filled with manifold sufferings / and crowded with death, no trust should be placed at all.

1.34.s:
tasmācchṛṇuṣva viprendra satyametadvravīmyaham /
dehayoganivṛttyarthaṃ sadya eva janārdanam //
1.34.d:
तस्माच्छृणुष्व विप्रेन्द्र सत्यमेतद्व्रवीम्यहम् ।
देहयोगनिवृत्त्यर्थं सद्य एव जनार्दनम् ॥
1.34.m: Therefore listen, O best of brāhmaṇas, I speak this truth to you: / for the cessation of union with the body, [worship] Janārdana at once.

1.34.s:
mānaṃ tyaktvā tathā lobhaṃ kāmakrodhavivarjitaḥ /
bhajasva satataṃ viṣṇuṃ mānuṣyamatidurlabham //
1.34.d:
मानं त्यक्त्वा तथा लोभं कामक्रोधविवर्जितः ।
भजस्व सततं विष्णुं मानुष्यमतिदुर्लभम् ॥
1.34.m: Casting aside pride and greed, rid of lust and anger, / constantly worship Viṣṇu; human birth is exceedingly difficult to attain.

1.34.s:
koṭijanmasahasreṣu sthāvarādiṣu sattama /
saṃbhrāntasya tu mānuṣyaṃ kathañcitparilabhyate //
1.34.d:
कोटिजन्मसहस्रेषु स्थावरादिषु सत्तम ।
संभ्रान्तस्य तु मानुष्यं कथञ्चित्परिलभ्यते ॥
1.34.m: O best of men, wandering through tens of millions of births among stationary beings and the rest, / a human birth is somehow attained.

1.34.s:
tatrāpi devatābuddhirdānabuddhiśca sattama /
bhogabuddhistathā nṝṇāṃ janmāntaratapaḥ phalam //
1.34.d:
तत्रापि देवताबुद्धिर्दानबुद्धिश्च सत्तम ।
भोगबुद्धिस्तथा नॄणां जन्मान्तरतपः फलम् ॥
1.34.m: Even there, a mind inclined to the divine, a mind inclined to charity, O best of men, / and an attitude towards enjoyments [free from attachment] is the fruit of austerities performed in previous lives.

1.34.s:
mānuṣyaṃ durlabhaṃ prāpya yo hariṃ nārcayetsakṛt /
mūrkhaḥ ko 'sti parastasmājjaḍabuddhiracetanaḥ //
1.34.d:
मानुष्यं दुर्लभं प्राप्य यो हरिं नार्चयेत्सकृत् ।
मूर्खः को ऽस्ति परस्तस्माज्जडबुद्धिरचेतनः ॥
1.34.m: Having obtained a rare human birth, who does not worship Hari even once? / Who is a greater fool than he, dull-witted and devoid of consciousness?

1.34.s:
durlabhaṃ prāpya mānuṣyaṃ nārcayanti ca ye harim /
teṣāmatīva mūrkhāṇāṃ vivekaḥ kutra tiṣṭhati //
1.34.d:
दुर्लभं प्राप्य मानुष्यं नार्चयन्ति च ये हरिम् ।
तेषामतीव मूर्खाणां विवेकः कुत्र तिष्ठति ॥
1.34.m: Those who, having attained a rare human birth, do not worship Hari— / where does the discernment of those utter fools abide?

1.34.s:
ārādhito jagannātho dadātyabhimataṃ phalam /
kastaṃ na pūjayedviprasaṃsārāpripradīpitaḥ //
1.34.d:
आराधितो जगन्नाथो ददात्यभिमतं फलम् ।
कस्तं न पूजयेद्विप्रसंसाराप्रिप्रदीपितः ॥
1.34.m: Propitiated, Jagannātha grants one's desired reward; / who, scorched by the fire of worldly existence, would not worship him, O brāhmaṇa?

1.34.s:
caṇḍālo 'pi muniśreṣṭa viṣṇubhakto dvijādhikaḥ /
viṣṇubhaktivihīnaśca dvijo 'pi śvapacādhamaḥ //
1.34.d:
चण्डालो ऽपि मुनिश्रेष्ट विष्णुभक्तो द्विजाधिकः ।
विष्णुभक्तिविहीनश्च द्विजो ऽपि श्वपचाधमः ॥
1.34.m: Even an outcaste who is devoted to Viṣṇu is superior to a twice-born, O best of sages; / and even a twice-born lacking devotion to Viṣṇu is lower than a dog-cooker.

1.34.s:
tasmātkāmādikaṃ tyaktvā bhajeta harimavyayam /
yasmiṃstuṣṭe 'khilaṃ tuṣyedyataḥ sarvagato hariḥ //
1.34.d:
तस्मात्कामादिकं त्यक्त्वा भजेत हरिमव्ययम् ।
यस्मिंस्तुष्टे ऽखिलं तुष्येद्यतः सर्वगतो हरिः ॥
1.34.m: Therefore, casting aside lust and the like, one should worship imperishable Hari; / when he is pleased, all is pleased, because Hari is omnipresent.

1.34.s:
yathā hastipade sarvaṃ padamātraṃ pralīyate /
tathaḥā carācaraṃ viśvaṃ viṣṇāviva pralīyate //
1.34.d:
यथा हस्तिपदे सर्वं पदमात्रं प्रलीयते ।
तथःआ चराचरं विश्वं विष्णाविव प्रलीयते ॥
1.34.m: Just as every footprint dissolves into an elephant's footprint, / so the entire universe, moving and stationary, dissolves into Viṣṇu.

1.34.s:
ākāśena yathā vyātpaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam /
tathaiva hariṇā vyātpaṃ viśvametaccarācaram //
1.34.d:
आकाशेन यथा व्यात्पं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
तथैव हरिणा व्यात्पं विश्वमेतच्चराचरम् ॥
1.34.m: Just as the universe of the moving and unmoving is pervaded by space, / so this entire universe, moving and stationary, is pervaded by Hari.

1.34.s:
janmano maraṇaṃ nṝṇāṃ janma vai mṛtyusādhanam /
ubhe te nikaṭe viddhi tannāśo harisevayā //
1.34.d:
जन्मनो मरणं नॄणां जन्म वै मृत्युसाधनम् ।
उभे ते निकटे विद्धि तन्नाशो हरिसेवया ॥
1.34.m: Death comes from birth for men; birth indeed is the means to death; / know that both are near; their destruction comes through the service of Hari.

1.34.s:
dhyātaḥ smṛtaḥ pūjito vā praṇato vā janārdanaḥ /
saṃsārapāśavicchedīkastaṃ na pratipūjayet //
1.34.d:
ध्यातः स्मृतः पूजितो वा प्रणतो वा जनार्दनः ।
संसारपाशविच्छेदीकस्तं न प्रतिपूजयेत् ॥
1.34.m: Whether meditated upon, remembered, worshipped, or bowed to, Janārdana / cuts the bonds of worldly existence; who would not revere him?

1.34.s:
yannāmoccāṃraṇādeva mahāpātakanāśanam /
yaṃ samabhyarcya viprarṣe mokṣabhāgī bhavennaraḥ //
1.34.d:
यन्नामोच्चांरणादेव महापातकनाशनम् ।
यं समभ्यर्च्य विप्रर्षे मोक्षभागी भवेन्नरः ॥
1.34.m: Just by uttering his name, great sins are destroyed; / by thoroughly worshipping him, O brāhmaṇa sage, a man becomes an heir to liberation.

1.34.s:
aho citramaho citramaho citramidaṃ dvija /
harināmni sthite lokaḥ saṃsāre parivarttate //
1.34.d:
अहो चित्रमहो चित्रमहो चित्रमिदं द्विज ।
हरिनाम्नि स्थिते लोकः संसारे परिवर्त्तते ॥
1.34.m: Ah, what a wonder! Ah, what a wonder! Ah, what a wonder this is, O twice-born! / Though the name of Hari exists, the world still wanders in worldly existence!

1.34.s:
bhūyobhūyo 'pi vakṣyāmi satyametattapodhana /
nīyamāno yamabhaṭairaśakto dharmasādhanaiḥ //
1.34.d:
भूयोभूयो ऽपि वक्ष्यामि सत्यमेतत्तपोधन ।
नीयमानो यमभटैरशक्तो धर्मसाधनैः ॥
1.34.m: Again and again I tell you this truth, O rich in austerity: / when being dragged away by the soldiers of Yama, one is unable [to practice] the means of righteousness.

1.34.s:
yāvannendriyavaikalyaṃ yāvadvyādhirna bādhate /
tāvadevārcayedviṣṇuṃ yadi muktimabhīpsati //
māturgarbhādviniḥ
1.34.d:
यावन्नेन्द्रियवैकल्यं यावद्व्याधिर्न बाधते ।
तावदेवार्चयेद्विष्णुं यदि मुक्तिमभीप्सति ॥
मातुर्गर्भाद्विनिः
1.34.m:
As long as the senses are not impaired, as long as disease does not afflict one, / so long should one worship Viṣṇu, if one desires liberation.

The very moment a living being has emerged from the mother's womb, / death draws near; therefore, one should be devoted to righteousness.

1.34.s:
māturgarbhādviniṣkrānto yadā jantustadaiva hi /
mṛtyuḥ saṃnihito bhūyāttasmāddharmaparo bhavet //
1.34.d:
मातुर्गर्भाद्विनिष्क्रान्तो यदा जन्तुस्तदैव हि ।
मृत्युः संनिहितो भूयात्तस्माद्धर्मपरो भवेत् ॥

1.34.s:
aho kaṣṭamaho kaṣṭamahokaṣṭamidaṃ vapuḥ /
vinaśvaraṃ samājñāya dharmaṃ naivācaratyayam //
1.34.d:
अहो कष्टमहो कष्टमहोकष्टमिदं वपुः ।
विनश्वरं समाज्ञाय धर्मं नैवाचरत्ययम् ॥
1.34.m: Ah, what misery! Ah, what misery! Ah, what misery! Though knowing this body / to be perishable, a person does not practice righteousness at all!

1.34.s:
satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyamuddhṛtya bhujamucyate /
dambhācāraṃ parityajyaṃ vāsudevaṃ samarcayet //
1.34.d:
सत्यं सत्यं पुनः सत्यमुद्धृत्य भुजमुच्यते ।
दम्भाचारं परित्यज्यं वासुदेवं समर्चयेत् ॥
1.34.m: It is true, true, and true again, proclaimed with arm raised high: / abandoning hypocritical conduct, one should worship Vāsudeva.

1.34.s:
bhūyo bhūyo hitaṃ vacmi bhujamuddhṛtya nārada /
viṣṇuḥ sarvātmanā pūjyastyājyāsūyā tathānṛtam //
1.34.d:
भूयो भूयो हितं वच्मि भुजमुद्धृत्य नारद ।
विष्णुः सर्वात्मना पूज्यस्त्याज्यासूया तथानृतम् ॥
1.34.m: Again and again I declare what is beneficial, raising my arm, O Nārada: / Viṣṇu is to be worshipped with all one's being; malice and falsehood must be abandoned.

1.34.s:
krodhamūlo manastāpaḥ krodhaḥ saṃsārabandhanam /
dharmakṣayakaraḥ krodhastasmāttaṃ parivarjayet //
1.34.d:
क्रोधमूलो मनस्तापः क्रोधः संसारबन्धनम् ।
धर्मक्षयकरः क्रोधस्तस्मात्तं परिवर्जयेत् ॥
1.34.m: Anger is the root of mental distress; anger is the bond of worldly existence; / anger causes the destruction of righteousness; therefore, one should avoid it.

1.34.s:
kāmamūlamidaṃ janma kāmaḥ pāpasya kāraṇam /
yaśaḥ kṣayakaraḥ kāmastasmāttaṃ parivarjayet //
1.34.d:
काममूलमिदं जन्म कामः पापस्य कारणम् ।
यशः क्षयकरः कामस्तस्मात्तं परिवर्जयेत् ॥
1.34.m: This birth has desire as its root; desire is the cause of sin; / desire causes the destruction of renown; therefore, one should avoid it.

1.34.s:
samastaduḥkhajālānāṃ mātsaryaṃ kāraṇaṃ smṛtam /
narakāṇāṃ sādhanaṃ ca tasmāttadapi saṃtyajet //
1.34.d:
समस्तदुःखजालानां मात्सर्यं कारणं स्मृतम् ।
नरकाणां साधनं च तस्मात्तदपि संत्यजेत् ॥
1.34.m: Envy is known to be the cause of all networks of suffering / and the means to hells; therefore, one should abandon that as well.

1.34.s:
mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandhamokṣayoḥ /
tasmāttadabhisaṃyojya parātmani sukhī bhavet //
1.34.d:
मन एव मनुष्याणां कारणं बन्धमोक्षयोः ।
तस्मात्तदभिसंयोज्य परात्मनि सुखी भवेत् ॥
1.34.m: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings; / therefore, having joined it to the supreme Self, one may become happy.

1.34.s:
aho dhairyamaho dhairyamaho dhairyamaho nṛṇām /
viṣṇau sthite jagannāthe na bhajanti madoddhatāḥ //
1.34.d:
अहो धैर्यमहो धैर्यमहो धैर्यमहो नृणाम् ।
विष्णौ स्थिते जगन्नाथे न भजन्ति मदोद्धताः ॥
1.34.m: Ah, what persistence! Ah, what persistence! Ah, what persistence of men, / that while Viṣṇu, the Lord of the world, exists, haughty with pride they do not worship him!

1.34.s:
anārādhya jagannāthaṃ sarvadhātāramacyutam /
saṃsārasāgare magnāḥ kathaṃ pāraṃ prayānti hi //
1.34.d:
अनाराध्य जगन्नाथं सर्वधातारमच्युतम् ।
संसारसागरे मग्नाः कथं पारं प्रयान्ति हि ॥
1.34.m: Without propitiating Jagannātha, the supporter of all, Acyuta, / how can those sunk in the ocean of worldly existence reach the further shore?

1.34.s:
acyutānantagovindanāmoccāraṇabheṣajāt /
naśyanti sakalā rogāḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham //
1.34.d:
अच्युतानन्तगोविन्दनामोच्चारणभेषजात् ।
नश्यन्ति सकला रोगाः सत्यं सत्यं वदाम्यहम् ॥
1.34.m: By the medicine of uttering the names 'Acyuta, Ananta, Govinda,' / all diseases are destroyed; I speak the truth, the truth!

1.34.s:
nārāyaṇa jagannātha vāsudeva janārddana /
itīrayanti ye nityaṃ te vai sarvatra vanditāḥ //
1.34.d:
नारायण जगन्नाथ वासुदेव जनार्द्दन ।
इतीरयन्ति ये नित्यं ते वै सर्वत्र वन्दिताः ॥
1.34.m: Those who constantly utter: 'Nārāyaṇa, Jagannātha, Vāsudeva, Janārdana,' / are indeed revered everywhere.

1.34.s:
adyāpi ca muniśreṣṭa brahmādyā api devatāḥ /
yatprābhāvaṃ na jānanti taṃ yāhi śaraṇaṃ mune //
1.34.d:
अद्यापि च मुनिश्रेष्ट ब्रह्माद्या अपि देवताः ।
यत्प्राभावं न जानन्ति तं याहि शरणं मुने ॥
1.34.m: Even today, O best of sages, the deities headed by Brahmā / do not know his majesty; take refuge in him, O sage!

1.34.s:
aho maurkhyamaho maurkhyamaho maurkhyaṃ durātmanām /
hṛtpadmasaṃsthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ na vijānanti nārada //
1.34.d:
अहो मौर्ख्यमहो मौर्ख्यमहो मौर्ख्यं दुरात्मनाम् ।
हृत्पद्मसंस्थितं विष्णुं न विजानन्ति नारद ॥
1.34.m: Ah, the foolishness, ah, the foolishness, ah, the foolishness of the wicked, / who do not recognize Viṣṇu seated in the lotus of the heart, O Nārada!

1.34.s:
śṛṇuṣva muniśārdūla bhūyobhūyo vadāmyaham /
hariḥ śraddhāvatāṃ tuṣyenna dhanairna ca bāndhavaiḥ //
1.34.d:
शृणुष्व मुनिशार्दूल भूयोभूयो वदाम्यहम् ।
हरिः श्रद्धावतां तुष्येन्न धनैर्न च बान्धवैः ॥
1.34.m: Listen, O tiger among sages, I say again and again: / Hari is pleased with those who have faith, not by wealth nor by kin.

1.34.s:
bandhumattvaṃ dhanāḍhyatvaṃ putravattvaṃ ca sattama /
viṣṇubhaghaktimatāṃ nṝṇāṃ bhavejjanmani janmani //
1.34.d:
बन्धुमत्त्वं धनाढ्यत्वं पुत्रवत्त्वं च सत्तम ।
विष्णुभघक्तिमतां नॄणां भवेज्जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥
1.34.m: Possession of kin, richness in wealth, and possession of sons, O best of beings, / shall belong in birth after birth to people endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu.

1.34.s:
pāpamūlamayaṃ dehaḥ pāpakarmaratastathā /
etadviditvā satataṃ pūjanīyo janārddanaḥ //
1.34.d:
पापमूलमयं देहः पापकर्मरतस्तथा ।
एतद्विदित्वा सततं पूजनीयो जनार्द्दनः ॥
1.34.m: This body is rooted in sin, and likewise intent on sinful deeds; / knowing this, Janārdana must be worshipped constantly.

1.34.s:
putramitrakalatrādyā bahavaḥ syuśca saṃpadaḥ /
haripūjāratānāṃ tu bhavatyena na saṃśayaḥ //
1.34.d:
पुत्रमित्रकलत्राद्या बहवः स्युश्च संपदः ।
हरिपूजारतानां तु भवत्येन न संशयः ॥
1.34.m: Sons, friends, wives, and so forth, and many riches / come indeed to those devoted to the worship of Hari; of this there is no doubt.

1.34.s:
ihāmutra sukhaprepsuḥ pūjayetsatataṃ harim /
ihāmutrāsukhaprepsuḥ paranindāparo bhavet //
1.34.d:
इहामुत्र सुखप्रेप्सुः पूजयेत्सततं हरिम् ।
इहामुत्रासुखप्रेप्सुः परनिन्दापरो भवेत् ॥
1.34.m: Desiring happiness here and in the hereafter, one should constantly worship Hari; / desiring unhappiness here and in the hereafter, one would be intent on censuring others.

1.34.s:
dhigjanma bhaktihīnānāṃ devadeve janārddane /
satpātradānaśūnyaṃ yattaddhanaṃ dhikpunaḥ punaḥ //
1.34.d:
धिग्जन्म भक्तिहीनानां देवदेवे जनार्द्दने ।
सत्पात्रदानशून्यं यत्तद्धनं धिक्पुनः पुनः ॥
1.34.m: Fie on the birth of those devoid of devotion to the god of gods, Janārdana! / Fie, fie again on that wealth which is destitute of gift to a worthy recipient!

1.34.s:
na namedviṣṇave yasya śarīraṃ karmabhedine /
pāpānāmākaraṃ tadvai vijñeyaṃ munisattama //
1.34.d:
न नमेद्विष्णवे यस्य शरीरं कर्मभेदिने ।
पापानामाकरं तद्वै विज्ञेयं मुनिसत्तम ॥
1.34.m: The body of one that does not bow to Viṣṇu, who destroys karma, / is surely to be known, O best of sages, as a mine of sins.

1.34.s:
satpātradānarahitaṃ yaddravyaṃ yena rakṣitam /
cauryeṇa rakṣitamiva viddhi lokeṣu niścitam //
1.34.d:
सत्पात्रदानरहितं यद्द्रव्यं येन रक्षितम् ।
चौर्येण रक्षितमिव विद्धि लोकेषु निश्चितम् ॥
1.34.m: Whatever wealth is guarded without giving to a worthy recipient, / know that in the worlds it is certainly as if guarded by theft.

1.34.s:
taḍillolaśriyā mattāḥ kṣaṇaṃbhayuraśālinaḥ /
nārādhayanti viśveśaṃ paśupāśavimocakam //
1.34.d:
तडिल्लोलश्रिया मत्ताः क्षणंभयुरशालिनः ।
नाराधयन्ति विश्वेशं पशुपाशविमोचकम् ॥
1.34.m: Intoxicated by fortune flickering as lightning, possessing only momentary radiance, / they do not worship the Lord of the Universe, who liberates beasts from their bonds.

1.34.s:
sṛṣṭistu dvividhā proktā daivāsuravibhedataḥ /
hari bhakti yutā daivī taddhīnā hyāsurī mahā //
1.34.d:
सृष्टिस्तु द्विविधा प्रोक्ता दैवासुरविभेदतः ।
हरि भक्ति युता दैवी तद्धीना ह्यासुरी महा ॥
1.34.m: Creation is declared to be twofold, distinguished as divine and demonic: / the divine is endowed with devotion to Hari; that devoid of it is indeed greatly demonic.

1.34.s:
tasmācchṛṇaṣva viprendra haribhaktiparāyaṇāḥ /
śreṣṭhāḥ sarvatra vikhyātā yato bhaktiḥ sudurlabhā //
1.34.d:
तस्माच्छृणष्व विप्रेन्द्र हरिभक्तिपरायणाः ।
श्रेष्ठाः सर्वत्र विख्याता यतो भक्तिः सुदुर्लभा ॥
1.34.m: Therefore listen, O leader of brahmins: those devoted to devotion to Hari / are celebrated everywhere as the best, because devotion is exceedingly difficult to attain.

1.34.s:
asūyārahitā ye ca vipratrāṇaparāyaṇāḥ /
kāmādirahitā ye ca teṣāṃ tuṣyati keśavaḥ //
1.34.d:
असूयारहिता ये च विप्रत्राणपरायणाः ।
कामादिरहिता ये च तेषां तुष्यति केशवः ॥
1.34.m: Those who are free from malice, intent on protecting brahmins, / and devoid of desire and the like—with them Keśava is pleased.

1.34.s:
saṃmārjanādinā ye tu viṣṇuśuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ /
satpātradānaniratāḥ prayānti paramaṃ padam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde haribhaktilakṣaṇaṃ nāma catustriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.34.d:
संमार्जनादिना ये तु विष्णुशुश्रूषणे रताः ।
सत्पात्रदाननिरताः प्रयान्ति परमं पदम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे हरिभक्तिलक्षणं नाम चतुस्त्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.34.m:
Those, however, who are intent on serving Viṣṇu by sweeping and the like, / and devoted to giving to worthy recipients, go to the supreme abode.

Thus ends the thirty-fourth chapter, named 'The Characteristics of Devotion to Hari', in the first quarter of the Pūrvabhāga of the glorious Bṛhannāradīyapurāṇa.

1.35.s:
sanaka uvāca
punarvakṣyāmi māhātmyaṃ devadevasya cakriṇaḥ /
paṭhatāṃ śuṇvatāṃ sadyaḥ pāparāśiḥ praṇaśyati //
1.35.d:
सनक उवाच
पुनर्वक्ष्यामि माहात्म्यं देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ।
पठतां शुण्वतां सद्यः पापराशिः प्रणश्यति ॥
1.35.m: Sanaka said: / I shall again speak of the eulogy of greatness of the god of gods, the Wielder of the Discus, / by reciting and hearing which the mass of sins is instantly destroyed.

1.35.s:
śāntā jitāriṣaḍvargā yogenāpyanahṝṅkṛtāḥ /
yajanti jñānayogena jñānarūpiṇamavyayam //
1.35.d:
शान्ता जितारिषड्वर्गा योगेनाप्यनहॄङ्कृताः ।
यजन्ति ज्ञानयोगेन ज्ञानरूपिणमव्ययम् ॥
1.35.m: The peaceful, who have conquered the six enemies and become free of egoism through yoga, / worship through the yoga of knowledge the imperishable One whose nature is knowledge.

1.35.s:
tīrthasnānairviśuddhā ye vratadānatapomakhaiḥ /
yajanti karmayogena sarvadhātāramacyutam //
1.35.d:
तीर्थस्नानैर्विशुद्धा ये व्रतदानतपोमखैः ।
यजन्ति कर्मयोगेन सर्वधातारमच्युतम् ॥
1.35.m: Those purified by bathing at sacred fords, by vows, gifts, austerities, and sacrifices, / worship through the yoga of action the supporter of all, Acyuta.

1.35.s:
lubdhā vyasanito 'jñāśca na yajanti jagatpatim /
ajarāmaravanmūḍhāstiṣṭanti narakīṭakāḥ //
1.35.d:
लुब्धा व्यसनितो ऽज्ञाश्च न यजन्ति जगत्पतिम् ।
अजरामरवन्मूढास्तिष्टन्ति नरकीटकाः ॥
1.35.m: The greedy, the addicted, and the ignorant do not worship the Lord of the World; / foolish, like worms of hell, they behave as though unaging and immortal.

1.35.s:
taḍillekhāśriyā mattā vṛthāhṝṅkāradviṣitāḥ /
na yajanti jagannāthaṃ sarvaśraiyovidhāyakam //
1.35.d:
तडिल्लेखाश्रिया मत्ता वृथाहॄङ्कारद्विषिताः ।
न यजन्ति जगन्नाथं सर्वश्रैयोविधायकम् ॥
1.35.m: Intoxicated by fortune like a flash of lightning, hateful with vain egoism, / they do not worship Jagannātha, the bestower of all welfare.

1.35.s:
haridharmaratāḥ śāntā haripādābjasevakāḥ /
daivātke 'pīha jāyante lokānugrahatatparāḥ //
1.35.d:
हरिधर्मरताः शान्ता हरिपादाब्जसेवकाः ।
दैवात्के ऽपीह जायन्ते लोकानुग्रहतत्पराः ॥
1.35.m: Devoted to the dharma of Hari, peaceful, servants of Hari's lotus feet, / by fate some are born here intent on showing favor to the worlds.

1.35.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā yo yajedbhaktito harim /
sa yāti paramaṃ sthānaṃ sarvalokottamottamam //
1.35.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यो यजेद्भक्तितो हरिम् ।
स याति परमं स्थानं सर्वलोकोत्तमोत्तमम् ॥
1.35.m: Whoever worships Hari with devotion through action, mind, and speech, / he goes to the supreme station, the highest among all the worlds.

1.35.s:
atraivodāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam /
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
1.35.d:
अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
पठतां शृण्वतां चैव सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
1.35.m: Right here they cite this ancient account, / which destroys all sins for those who recite and hear it.

1.35.s:
tatpravakṣyāmi caritaṃ yajñamālisumālinoḥ /
yasya śravaṇamātreṇa vācimedha phalaṃ labhet //
1.35.d:
तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि चरितं यज्ञमालिसुमालिनोः ।
यस्य श्रवणमात्रेण वाचिमेध फलं लभेत् ॥
1.35.m: I shall relate that story of Yajñamālin and Sumālin, / by merely hearing which one obtains the fruit of an aśvamedha.

1.35.s:
kaścidāsītpurā vipra brahmaṇo raivateṃ'tare /
vedamāliriti khyāto vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ //
1.35.d:
कश्चिदासीत्पुरा विप्र ब्रह्मणो रैवतेंऽतरे ।
वेदमालिरिति ख्यातो वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ॥
1.35.m: Long ago, O brahmin, during the Raivata Manvantara, there was a certain brahmin / known as Vedamālin, who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

1.35.s:
sarvabhūtadayāyukto haripūjāparāyaṇaḥ /
putramitrakalatrārthaṃ dhanārjanaparo 'bhavat //
1.35.d:
सर्वभूतदयायुक्तो हरिपूजापरायणः ।
पुत्रमित्रकलत्रार्थं धनार्जनपरो ऽभवत् ॥
1.35.m: Endowed with compassion for all beings, intent on the worship of Hari, / he became bent on acquiring wealth for the sake of his sons, friends, and wife.

1.35.s:
apaṇyaṃvikrayaṃ cakre tathā ca rasivikrayam /
caṇḍālādyairapi tathā saṃbhaṣī tatpratigrahī //
1.35.d:
अपण्यंविक्रयं चक्रे तथा च रसिविक्रयम् ।
चण्डालाद्यैरपि तथा संभषी तत्प्रतिग्रही ॥
1.35.m: He engaged in the sale of illicit goods, and likewise in the sale of fluids; / he also conversed with outcasts and others, and received gifts from them.

1.35.s:
tapasāṃ vikrayaṃ cakre vratānāṃ vikrayaṃ tathā /
parārthaṃ tīrthagamanaṃ kalatrārthamakārayat //
1.35.d:
तपसां विक्रयं चक्रे व्रतानां विक्रयं तथा ।
परार्थं तीर्थगमनं कलत्रार्थमकारयत् ॥
1.35.m: He sold austerities, and likewise he sold religious vows; / he undertook pilgrimages to sacred fords for others, for the sake of his wife.

1.35.s:
kālena gacchatā vipra jātau tasya sutāvubho /
yajñamālī sumālī ca yamalāvatiśobhanau //
1.35.d:
कालेन गच्छता विप्र जातौ तस्य सुतावुभो ।
यज्ञमाली सुमाली च यमलावतिशोभनौ ॥
1.35.m: As time passed, O brahmin, two sons were born to him, / Yajñamālin and Sumālin, exceedingly handsome twins.

1.35.s:
tataḥ pitā kumārau tāvatisnehasamanvitaḥ /
poṣayāmāsa vātsalyādbahubhiḥ sādhanaistadā //
1.35.d:
ततः पिता कुमारौ तावतिस्नेहसमन्वितः ।
पोषयामास वात्सल्याद्बहुभिः साधनैस्तदा ॥
1.35.m: Then the father, endowed with great affection, / nurtured the two boys out of fondness through many means at that time.

1.35.s:
vedamālirbahūpāyairdhanaṃ saṃpādya yatnataḥ /
svadhanaṃ gaṇayāmāsa kiyatsyāditi veditum //
1.35.d:
वेदमालिर्बहूपायैर्धनं संपाद्य यत्नतः ।
स्वधनं गणयामास कियत्स्यादिति वेदितुम् ॥
1.35.m: Vedamālin, having acquired wealth diligently by many expedients, / counted his wealth in order to know how much it might be.

1.35.s:
nidhikoṭisahasrāṇāṃ koṭikoṭiguṇānvitam /
vigaṇayya svayaṃ dṛṣṭo vismitaścārthacintayā //
1.35.d:
निधिकोटिसहस्राणां कोटिकोटिगुणान्वितम् ।
विगणय्य स्वयं दृष्टो विस्मितश्चार्थचिन्तया ॥
1.35.m: Having counted and seen for himself that it was multiplied by crores of crores of thousands of crores of treasures, / he was astonished, pondering over his riches:

1.35.s:
asatpratigrahaiścaiva apaṇyānāṃ ca vikrayaiḥ /
meyā tapo vikrayādyairetaddhanamupārjitam //
1.35.d:
असत्प्रतिग्रहैश्चैव अपण्यानां च विक्रयैः ।
मेया तपो विक्रयाद्यैरेतद्धनमुपार्जितम् ॥
1.35.m: "By accepting illicit gifts and by sales of illicit goods, / by the sale of austerities and such, this wealth has been amassed by me.

1.35.s:
nādyāpi śāntimāpannā mama tṛṣṇātiduḥsahā /
merutulyasuvarṇāni hyasaṃkhyātāni vāñchati //
1.35.d:
नाद्यापि शान्तिमापन्ना मम तृष्णातिदुःसहा ।
मेरुतुल्यसुवर्णानि ह्यसंख्यातानि वाञ्छति ॥
1.35.m: Even today my exceedingly unbearable craving has not attained peace; / it desires countless [masses of] gold equal to Meru.

1.35.s:
aho manye mahākaṣṭaṃ samastakleśasādhanam /
sarvānkāmānavāṃpnoti punaranyañca kāṅkṣati //
1.35.d:
अहो मन्ये महाकष्टं समस्तक्लेशसाधनम् ।
सर्वान्कामानवांप्नोति पुनरन्यञ्च काङ्क्षति ॥
1.35.m: Ah, I consider it a great distress, the instrument of all afflictions: / one attains all desires, and yet longs for another!

1.35.s:
jīryanti jīryataḥ keśāḥ dantā jīryanti jīryataḥ /
cakṣuḥśrotre ca jīryete tṛṣṇekā taruṇāyate //
1.35.d:
जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशाः दन्ता जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः ।
चक्षुःश्रोत्रे च जीर्येते तृष्णेका तरुणायते ॥
1.35.m: The hair decays as one ages, the teeth decay as one ages, / the eyes and ears decay; craving alone remains youthful.

1.35.s:
mamedriyāṇi sarvāṇi mandabhāvaṃ vrajanti ca /
balaṃ hataṃ ca jarasā tṛṣṇā taruṇatāṃ gatā //
1.35.d:
ममेद्रियाणि सर्वाणि मन्दभावं व्रजन्ति च ।
बलं हतं च जरसा तृष्णा तरुणतां गता ॥
1.35.m: All my senses are becoming dull, / my strength is destroyed by old age, [yet] craving has attained youthfulness.

1.35.s:
kaṣṭāśā varttate yasya sa vidrānatha paṇḍitaḥ /
suśānto 'pi pramanyuḥ syāddhīmānapyatimūḍhadhīḥ //
1.35.d:
कष्टाशा वर्त्तते यस्य स विद्रानथ पण्डितः ।
सुशान्तो ऽपि प्रमन्युः स्याद्धीमानप्यतिमूढधीः ॥
1.35.m: He in whom painful desire dwells, even if learned or a scholar, / even if very peaceful, becomes angry, and though wise, becomes extremely foolish-minded.

1.35.s:
āśā bhaṅgakarī puṃsāmajeyārātisannibhā /
tasmādāśāṃ tyajetprājño yadīcchecchāśvataṃ sukham //
1.35.d:
आशा भङ्गकरी पुंसामजेयारातिसन्निभा ।
तस्मादाशां त्यजेत्प्राज्ञो यदीच्छेच्छाश्वतं सुखम् ॥
1.35.m: Desire ruins men; it is like an unconquerable enemy; / therefore, a wise man should abandon desire if he wishes for eternal happiness.

1.35.s:
balaṃ tejoḥ yaśaśvaiva vidyāṃ mānaṃ ca vṛddhatām /
tathaiva satkule janma āśā hatyativegataḥ //
1.35.d:
बलं तेजोः यशश्वैव विद्यां मानं च वृद्धताम् ।
तथैव सत्कुले जन्म आशा हत्यतिवेगतः ॥
1.35.m: Strength, splendor, fame, learning, honor, senior status, / and likewise birth in a noble family—desire destroys them with great swiftness.

1.35.s:
nṛṇāmāśābhibhūtānāmāścaryamidasucyate /
kiñciddātāpi cāṇḍālastasmādadhikatāṃ gataḥ //
1.35.d:
नृणामाशाभिभूतानामाश्चर्यमिदसुच्यते ।
किञ्चिद्दातापि चाण्डालस्तस्मादधिकतां गतः ॥
1.35.m: This wonder is spoken of concerning men overcome by desire: / even an outcast who gives a little becomes superior to them.

1.35.s:
āśābhibhūtā ye martyā mahāmohā mahoddhatāḥ /
avamānādikaṃ duḥkhaṃ na jānanti kadāpyaho //
1.35.d:
आशाभिभूता ये मर्त्या महामोहा महोद्धताः ।
अवमानादिकं दुःखं न जानन्ति कदाप्यहो ॥
1.35.m: Mortals overcome by desire, deeply deluded and exceedingly arrogant, / ah, never recognize the suffering of dishonor and the like!

1.35.s:
mayāpyevaṃ bahukliśairetaddhanamupārjitam /
śarīramapi jīrṇaṃ ca jarasāpahataṃ balam //
1.35.d:
मयाप्येवं बहुक्लिशैरेतद्धनमुपार्जितम् ।
शरीरमपि जीर्णं च जरसापहतं बलम् ॥
1.35.m: Even so has this wealth been amassed by me through many hardships; / the body is worn out, and strength has been carried away by old age.

1.35.s:
itaḥ paraṃ yatiṣyāmi paralokārthamādarāt /
evaṃ niścitya viprendra dharmamārga rato 'bhavat //
1.35.d:
इतः परं यतिष्यामि परलोकार्थमादरात् ।
एवं निश्चित्य विप्रेन्द्र धर्ममार्ग रतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.35.m: Henceforth I shall strive with care for the sake of the next world." / Having thus resolved, O best of brahmins, he became intent upon the path of righteousness.

1.35.s:
tadaiva taddhanaṃ sarvaṃ caturddhā vyabhajattathā /
svayaṃ tu bhāga dvitaya svārjitārthādapāharat //
1.35.d:
तदैव तद्धनं सर्वं चतुर्द्धा व्यभजत्तथा ।
स्वयं तु भाग द्वितय स्वार्जितार्थादपाहरत् ॥
1.35.m: Right then he divided all that wealth into four parts; / and he took for himself two parts from the wealth he had amassed,

1.35.s:
śeṣaṃ ca bhāgadvitayaṃ putrayorubhayordadau /
svenārjitānāṃ pāpānāṃ nāśaṃ kartumanāstadā //
1.35.d:
शेषं च भागद्वितयं पुत्रयोरुभयोर्ददौ ।
स्वेनार्जितानां पापानां नाशं कर्तुमनास्तदा ॥
1.35.m: and gave the remaining two parts to his two sons. / Intending at that time to bring about the destruction of the sins he had amassed,

1.35.s:
prapātaḍāgārāmāṃśca tathā devagṛhānbahūn /
annādīnāṃ ca dānāni gaṅgātīre cakāra saḥ //
1.35.d:
प्रपातडागारामांश्च तथा देवगृहान्बहून् ।
अन्नादीनां च दानानि गङ्गातीरे चकार सः ॥
1.35.m: he constructed water-sheds, ponds, and groves, and likewise many temples of the gods, / and made gifts of food and the like on the bank of the Gaṅgā.

1.35.s:
evaṃ dhanamaśeṣaṃ ca viśrāṇya haribhaktimān /
nāranārāyaṇa sthānaṃ jagāma tapase vanam //
1.35.d:
एवं धनमशेषं च विश्राण्य हरिभक्तिमान् ।
नारनारायण स्थानं जगाम तपसे वनम् ॥
1.35.m: Having thus distributed all the wealth, full of devotion to Hari, / he went to the forest, the dwelling of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, for the purpose of austerity.

1.35.s:
tatrāpaśyanmahāramyamāśramaṃ munisevitam /
phalitaiḥ puṣaapitaiścaiva śobhitaṃ vṛkṣasaṃcayaiḥ //
1.35.d:
तत्रापश्यन्महारम्यमाश्रमं मुनिसेवितम् ।
फलितैः पुषअपितैश्चैव शोभितं वृक्षसंचयैः ॥
1.35.m: There he saw a very delightful hermitage frequented by sages, / adorned with masses of trees bearing fruit and flowers.

1.35.s:
gṛṇadbhiḥ paramaṃ brahma śāstracintāparaistathā /
paricaryāparairvṛddhairmunibhiḥ pariśobhitam //
1.35.d:
गृणद्भिः परमं ब्रह्म शास्त्रचिन्तापरैस्तथा ।
परिचर्यापरैर्वृद्धैर्मुनिभिः परिशोभितम् ॥
1.35.m: [An ashram] adorned by elderly sages who recited the supreme Brahman, / who were devoted to reflecting on the sacred scriptures, and intent on pious service;

1.35.s:
śiṣyaiḥ parivṛtaṃ tatra muniṃ jānanti saṃjñakam /
gṛṇantaṃ paramaṃ brahma tejorāśiṃ dadarśa ha //
1.35.d:
शिष्यैः परिवृतं तत्र मुनिं जानन्ति संज्ञकम् ।
गृणन्तं परमं ब्रह्म तेजोराशिं ददर्श ह ॥
1.35.m: There he beheld a sage named Jānanti, surrounded by disciples, / reciting the supreme Brahman—a mass of fiery splendour.

1.35.s:
śamādiguṇasaṃyuktaṃ rāgādirahitaṃ munim /
śīrṇaparṇāśanaṃ dṛṣṭvā vedamālirnanāma tam //
1.35.d:
शमादिगुणसंयुक्तं रागादिरहितं मुनिम् ।
शीर्णपर्णाशनं दृष्ट्वा वेदमालिर्ननाम तम् ॥
1.35.m: Seeing that sage endowed with tranquillity and other virtues, free from passion and [its companion vices], / who fed on fallen leaves, Vedamālin bowed down to him.

1.35.s:
tasya jānantirāgantoḥ kalpayāmāsa cārhaṇam /
kandamūlaphalādyaistu nārāyaṇadhiyā mune //
1.35.d:
तस्य जानन्तिरागन्तोः कल्पयामास चार्हणम् ।
कन्दमूलफलाद्यैस्तु नारायणधिया मुने ॥
1.35.m: Jānanti prepared hospitality for the guest / with roots, fruits, and the like, O sage, regarding him with the thought of Nārāyaṇa.

1.35.s:
kṛtātithyakriyastena vedamālī kṛtāñjaliḥ /
vinayāvanato bhūtvā provāca vadatāṃ varam //
1.35.d:
कृतातिथ्यक्रियस्तेन वेदमाली कृताञ्जलिः ।
विनयावनतो भूत्वा प्रोवाच वदतां वरम् ॥
1.35.m: Having received hospitable rites from him, Vedamālin, with joined palms / and bowed down in humility, spoke to that foremost of eloquent men:

1.35.s:
bhagavankṛtakṛtyo 'smi vigataṃ kalmaṣaṃ mama /
māmuddhara mahābhāga jñānadānena paṇḍita //
1.35.d:
भगवन्कृतकृत्यो ऽस्मि विगतं कल्मषं मम ।
मामुद्धर महाभाग ज्ञानदानेन पण्डित ॥
1.35.m: “O venerable one, I have accomplished my purpose! My stain is gone. / Deliver me, O highly fortunate one, wise one, by the bestowal of knowledge!”

1.35.s:
evamuktastatastena jānantirmunisattamaḥ /
provāca prahasanvāgmī vedamāliṃ guṇānvitam //
1.35.d:
एवमुक्तस्ततस्तेन जानन्तिर्मुनिसत्तमः ।
प्रोवाच प्रहसन्वाग्मी वेदमालिं गुणान्वितम् ॥
1.35.m: Thus addressed by him, Jānanti, the best of sages, / an eloquent speaker, smiled gently and said to the virtuous Vedamālin:

1.35.s:
jānantiruvāca
śṛṇaṣva vipraśārdūla saṃsāracchedakāraṇam /
pravakṣyāmi samāsena durlabhaṃ tvakṛtātmanām //
1.35.d:
जानन्तिरुवाच
शृणष्व विप्रशार्दूल संसारच्छेदकारणम् ।
प्रवक्ष्यामि समासेन दुर्लभं त्वकृतात्मनाम् ॥
1.35.m:
Jānanti said:
“Listen, O tiger among Brahmins, to the cause of severing worldly existence, / which I shall declare in brief, difficult to attain for those whose minds are undisciplined.

1.35.s:
bhaja viṣṇuṃ paraṃ nityaṃ smara nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum /
parāpavādaṃ paiśunyaṃ kadācidapi mā kṛthāḥ //
1.35.d:
भज विष्णुं परं नित्यं स्मर नारायणं प्रभुम् ।
परापवादं पैशुन्यं कदाचिदपि मा कृथाः ॥
1.35.m: Constantly worship the supreme Viṣṇu; remember the lord Nārāyaṇa. / Never engage in slandering others or in calumny.

1.35.s:
paropakāranirataḥ sa dā bhava mahāmate /
haripūjāparaścaiva tyaja mūrkhasamāgamam //
1.35.d:
परोपकारनिरतः स दा भव महामते ।
हरिपूजापरश्चैव त्यज मूर्खसमागमम् ॥
1.35.m: Always be devoted to the welfare of others, O highly intelligent one; / be dedicated to the worship of Hari, and abandon the company of fools.

1.35.s:
kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca mohaṃ ca madamatsarau /
parityajyātmavallokaṃ dṛṣṭvā śāntiṃ gamiṣyasi //
1.35.d:
कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च मोहं च मदमत्सरौ ।
परित्यज्यात्मवल्लोकं दृष्ट्वा शान्तिं गमिष्यसि ॥
1.35.m: Abandoning desire, anger, greed, delusion, arrogance, and envy, / and viewing the world as yourself, you will attain peace.

1.35.s:
asūyāṃ paranindāṃ ca kadācidapi mā kuru /
draṃbhācāramahṝṅkāraṃ naiṣṭhuryaṃ ca parityaja //
1.35.d:
असूयां परनिन्दां च कदाचिदपि मा कुरु ।
द्रंभाचारमहॄङ्कारं नैष्ठुर्यं च परित्यज ॥
1.35.m: Never indulge in malice or censuring others; / renounce hypocritical conduct, egotism, and cruelty.

1.35.s:
dayāṃ kuruṣva bhuteṣu śuśrūṣāṃ ca tathā satām /
tvayā kṛtāṃśca dharmānvai mā prakāśaya pucchatām //
1.35.d:
दयां कुरुष्व भुतेषु शुश्रूषां च तथा सताम् ।
त्वया कृतांश्च धर्मान्वै मा प्रकाशय पुच्छताम् ॥
1.35.m: Show compassion to living beings and attendance upon the virtuous; / and do not disclose to those who inquire the righteous deeds you have done.

1.35.s:
anācāraparāndṛṣṭvā nopekṣāṃ kuru śaktitaḥ /
pūjayasvātiyiṃ nityaṃ svakuṭuṃbāvirodhataḥ //
1.35.d:
अनाचारपरान्दृष्ट्वा नोपेक्षां कुरु शक्तितः ।
पूजयस्वातियिं नित्यं स्वकुटुंबाविरोधतः ॥
1.35.m: Seeing those intent on improper conduct, do not be indifferent according to your ability. / Constantly honour a guest without causing hardship to your family.

1.35.s:
patraiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalairvāpi dūrvābhiḥ pallavairatha /
pūjayasva jagannāthaṃ nārāyaṇamakāṃ mataḥ //
1.35.d:
पत्रैः पुष्पैः फलैर्वापि दूर्वाभिः पल्लवैरथ ।
पूजयस्व जगन्नाथं नारायणमकां मतः ॥
1.35.m: With leaves, flowers, or fruits, or with dūrvā grass and shoots, / worship Nārāyaṇa, the lord of the world, free from selfish desires.

1.35.s:
devānṛpīnpitṝścāpi tarpayasva yathāvidhi /
agreśca vidhivadvapra paricaryāparo bhava //
1.35.d:
देवानृपीन्पितॄश्चापि तर्पयस्व यथाविधि ।
अग्रेश्च विधिवद्वप्र परिचर्यापरो भव ॥
1.35.m: Offer water libations duly to gods, sages, and ancestors; / and, O Brahmin, be devoted to attending upon the fire in accordance with the rules.

1.35.s:
devatāyatane nityaṃ saṃmārjanaparo bhava /
tathopalepanaṃ caiva kuruṣva susamāhitaḥ //
1.35.d:
देवतायतने नित्यं संमार्जनपरो भव ।
तथोपलेपनं चैव कुरुष्व सुसमाहितः ॥
1.35.m: Always be intent on sweeping the temple of the deity, / and well-concentrated, perform plastering [its floor].

1.35.s:
śīrṇasphaṭitasaṃdhānaṃ kuru devagṛhe sadā /
mārgaśobhāṃ ca dīpaṃ ca viṣṇorāyatane kuru //
1.35.d:
शीर्णस्फटितसंधानं कुरु देवगृहे सदा ।
मार्गशोभां च दीपं च विष्णोरायतने कुरु ॥
1.35.m: Always repair what is broken and cracked in the house of God; / make the approach path beautiful, and offer lamps in the temple of Viṣṇu.

1.35.s:
kandamūlaphalairvāpi sadā pūjaya mādhavam /
pradakṣiṇanamaskāraiḥ stotrāṇāṃ paṭhanaistathā //
1.35.d:
कन्दमूलफलैर्वापि सदा पूजय माधवम् ।
प्रदक्षिणनमस्कारैः स्तोत्राणां पठनैस्तथा ॥
1.35.m: Constantly worship Mādhava with bulbs, roots, or fruits, / with circumambulations, prostrations, and the recitation of hymns.

1.35.s:
yurāṇaśravaṇaṃ caiva purāṇapaṭhanaṃ tathā /
vedāntapaṭhanaṃ caiva pratyahaṃ kuru śaktitaḥ //
1.35.d:
युराणश्रवणं चैव पुराणपठनं तथा ।
वेदान्तपठनं चैव प्रत्यहं कुरु शक्तितः ॥
1.35.m: Hear the Purāṇas, recite the Purāṇas, / and recite the Vedānta every day according to your ability.

1.35.s:
evaṃ sthiti tava jñānaṃ bhaghaviṣyatyuttamottamam /
jñānātsamastapāpānāṃ mokṣo bhavati niścitam //
1.35.d:
एवं स्थिति तव ज्ञानं भघविष्यत्युत्तमोत्तमम् ।
ज्ञानात्समस्तपापानां मोक्षो भवति निश्चितम् ॥
1.35.m: In this condition, the most excellent knowledge will arise in you; / from knowledge, release from all sins is assuredly achieved.”

1.35.s:
evaṃ prabodhitastena vedamālirmahāmatiḥ /
tathā jñānarato nityaṃ jñānaleśamavāptavān //
1.35.d:
एवं प्रबोधितस्तेन वेदमालिर्महामतिः ।
तथा ज्ञानरतो नित्यं ज्ञानलेशमवाप्तवान् ॥
1.35.m: Thus awakened by him, the highly intelligent Vedamālin, / ever intent on knowledge in that manner, attained a fraction of knowledge.

1.35.s:
vedamāliḥ kadācittu jñānaleśapracoditaḥ /
ko 'haṃ mama kriyā keti svayameva vyaktintayat //
1.35.d:
वेदमालिः कदाचित्तु ज्ञानलेशप्रचोदितः ।
को ऽहं मम क्रिया केति स्वयमेव व्यक्तिन्तयत् ॥
1.35.m: One day Vedamālin, impelled by that fraction of knowledge, / reflected within himself: “Who am I? What is my action?”

1.35.s:
mama janma kathaṃ jātaṃ rūpaṃ kīdṛgvidhaṃ mama /
evaṃ vicāraṇaparoḥ divāniśamatandritaḥ //
1.35.d:
मम जन्म कथं जातं रूपं कीदृग्विधं मम ।
एवं विचारणपरोः दिवानिशमतन्द्रितः ॥
1.35.m: “How did my birth come about? What kind of form is mine?” / Ever engaged in such inquiry, unwearied day and night,

1.35.s:
aniścitamatirbhūtvā vedamālirddhijottamaḥ /
punarjānantimāgamya praṇamyedamuvāca ha //
1.35.d:
अनिश्चितमतिर्भूत्वा वेदमालिर्द्धिजोत्तमः ।
पुनर्जानन्तिमागम्य प्रणम्येदमुवाच ह ॥
1.35.m: with an unsettled mind, Vedamālin, the best of Brahmins, / approached Jānanti once again, bowed down, and said:

1.35.s:
vedamāliruvāca
mama cittamatibhrātaṃ guro brahmavidāṃ vara /
ko 'haṃ mama kriyā kā ca mama janma kathaṃ vada //
1.35.d:
वेदमालिरुवाच
मम चित्तमतिभ्रातं गुरो ब्रह्मविदां वर ।
को ऽहं मम क्रिया का च मम जन्म कथं वद ॥
1.35.m:
Vedamālin said:
“My mind is deeply bewildered, O guru, best among knowers of Brahman! / Who am I? What is my action? And how did my birth occur? Tell me!”

1.35.s:
jānantiruvāca
satyaṃ satyaṃ mahābhāgaṃ cittaṃ bhrātaṃ suniścitam /
avidyānilarya cittaṃ kathaṃ sadbhāvagagameṣyati //
1.35.d:
जानन्तिरुवाच
सत्यं सत्यं महाभागं चित्तं भ्रातं सुनिश्चितम् ।
अविद्यानिलर्य चित्तं कथं सद्भावगगमेष्यति ॥
1.35.m:
Jānanti said:
“Truly, truly, O highly fortunate one, the mind is thoroughly confused! / For how can a mind that is the abode of ignorance attain the true reality?

1.35.s:
mameti gaditaṃ yattu tadapi bhrāntiriṣyate /
ahṝṅkāro manodharma ātmano nahi paṇḍita //
1.35.d:
ममेति गदितं यत्तु तदपि भ्रान्तिरिष्यते ।
अहॄङ्कारो मनोधर्म आत्मनो नहि पण्डित ॥
1.35.m: Even that which is called ‘mine’ is regarded as delusion; / egotism is a property of the mind, not of the Self, O wise one.

1.35.s:
punaśca ko 'hamityuktaṃ vedamāle tvayā tu yat /
mama jātyādi śūnyasya kathaṃ nāma karomyaham //
1.35.d:
पुनश्च को ऽहमित्युक्तं वेदमाले त्वया तु यत् ।
मम जात्यादि शून्यस्य कथं नाम करोम्यहम् ॥
1.35.m: Furthermore, as to what you asked, ‘Who am I?’, O Vedamālin: / how can I give a name to [the Self] that is devoid of caste, [birth], and the like?

1.35.s:
anaupamyasvabhāvasya nirguṇasya parātmanaḥ /
nīrūpasyāprameyasya kathaṃ nāma karomyaham //
1.35.d:
अनौपम्यस्वभावस्य निर्गुणस्य परात्मनः ।
नीरूपस्याप्रमेयस्य कथं नाम करोम्यहम् ॥
1.35.m: To the supreme Self whose nature is incomparable, devoid of attributes, / formless, and immeasurable—how can I give a name?

1.35.s:
parajyotiḥ svarūpasya paripūrṇāvyayātmanaḥ /
avicchinnasvabhāvasya kathyate ca kathaṃ kriyā //
1.35.d:
परज्योतिः स्वरूपस्य परिपूर्णाव्ययात्मनः ।
अविच्छिन्नस्वभावस्य कथ्यते च कथं क्रिया ॥
1.35.m: To that whose essential form is supreme light, the complete, immutable Self, / whose nature is unbroken—how can action be predicated?

1.35.s:
svaprakāśātmano vipra nityasya paramātmanaḥ /
anantasya kriyā caiva kathaṃ janma ca kathyate //
1.35.d:
स्वप्रकाशात्मनो विप्र नित्यस्य परमात्मनः ।
अनन्तस्य क्रिया चैव कथं जन्म च कथ्यते ॥
1.35.m: Of the supreme Self, self-luminous, eternal, / and infinite, O Brahmin, how can action or birth be spoken of?

1.35.s:
jñānaikavedyamajaraṃ paraṃ brahma sanātanam /
paripūrṇaṃ parānandaṃ tasmānnānyadiha dvija //
1.35.d:
ज्ञानैकवेद्यमजरं परं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
परिपूर्णं परानन्दं तस्मान्नान्यदिह द्विज ॥
1.35.m: The ageless, supreme Brahman is known by knowledge alone; it is eternal, / complete, and supreme bliss; other than that there is nothing here, O Brahmin.

1.35.s:
tattvamasyādivākyebhyo jñānaṃ mokṣasya sādhanam /
jñāne tvanāhate siddhe sarvaṃ brahmamayaṃ bhavet //
1.35.d:
तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्येभ्यो ज्ञानं मोक्षस्य साधनम् ।
ज्ञाने त्वनाहते सिद्धे सर्वं ब्रह्ममयं भवेत् ॥
1.35.m: From statements such as ‘Thou art that’ arises knowledge, the means to liberation; / when that pure knowledge is accomplished, everything becomes Brahman.

1.35.s:
evaṃ prabodhitastena vedamālirmunīśvara /
mumoda paśyannātmānamātmanyevācyutaṃ prabhum //
1.35.d:
एवं प्रबोधितस्तेन वेदमालिर्मुनीश्वर ।
मुमोद पश्यन्नात्मानमात्मन्येवाच्युतं प्रभुम् ॥
1.35.m: Thus awakened by him, O lord of sages, Vedamālin / rejoiced, seeing the Self, the lord Acyuta, within the Self alone.

1.35.s:
upādhirahitaṃ brahma svaprakāśaṃ nirañjanam /
ahameveti niścitya parāṃ śāntimavāptavān //
1.35.d:
उपाधिरहितं ब्रह्म स्वप्रकाशं निरञ्जनम् ।
अहमेवेति निश्चित्य परां शान्तिमवाप्तवान् ॥
1.35.m: Ascertaining ‘I alone am Brahman, free from conditioning adjuncts, self-luminous, and taintless,’ / he attained supreme peace.

1.35.s:
tataśca vyavahārārthaṃ vedamālirmunīśvaram /
guruṃ praṇamya jānanti sadā dhyānaparo 'bhavat //
1.35.d:
ततश्च व्यवहारार्थं वेदमालिर्मुनीश्वरम् ।
गुरुं प्रणम्य जानन्ति सदा ध्यानपरो ऽभवत् ॥
1.35.m: Then, for the sake of practical conduct, Vedamālin, / having bowed down to his guru Jānanti, best among sages, remained ever devoted to meditation.

1.35.s:
gate bahutithe kāle vedamālirmunīśva /
vārāṇasīpuraṃ prāpya paraṃ mokṣamavāptavān //
1.35.d:
गते बहुतिथे काले वेदमालिर्मुनीश्व ।
वाराणसीपुरं प्राप्य परं मोक्षमवाप्तवान् ॥
1.35.m: When a long period of time had elapsed, Vedamālin, O lord of sages, / reached the city of Vārāṇasī and attained supreme liberation.

1.35.s:
ya imaṃ paṭhate 'dhyāyaṃ śṛṇuyādvā samāhitaḥ /
sa karmapāśavicchedaṃ prāpya saukhyamavānpuyāt //
iti śrībṛhannārādīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde jñānanirūpaṇa nāma pañcatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.35.d:
य इमं पठते ऽध्यायं शृणुयाद्वा समाहितः ।
स कर्मपाशविच्छेदं प्राप्य सौख्यमवान्पुयात् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारादीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे ज्ञाननिरूपण नाम पञ्चत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.35.m:
Whoever recites this chapter or hears it with concentrated mind / shall sever the bondage of karma and attain happiness.

Thus ends the thirty-fifth chapter, named ‘Exposition of Knowledge’, in the first quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.36.s:
sanaka uvāca
vedamāleḥ sutau proktau yāvubhau munisattama /
yajñamālī sumālī ca tayoḥ karmādhunocyata //
1.36.d:
सनक उवाच
वेदमालेः सुतौ प्रोक्तौ यावुभौ मुनिसत्तम ।
यज्ञमाली सुमाली च तयोः कर्माधुनोच्यत ॥
1.36.m:
Sanaka said:
“The two sons of Vedamālin who were mentioned, O best of sages— / Yajñamālin and Sumālin—their conduct is now described.

1.36.s:
tayorādyo yajñamālī vibheda pitṛsaṃcitam /
dhanaṃ dvidhā kaniṣṭasya bhāgamekaṃ dadau tadā //
1.36.d:
तयोराद्यो यज्ञमाली विभेद पितृसंचितम् ।
धनं द्विधा कनिष्टस्य भागमेकं ददौ तदा ॥
1.36.m: The elder of them, Yajñamālin, divided the wealth accumulated by their father / into two parts and gave one share to his younger brother.

1.36.s:
sumālī ca dhanaṃ sarvaṃ vyasanābhirakataḥ sadā /
apādānā dibhiścaiva nāśayāmāsa bho dvija //
1.36.d:
सुमाली च धनं सर्वं व्यसनाभिरकतः सदा ।
अपादाना दिभिश्चैव नाशयामास भो द्विज ॥
1.36.m: And Sumālin, constantly addicted to vices, O Brahmin, / squandered all that wealth through inappropriate gifts and other means.

1.36.s:
gītavādyarato nityaṃ madyapānarato 'bhavat /
veśyāvibhramalubdho 'sau paradārato 'bhavat //
1.36.d:
गीतवाद्यरतो नित्यं मद्यपानरतो ऽभवत् ।
वेश्याविभ्रमलुब्धो ऽसौ परदारतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.36.m: Always devoted to singing and instrumental music, he indulged in drinking wine; / infatuated by the charms of prostitutes, he committed adultery with others' wives.

1.36.s:
sarvasminnāśamāyāte hiraṇye pitṛsaṃcite /
apahṛtya paraṃ dravyaṃ vārastrīnirato 'bhavat //
1.36.d:
सर्वस्मिन्नाशमायाते हिरण्ये पितृसंचिते ।
अपहृत्य परं द्रव्यं वारस्त्रीनिरतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.36.m: When all the gold accumulated by his father had been completely exhausted, / he stole other people's property and remained devoted to courtesans.

1.36.s:
dṛṣṭvā sumālinaḥ śūlaṃ yajñamālī mahāmatiḥ /
babhūva duḥkhito 'tyarthaṃ bhrātaraṃ cedamabravīt //
1.36.d:
दृष्ट्वा सुमालिनः शूलं यज्ञमाली महामतिः ।
बभूव दुःखितो ऽत्यर्थं भ्रातरं चेदमब्रवीत् ॥
1.36.m: Seeing the wicked nature of Sumālin, the highly intelligent Yajñamālin / became exceedingly grieved and said to his brother:

1.36.s:
alamamatyantakaṣṭena vṛttenāsmatkule 'nuja /
tvameka eva duṣṭātmā mahāpāparato 'bhavaḥ //
1.36.d:
अलममत्यन्तकष्टेन वृत्तेनास्मत्कुले ऽनुज ।
त्वमेक एव दुष्टात्मा महापापरतो ऽभवः ॥
1.36.m: ‘Enough of such deeply shameful conduct in our family, younger brother! / You alone are wicked-minded, devoted to terrible sin!’

1.36.s:
evaṃ nivārayantaṃ taṃ bahuśo jyeṣṭasodaram /
haniṣyāmīti niścitya khaḍgahastaḥ kace 'grahīt //
1.36.d:
एवं निवारयन्तं तं बहुशो ज्येष्टसोदरम् ।
हनिष्यामीति निश्चित्य खड्गहस्तः कचे ऽग्रहीत् ॥
1.36.m: As he repeatedly restrained him thus, [Sumālin], sword in hand, / seized his elder brother by the hair, resolved: ‘I will kill him!’”

1.36.s:
tato mahāravo jajñe nagare bhṛśadāruṇaḥ /
babandhurnāgarāścainaṃ kupitāste sumālinam //
1.36.d:
ततो महारवो जज्ञे नगरे भृशदारुणः ।
बबन्धुर्नागराश्चैनं कुपितास्ते सुमालिनम् ॥
1.36.m: Then a very dreadful, great outcry arose in the city; / and those citizens, enraged, bound Sumālī.

1.36.s:
yajñamālī hyameyātmā paurānsaṃprārthya duḥkhitaḥ /
bandhanānmocayāmāsa bhrātṛsnehavimohitaḥ //
1.36.d:
यज्ञमाली ह्यमेयात्मा पौरान्संप्रार्थ्य दुःखितः ।
बन्धनान्मोचयामास भ्रातृस्नेहविमोहितः ॥
1.36.m: Yajñamālī of boundless soul, grieved, entreated the citizens, / and, infatuated by love for his brother, released him from captivity.

1.36.s:
yajñamālī punaścāpi bibhide svadhanaṃ dvidhā /
ādade svayamarddhaṃ ca dadāvarddhaṃ yavīyase //
1.36.d:
यज्ञमाली पुनश्चापि बिभिदे स्वधनं द्विधा ।
आददे स्वयमर्द्धं च ददावर्द्धं यवीयसे ॥
1.36.m: And Yajñamālī further divided his wealth into two parts: / he himself took one half, and gave the other half to his younger brother.

1.36.s:
sumālī tvatimūḍhātmā taddhanaṃ cāpi nārada /
mūrkhaiḥ pāraṃvaḍacaṇḍālairbubhuje ca sahoddhataḥ //
1.36.d:
सुमाली त्वतिमूढात्मा तद्धनं चापि नारद ।
मूर्खैः पारंवडचण्डालैर्बुभुजे च सहोद्धतः ॥
1.36.m: Sumālī, however, utterly foolish, O Nārada, / arrogantly squandered that wealth with fools, outcasts, and cāṇḍālas.

1.36.s:
asatāmupabho gāya durjanānāṃ vibhūtayaḥ /
picumandaḥ phalāḍhyo 'pi kākairevopabhujyate //
1.36.d:
असतामुपभो गाय दुर्जनानां विभूतयः ।
पिचुमन्दः फलाढ्यो ऽपि काकैरेवोपभुज्यते ॥
1.36.m: The riches of wicked people are for the enjoyment of the unrighteous; / the neem tree, though full of fruit, is eaten only by crows.

1.36.s:
bhrātrā dattaṃ dhanaṃ tañca sumālī nāśayanmune /
madyapānapramattaśca gomāṃsā dīnyabhakṣayat //
1.36.d:
भ्रात्रा दत्तं धनं तञ्च सुमाली नाशयन्मुने ।
मद्यपानप्रमत्तश्च गोमांसा दीन्यभक्षयत् ॥
1.36.m: Wasting the wealth given by his brother, O sage, / Sumālī, drunk from drinking wine, ate beef and other [forbidden foods].

1.36.s:
tyakto bandhujanaiḥ sarvaiścāṇḍālastrīsamanvitaḥ /
rājñāpi bādhito vipraprapede nirjanaṃ vanam //
1.36.d:
त्यक्तो बन्धुजनैः सर्वैश्चाण्डालस्त्रीसमन्वितः ।
राज्ञापि बाधितो विप्रप्रपेदे निर्जनं वनम् ॥
1.36.m: Forsaken by all his kinsmen, accompanied by an outcast cāṇḍāla woman, / and expelled by the king, O brāhmaṇa, he took refuge in a deserted forest.

1.36.s:
yajñamālī sudhīrvipra sadā dharmarato 'bhavet /
avāritaṃ dadāvannaṃ satsaṅgagatakalmaṣaḥ //
1.36.d:
यज्ञमाली सुधीर्विप्र सदा धर्मरतो ऽभवेत् ।
अवारितं ददावन्नं सत्सङ्गगतकल्मषः ॥
1.36.m: Wise Yajñamālī, O brāhmaṇa, was always devoted to dharma; / with his sins removed by good association, he gave food without restriction.

1.36.s:
pitrā kṛtāni sarvāṇi taḍāgādīni sattama /
apālayatprayatnena sadā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.36.d:
पित्रा कृतानि सर्वाणि तडागादीनि सत्तम ।
अपालयत्प्रयत्नेन सदा धर्मपरायणः ॥
1.36.m: All the reservoirs and other works made by his father, O best of men, / he carefully maintained, ever dedicated to dharma.

1.36.s:
viśrāṇitaṃ dhanaṃ sarvaṃ yajñamālermahātmanaḥ /
satpātradānaniṣṭasya dharmamārgapravartinaḥ //
1.36.d:
विश्राणितं धनं सर्वं यज्ञमालेर्महात्मनः ।
सत्पात्रदाननिष्टस्य धर्ममार्गप्रवर्तिनः ॥
1.36.m: All the wealth of high-souled Yajñamālī was given away, / steadfast as he was in gifts to worthy recipients, proceeding along the path of dharma.

1.36.s:
aho sadupabhogāya sajjanānāṃ vibhūtayaḥ /
kalpavṛkṣaphalaṃ sarvamamaraireva bhujyate //
1.36.d:
अहो सदुपभोगाय सज्जनानां विभूतयः ।
कल्पवृक्षफलं सर्वममरैरेव भुज्यते ॥
1.36.m: Ah! The wealth of good people is for good enjoyment; / the entire fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree is consumed only by the immortals.

1.36.s:
dhanaṃ viśrāṇya dharmārthaṃ yajñamālī mahāmatiḥ /
nityaṃ viṣṇugṛhe samyakparicaryyāparo 'bhavat //
1.36.d:
धनं विश्राण्य धर्मार्थं यज्ञमाली महामतिः ।
नित्यं विष्णुगृहे सम्यक्परिचर्य्यापरो ऽभवत् ॥
1.36.m: Having bestowed his wealth for the sake of dharma, the highly intelligent Yajñamālī / was constantly and properly devoted to service in the temple of Viṣṇu.

1.36.s:
kālena gacchatā tau tu vṛddhabhāvamupāgatau /
yajñamālī sumālī ca hyekakāle mṛtāvubhau //
1.36.d:
कालेन गच्छता तौ तु वृद्धभावमुपागतौ ।
यज्ञमाली सुमाली च ह्येककाले मृतावुभौ ॥
1.36.m: With the passage of time, the two of them reached old age; / and both Yajñamālī and Sumālī died at the very same time.

1.36.s:
haripūjāratasyāsya yajñamālimahātmanaḥ /
hariḥ saṃpreṣayāmāsa vimānaṃ pārṣadā vṛtam //
1.36.d:
हरिपूजारतस्यास्य यज्ञमालिमहात्मनः ।
हरिः संप्रेषयामास विमानं पार्षदा वृतम् ॥
1.36.m: For this high-souled Yajñamālī, who was devoted to the worship of Hari, / Hari sent an aerial chariot surrounded by his attendants.

1.36.s:
divyaṃ vimānamāruhya yajñamālī mahāmatiḥ /
pūjyamānaḥ suragaṇaiḥ stūyamāno munīśvaraiḥ //
1.36.d:
दिव्यं विमानमारुह्य यज्ञमाली महामतिः ।
पूज्यमानः सुरगणैः स्तूयमानो मुनीश्वरैः ॥
1.36.m: Ascending the celestial chariot, the highly intelligent Yajñamālī, / worshipped by hosts of gods and praised by sovereign sages,

1.36.s:
gandharvairgīyamānaśca sevitaścāpsarogaṇaiḥ /
kāmadhenvā puṣyamāṇaścitrābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ //
1.36.d:
गन्धर्वैर्गीयमानश्च सेवितश्चाप्सरोगणैः ।
कामधेन्वा पुष्यमाणश्चित्राभरणभूषितः ॥
1.36.m: sung to by gandharvas and attended by hosts of apsarases, / nourished by Kāmadhenu and adorned with varied ornaments,

1.36.s:
komalaistulasīmālyairbhūṣitastejasāṃ nidhiḥ /
gacchanviṣṇupadaṃ divyaṃmanujaṃ pathi dṛṣṭavān //
1.36.d:
कोमलैस्तुलसीमाल्यैर्भूषितस्तेजसां निधिः ।
गच्छन्विष्णुपदं दिव्यंमनुजं पथि दृष्टवान् ॥
1.36.m: adorned with delicate tulasī garlands, a repository of splendours, / going to the celestial realm of Viṣṇu, saw a man upon the road:

1.36.s:
tāhyamānaṃ yamabhaṭaiḥ kṣuttṛḍbhyāṃ paripīḍitam /
pretabhūtaṃ vivastraṃ ca duḥkhitaṃ pāśaveṣṭitam /
itastataḥ prādhāvantaṃ vilapantamanāthavat //
1.36.d:
ताह्यमानं यमभटैः क्षुत्तृड्भ्यां परिपीडितम् ।
प्रेतभूतं विवस्त्रं च दुःखितं पाशवेष्टितम् ।
इतस्ततः प्राधावन्तं विलपन्तमनाथवत् ॥
1.36.m: beaten by Yama's soldiers, afflicted by hunger and thirst, / turned into a ghost, naked, wretched, bound with cords, / running hither and thither, lamenting like a helpless orphan.

1.36.s: krośantaṃ ca sudantaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā manasi vivyathe //
1.36.d: क्रोशन्तं च सुदन्तं च दृष्ट्वा मनसि विव्यथे ॥
1.36.m: Seeing him weeping loudly and crying bitterly, his heart was pained.

1.36.s:
yajñamālīdayāyukto viṣṇudūtānsamīpagān /
ko 'yaṃ bhaṭairbādhyamānaṃ ityapṛcchatkṛtāñjaliḥ //
1.36.d:
यज्ञमालीदयायुक्तो विष्णुदूतान्समीपगान् ।
को ऽयं भटैर्बाध्यमानं इत्यपृच्छत्कृताञ्जलिः ॥
1.36.m: Yajñamālī, moved with compassion, with joined palms / asked Viṣṇu's messengers who were near: "Who is this man being tormented by the soldiers?"

1.36.s:
atha te haridūtāstaṃ yajñamālimahaujasam /
asau sumālī bhrātā te pāpātmeti samabruvan //
1.36.d:
अथ ते हरिदूतास्तं यज्ञमालिमहौजसम् ।
असौ सुमाली भ्राता ते पापात्मेति समब्रुवन् ॥
1.36.m: Then those messengers of Hari said to the immensely powerful Yajñamālī: / "This is your sinful brother Sumālī."

1.36.s:
yajñamālī samākarṇya vyākhyātaṃ viṣṇukiṅkaraiḥ /
manasā duḥkhamāpannaḥ punaḥ papraccha nārada //
1.36.d:
यज्ञमाली समाकर्ण्य व्याख्यातं विष्णुकिङ्करैः ।
मनसा दुःखमापन्नः पुनः पप्रच्छ नारद ॥
1.36.m: Hearing the explanation given by Viṣṇu's servants, / Yajñamālī became sorrowful at heart, and asked again, O Nārada:

1.36.s:
kathamasya bhavenmokṣaḥ sāṃcitaiḥ pāpasaṃcayaiḥ /
tadupāyaṃbadadhvaṃ me yūyaṃ hi mamabāndhavāḥ //
1.36.d:
कथमस्य भवेन्मोक्षः सांचितैः पापसंचयैः ।
तदुपायंबदध्वं मे यूयं हि ममबान्धवाः ॥
1.36.m: "How can there be liberation for him from his accumulated heaps of sins? / Tell me the means for that, for you are indeed my kin.

1.36.s:
sakhyaṃ sāptapadīnaṃ syādityāhurdharmakovidāḥ /
satāṃ sāptapadī maitrī satsatāṃ tripadī tathā //
1.36.d:
सख्यं साप्तपदीनं स्यादित्याहुर्धर्मकोविदाः ।
सतां साप्तपदी मैत्री सत्सतां त्रिपदी तथा ॥
1.36.m: Those who know dharma say that friendship takes place upon seven paces; / the friendship of the virtuous is formed in seven paces, and that of the very virtuous in three paces;

1.36.s: satsatāmapi ye saṃtasteṣāṃ maitraghī pade pade //
1.36.d: सत्सतामपि ये संतस्तेषां मैत्रघी पदे पदे ॥
1.36.m: and of those who are the virtuous among the virtuous, friendship forms at every single step.

1.36.s:
tasmānme bāndhavā yūyaṃ māṃ netuṃ samupāgatāḥ /
yato 'yaṃ mama bhrātāpi mucyate tadihocyatām //
1.36.d:
तस्मान्मे बान्धवा यूयं मां नेतुं समुपागताः ।
यतो ऽयं मम भ्रातापि मुच्यते तदिहोच्यताम् ॥
1.36.m: Therefore, you who have come to lead me away are my kin. / Tell me here how this brother of mine too may be liberated."

1.36.s:
yajñamālivacaḥ śrutvā viṣṇudūtā dayālavaḥ /
punaḥ smitāmukhāḥ procuryajñamāliharipriyam //
1.36.d:
यज्ञमालिवचः श्रुत्वा विष्णुदूता दयालवः ।
पुनः स्मितामुखाः प्रोचुर्यज्ञमालिहरिप्रियम् ॥
1.36.m: Hearing the words of Yajñamālī, the compassionate messengers of Viṣṇu, / their faces smiling, spoke once again to Yajñamālī, beloved of Hari.

1.36.s:
viṣṇudūtā ūcuḥ
yajñamālinmahābhāga nārāyaṇaparāyaṇa /
upāyaṃ tava vakṣyāmaḥ sumālipremamuktidam //
1.36.d:
विष्णुदूता ऊचुः
यज्ञमालिन्महाभाग नारायणपरायण ।
उपायं तव वक्ष्यामः सुमालिप्रेममुक्तिदम् ॥
1.36.m: The messengers of Viṣṇu said: / "O highly fortunate Yajñamālī, dedicated to Nārāyaṇa, / we shall tell you the means that will lovingly bestow liberation upon Sumālī.

1.36.s:
kṛtaṃ yatsumahatkarma tvayā prāktanajanmani /
pravakṣyāmaḥ samāsena tacchraṇuṣva samāhitaḥ //
1.36.d:
कृतं यत्सुमहत्कर्म त्वया प्राक्तनजन्मनि ।
प्रवक्ष्यामः समासेन तच्छ्रणुष्व समाहितः ॥
1.36.m: We shall explain briefly the great deed done by you / in your previous birth; listen to it attentively.

1.36.s:
purā tvaṃ vaiśyajātīyo nāmnā viśvaṅghabharaḥ smṛtaḥ /
tvayā kṛtāni pāpāni ahantyagaṇitāni vai //
1.36.d:
पुरा त्वं वैश्यजातीयो नाम्ना विश्वङ्घभरः स्मृतः ।
त्वया कृतानि पापानि अहन्त्यगणितानि वै ॥
1.36.m: Formerly you belonged to the vaiśya caste, known by the name of Viśvaṅghabhara; / by you were committed sins, day and night, without count.

1.36.s:
sukarmavāsanāhīno mātāpitrorvirodhakṛt /
ekadā bandhubhistyaktaḥ śokasaṃtāpapīḍitaḥ //
1.36.d:
सुकर्मवासनाहीनो मातापित्रोर्विरोधकृत् ।
एकदा बन्धुभिस्त्यक्तः शोकसंतापपीडितः ॥
1.36.m: Lacking any inclination for virtuous action, causing conflict with your parents, / you were once abandoned by your kinsmen, afflicted by grief and torment.

1.36.s:
kṣudhāgnināpi saṃtaptaḥ prāptavānharimandiram /
tadā vṛṣṭirabhūttatra tatsthānaṃ paṅkilaṃ hyabhūta //
1.36.d:
क्षुधाग्निनापि संतप्तः प्राप्तवान्हरिमन्दिरम् ।
तदा वृष्टिरभूत्तत्र तत्स्थानं पङ्किलं ह्यभूत ॥
1.36.m: Tormented also by the fire of hunger, you reached a temple of Hari; / then rain fell there, and that place became muddy.

1.36.s:
dīrīkṛtastvayā paṅkastatsthāne sthātumicchayā /
upalepanatāṃ prāptaṃ tatsthānaṃ viṣṇumandire //
tvayoṣitaṃ tu tadgātrau tasmindevālaye dvija /
daṃśitaścaiva sarpeṇa prāptaṃ pañcatvameva ca //
tena puṇyaprabhāvena upalepakṛtena ca /
viprajanma tvayā prāptaṃ hari bhaktistathācalā //
1.36.d:
दीरीकृतस्त्वया पङ्कस्तत्स्थाने स्थातुमिच्छया ।
उपलेपनतां प्राप्तं तत्स्थानं विष्णुमन्दिरे ॥
त्वयोषितं तु तद्गात्रौ तस्मिन्देवालये द्विज ।
दंशितश्चैव सर्पेण प्राप्तं पञ्चत्वमेव च ॥
तेन पुण्यप्रभावेन उपलेपकृतेन च ।
विप्रजन्म त्वया प्राप्तं हरि भक्तिस्तथाचला ॥
1.36.m:
The mud was cleared away by you with the wish to rest in that spot; / in that temple of Viṣṇu, that spot was thus smeared clean.

You remained in that divine temple that night, O twice-born; / bitten by a serpent, you met your demise.

Through the power of that merit produced by the smearing, / you attained birth as a brāhmaṇa, as well as unshakeable devotion to Hari.

1.36.s:
kalpakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ saṃprāpya harisannidhim /
vasādya jñānamāsādya paraṃ mokṣaṃ gamiṣyasi //
1.36.d:
कल्पकोटिशतं साग्रं संप्राप्य हरिसन्निधिम् ।
वसाद्य ज्ञानमासाद्य परं मोक्षं गमिष्यसि ॥
1.36.m: Reaching the presence of Hari for a full hundred crore kalpas, / dwell there, and obtaining knowledge, you will attain supreme liberation.

1.36.s:
anujaṃ pātakiśreṣṭhaṃ tvaṃ samuddharttamicchasi /
upāyaṃ tava vakṣyāmastaṃ nibodha mahāmate //
1.36.d:
अनुजं पातकिश्रेष्ठं त्वं समुद्धर्त्तमिच्छसि ।
उपायं तव वक्ष्यामस्तं निबोध महामते ॥
1.36.m: You wish to deliver your younger brother, the foremost among sinners; / we shall tell you the means for it: understand it, O highly intelligent one!

1.36.s:
gocarmamātrabhūmestu upalepanajaṃ phalam /
dattvoddhara mahābhāga bhrātaraṃ kṛpayānvitaḥ //
1.36.d:
गोचर्ममात्रभूमेस्तु उपलेपनजं फलम् ।
दत्त्वोद्धर महाभाग भ्रातरं कृपयान्वितः ॥
1.36.m: Bestow the fruit born of smearing a piece of ground merely the size of a cowhide, / and full of compassion, deliver your brother, O highly fortunate one!"

1.36.s:
evamukto viṣṇudūtairyajñamālī mahāpatiḥ /
tatphalaṃ pradadau tasmai bhrātre pāpavimuktaye //
1.36.d:
एवमुक्तो विष्णुदूतैर्यज्ञमाली महापतिः ।
तत्फलं प्रददौ तस्मै भ्रात्रे पापविमुक्तये ॥
1.36.m: Thus addressed by the messengers of Viṣṇu, the high-minded Yajñamālī / gave that fruit to his brother for his liberation from sins.

1.36.s:
sumālī bhrātṛdattena puṇyena gatakalmaṣaḥ /
babhūva yamadūtāstu taṃ tyaktvā prapalāyitāḥ //
1.36.d:
सुमाली भ्रातृदत्तेन पुण्येन गतकल्मषः ।
बभूव यमदूतास्तु तं त्यक्त्वा प्रपलायिताः ॥
1.36.m: Sumālī, freed from sin through the merit given by his brother, / was delivered, and the messengers of Yama, abandoning him, fled.

1.36.s:
vimānaṃ cāgataṃ sadyaḥ sarvabhogasamanvitam /
tadā sumālī svaryānamāruhya mumude mune //
1.36.d:
विमानं चागतं सद्यः सर्वभोगसमन्वितम् ।
तदा सुमाली स्वर्यानमारुह्य मुमुदे मुने ॥
1.36.m: And instantly an aerial chariot arrived, endowed with all luxuries; / then Sumālī, mounting the celestial chariot, rejoiced, O sage.

1.36.s:
tāvubhau bhrātarau vipra suravṛndanamaskṛtau /
avāpaturbhṛśaṃ prītiṃ samāliṅgya parasparam //
1.36.d:
तावुभौ भ्रातरौ विप्र सुरवृन्दनमस्कृतौ ।
अवापतुर्भृशं प्रीतिं समालिङ्ग्य परस्परम् ॥
1.36.m: Both brothers, O brāhmaṇa, saluted by the assembly of gods, / experienced great joy, having embraced one another.

1.36.s:
yajñamālī sumālī ca stūyamānau maharṣibhiḥ /
gīyamānau ca gandharvairviṣṇulokaṃ prajagmatuḥ //
1.36.d:
यज्ञमाली सुमाली च स्तूयमानौ महर्षिभिः ।
गीयमानौ च गन्धर्वैर्विष्णुलोकं प्रजग्मतुः ॥
1.36.m: Yajñamālī and Sumālī, praised by great ṛṣis / and sung to by gandharvas, proceeded to the world of Viṣṇu.

1.36.s:
avāpya harisālokyaṃ sumālī munisattama /
yajñamālī coṣatustau kalpamekaṃ mudānvitau //
1.36.d:
अवाप्य हरिसालोक्यं सुमाली मुनिसत्तम ।
यज्ञमाली चोषतुस्तौ कल्पमेकं मुदान्वितौ ॥
1.36.m: Attaining residence in the same realm as Hari, O best of sages, / both Sumālī and Yajñamālī lived for an entire kalpa, full of joy.

1.36.s:
bhuktvā bhogānbahūṃstatra yajñamālī mahāmatiḥ /
tatraiva jñānasaṃpannaḥ paraṃ mokṣamupāgataḥ //
1.36.d:
भुक्त्वा भोगान्बहूंस्तत्र यज्ञमाली महामतिः ।
तत्रैव ज्ञानसंपन्नः परं मोक्षमुपागतः ॥
1.36.m: Having enjoyed many pleasures there, the highly intelligent Yajñamālī, / endowed with knowledge right there, reached supreme liberation.

1.36.s:
sumālī tu mahābhāgo viṣṇuloke mudānvitaḥ /
sthitvā bhūmiṃ punaḥ prāpya vipratvaṃ samupāgataḥ //
1.36.d:
सुमाली तु महाभागो विष्णुलोके मुदान्वितः ।
स्थित्वा भूमिं पुनः प्राप्य विप्रत्वं समुपागतः ॥
1.36.m: Sumālī, the highly fortunate, dwelling with joy in the world of Viṣṇu, / returned to the earth and attained the status of a brāhmaṇa.

1.36.s:
atiśuddhe kule jāto guṇavānvedapāragaḥ /
sarvasaṃpatsamopeto haribhaktiparāyaṇaḥ //
1.36.d:
अतिशुद्धे कुले जातो गुणवान्वेदपारगः ।
सर्वसंपत्समोपेतो हरिभक्तिपरायणः ॥
1.36.m: Born into an exceedingly pure family, virtuous, master of the Vedas, / endowed with all fortunes, he was devoted to devotion to Hari.

1.36.s:
vyāharanharināmāni prapede jāhnavītaṭam /
tatra snātaśca gaṅgāyāṃ dṛṣṭvā viśveśvaraṃ prabhum //
1.36.d:
व्याहरन्हरिनामानि प्रपेदे जाह्नवीतटम् ।
तत्र स्नातश्च गङ्गायां दृष्ट्वा विश्वेश्वरं प्रभुम् ॥
1.36.m: Chanting the names of Hari, he reached the bank of the Jāhnavī; / having bathed there in the Gaṅgā and beheld Lord Viśveśvara,

1.36.s:
avāpa paramaṃ sthānaṃ yogināmapi durlabham /
upalepanamāhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ te munīśvara //
1.36.d:
अवाप परमं स्थानं योगिनामपि दुर्लभम् ।
उपलेपनमाहात्म्यं कथितं ते मुनीश्वर ॥
