1.36.m: he attained the supreme state, difficult to reach even for yogins. / The eulogy of the greatness of smearing [a temple] has thus been told to you, O sovereign sage.

1.36.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena saṃpūjyo jagatāṃpatiḥ /
akāmādapi ye viṣṇoḥ sakṛtpūjāṃ prakurvate //
1.36.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन संपूज्यो जगतांपतिः ।
अकामादपि ये विष्णोः सकृत्पूजां प्रकुर्वते ॥
1.36.m: Therefore, the Lord of the worlds should be worshipped with every effort. / Even without desire, those who worship Viṣṇu even once,

1.36.s:
na teṣāṃ bhavabandhastu kadācidapi jāyate /
haribhaktiratānyastu haribuddhyā samarcayet //
1.36.d:
न तेषां भवबन्धस्तु कदाचिदपि जायते ।
हरिभक्तिरतान्यस्तु हरिबुद्ध्या समर्चयेत् ॥
1.36.m: never again experience the bondage of worldly existence. / Moreover, one who worships those devoted to devotion to Hari, viewing them as Hari himself,

1.36.s:
tasya tuṣyanti viprendra brahmaviṣṇumaheśvarāḥ /
haribhaktiparāṇāṃ tu saṃgināṃ saṃgamātrataḥ //
1.36.d:
तस्य तुष्यन्ति विप्रेन्द्र ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वराः ।
हरिभक्तिपराणां तु संगिनां संगमात्रतः ॥
1.36.m: pleases Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara, O best of brahmins. / Merely through contact with those who associate with people devoted to Hari,

1.36.s:
mucyate sarvapāpebhyo mahāpātakavānapi /
haripūjāparāṇāṃ ca harināmaratātmanām //
1.36.d:
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यो महापातकवानपि ।
हरिपूजापराणां च हरिनामरतात्मनाम् ॥
1.36.m: even one guilty of a mortal sin is freed from all sins. / And for those devoted to serving those intent on Viṣṇu's worship

1.36.s:
śuśrūṣāniratā yānti pāpino 'pi parāṃ gatim //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde viṣṇusevāprabhāvo nāma ṣaṭtriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.36.d:
शुश्रूषानिरता यान्ति पापिनो ऽपि परां गतिम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे विष्णुसेवाप्रभावो नाम षट्त्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.36.m:
and devoted in mind to Hari's name, even sinners attain the supreme destination.

Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, named 'The Power of Service to Viṣṇu', in the first quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.37.s:
sanaka uvāca
bhūyaḥ śṛṇuṣva viprendra māhātmyaṃ kamalāpateḥ /
kasya no jāyate prītiḥ śrotuṃ harikathāmṛtam //
1.37.d:
सनक उवाच
भूयः शृणुष्व विप्रेन्द्र माहात्म्यं कमलापतेः ।
कस्य नो जायते प्रीतिः श्रोतुं हरिकथामृतम् ॥
1.37.m: Sanaka said: / Listen again, O best of brahmins, to the eulogy of greatness of the consort of Kamalā. / In whom does love not arise to hear the nectar of Hari’s tales?

1.37.s:
narāṇāṃ viṣayāndhānāṃ mamatākulacetasām /
ekameva harernāma sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
1.37.d:
नराणां विषयान्धानां ममताकुलचेतसाम् ।
एकमेव हरेर्नाम सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
1.37.m: For men who are blind to sense objects and whose minds are troubled by possessiveness, / the single name of Hari alone destroys all sins.

1.37.s:
sakṛdvā na namedyastu viṣṇuṃ pāpaharaṃ nṛṇām /
śvapacaṃ taṃ vijānīyātkadācinnālapeñca tam //
1.37.d:
सकृद्वा न नमेद्यस्तु विष्णुं पापहरं नृणाम् ।
श्वपचं तं विजानीयात्कदाचिन्नालपेञ्च तम् ॥
1.37.m: He who does not bow even once to Viṣṇu, the destroyer of men’s sins, / one should know him as a dog-cooker; one should never even converse with him.

1.37.s:
haripūjāvihīnaṃ tu yasya veśma dvijottama /
śmaśānasadṛśaṃ taddhi kadācidapi no viśet //
1.37.d:
हरिपूजाविहीनं तु यस्य वेश्म द्विजोत्तम ।
श्मशानसदृशं तद्धि कदाचिदपि नो विशेत् ॥
1.37.m: The house of a man that is devoid of the worship of Hari, O best of the twice-born, / is indeed like a cremation ground; one should never enter it.

1.37.s:
haripūjāvihīnāśca vedavidveṣiṇastathā /
godvijadveṣaniratā rākṣasāḥ parikīrttitāḥ //
1.37.d:
हरिपूजाविहीनाश्च वेदविद्वेषिणस्तथा ।
गोद्विजद्वेषनिरता राक्षसाः परिकीर्त्तिताः ॥
1.37.m: Those devoid of the worship of Hari, and likewise those who despise the Vedas, / intent on hostility toward cows and brahmins, are declared to be rākṣasas.

1.37.s:
yo vā ko vāpi viprendra vipradveṣaparāyaṇaḥ /
samarcayati govindaṃ tatpūjā viphalā bhavet //
1.37.d:
यो वा को वापि विप्रेन्द्र विप्रद्वेषपरायणः ।
समर्चयति गोविन्दं तत्पूजा विफला भवेत् ॥
1.37.m: Whoever he may be, O best of brahmins, if devoted to hostility toward brahmins, / he worships Govinda, that worship of his becomes fruitless.

1.37.s:
anyaśreyovināśārthaṃ yer'cayanti janārdanam /
sā pūjaiva mahābhāga pūjakānāśu hṝnti vai //
1.37.d:
अन्यश्रेयोविनाशार्थं येर्ऽचयन्ति जनार्दनम् ।
सा पूजैव महाभाग पूजकानाशु हॄन्ति वै ॥
1.37.m: Those who worship Janārdana for the sake of destroying another’s welfare, / that very worship, O fortunate one, swiftly slays the worshippers.

1.37.s:
haripūjākaro yastu yadi pāpaṃ samācaret /
tameva viṣmudveṣṭāraṃ prāhustattvārtthakovidāḥ //
1.37.d:
हरिपूजाकरो यस्तु यदि पापं समाचरेत् ।
तमेव विष्मुद्वेष्टारं प्राहुस्तत्त्वार्त्थकोविदाः ॥
1.37.m: If someone who performs the worship of Hari should commit sin, / the knowers of the truth proclaim him to be an actual hater of Viṣṇu.

1.37.s:
ye viṣṇuniratāḥ saṃti lokānugrahatatparāḥ /
dharmakāryaratāḥ śaśvadviṣṇurupāstu te matāḥ //
1.37.d:
ये विष्णुनिरताः संति लोकानुग्रहतत्पराः ।
धर्मकार्यरताः शश्वद्विष्णुरुपास्तु ते मताः ॥
1.37.m: Those who are devoted to Viṣṇu, intent upon doing grace to the world, / constantly engaged in virtuous deeds—they are considered forms of Viṣṇu Himself.

1.37.s:
koṭijanmārdajitaiḥ puṇyairviṣṇubhaktiḥ prajāyate /
dṛḍhabhaktimatāṃ viṣṇau pāpabuddhiḥ kathaṃ bhavet //
1.37.d:
कोटिजन्मार्दजितैः पुण्यैर्विष्णुभक्तिः प्रजायते ।
दृढभक्तिमतां विष्णौ पापबुद्धिः कथं भवेत् ॥
1.37.m: Devotion to Viṣṇu arises from merit accumulated over ten million births; / how could a sinful intention arise in those who have firm devotion to Viṣṇu?

1.37.s:
janmakoṭyarjitaṃ pāpaṃ viṣṇupūjāratātmanām /
kṣayaṃ yāti kṣaṇādeva teṣāṃ syātpāpadhīḥ katham //
1.37.d:
जन्मकोट्यर्जितं पापं विष्णुपूजारतात्मनाम् ।
क्षयं याति क्षणादेव तेषां स्यात्पापधीः कथम् ॥
1.37.m: Sin accumulated over ten million births of those whose souls are devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu / reaches destruction in an instant; how could there be a sinful intellect in them?

1.37.s:
viṣṇubhaktivihīnā ye caṇḍālāḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
caṇḍālā api vai śreṣṭhā haribhaktiparāyaṇāḥ //
1.37.d:
विष्णुभक्तिविहीना ये चण्डालाः परिकीर्तिताः ।
चण्डाला अपि वै श्रेष्ठा हरिभक्तिपरायणाः ॥
1.37.m: Those who are devoid of devotion to Viṣṇu are declared to be outcasts; / even outcasts are the best if they are dedicated to devotion to Hari.

1.37.s:
narāṇāṃ viṣayāndhānāṃ sarvaduḥkhavināśinī /
hariseveti vikhyātā bhuktimuktipradāyinī //
1.37.d:
नराणां विषयान्धानां सर्वदुःखविनाशिनी ।
हरिसेवेति विख्याता भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायिनी ॥
1.37.m: For men who are blind to sense objects, the renowned service to Hari / destroys all sorrow and bestows enjoyment and liberation.

1.37.s:
saṃgātsnehādbhayāllobhādajñānādvāpi yo naraḥ /
viṣṇorupāsanaṃ kuryātso 'kṣayaṃ sukhamaśnute //
1.37.d:
संगात्स्नेहाद्भयाल्लोभादज्ञानाद्वापि यो नरः ।
विष्णोरुपासनं कुर्यात्सो ऽक्षयं सुखमश्नुते ॥
1.37.m: Whatever person worships Viṣṇu out of company, affection, fear, greed, / or even ignorance, he attains imperishable happiness.

1.37.s:
haripādodakaṃ yastu kaṇamātraṃ pibedapi /
sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu viṣṇoḥ priyataro bhavet //
1.37.d:
हरिपादोदकं यस्तु कणमात्रं पिबेदपि ।
स स्नातः सर्वतीर्थेषु विष्णोः प्रियतरो भवेत् ॥
1.37.m: He who drinks even a single drop of Hari’s foot-water, / has bathed in all the sacred fords and becomes most dear to Viṣṇu.

1.37.s:
akālamṛtyuśamanaṃ sarvavyādhivināśanam /
sarvaduḥkhopaśamanaṃ haripododaka smṛtam //
1.37.d:
अकालमृत्युशमनं सर्वव्याधिविनाशनम् ।
सर्वदुःखोपशमनं हरिपोदोदक स्मृतम् ॥
1.37.m: The water of Hari's feet is recorded as / pacifying untimely death, destroying all diseases, and quelling all sorrow.

1.37.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ paraṃ dhāma jyotiṣāṃ jyotiruttamam /
ye prapannā mahātmānasteṣāṃ muktirhi śāśvatī //
1.37.d:
नारायणं परं धाम ज्योतिषां ज्योतिरुत्तमम् ।
ये प्रपन्ना महात्मानस्तेषां मुक्तिर्हि शाश्वती ॥
1.37.m: Nārāyaṇa is the supreme abode, the ultimate light of lights; / the great souls who take refuge in Him indeed attain eternal liberation.

1.37.s:
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam /
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
1.37.d:
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
पठतां शृण्वतां चैव सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
1.37.m: Here, indeed, they recount this ancient historical narrative / that destroys all sins for those who recite and hear it.

1.37.s:
āsītpurā kṛtayuge guliko nāma lubdhakaḥ /
paradāraparadravyaharaṇe satatodyataḥ //
1.37.d:
आसीत्पुरा कृतयुगे गुलिको नाम लुब्धकः ।
परदारपरद्रव्यहरणे सततोद्यतः ॥
1.37.m: Formerly, in the Kṛta age, there was a hunter named Gulika, / constantly intent on stealing others' wives and others' wealth.

1.37.s:
paranindāparo nityaṃ jantūpadravakṛttathā /
hatavānbrāhmaṇān gāśca śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ //
1.37.d:
परनिन्दापरो नित्यं जन्तूपद्रवकृत्तथा ।
हतवान्ब्राह्मणान् गाश्च शतशो ऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
1.37.m: Constantly bent on slandering others, and afflicting living beings, / he killed hundreds and thousands of brahmins and cows.

1.37.s:
devasvaharaṇe nityaṃ parasvaharaṇe tathā /
udyuktaḥ sarvadā vipra kīnāśānāmadhīśvaraḥ //
1.37.d:
देवस्वहरणे नित्यं परस्वहरणे तथा ।
उद्युक्तः सर्वदा विप्र कीनाशानामधीश्वरः ॥
1.37.m: Always engaged in taking the property of deities and likewise taking the property of others, / O brahmin, he was always a master of villains.

1.37.s:
tena pāpānyanekāni kṛtāni sumahānti ca /
na teṣāṃ śakyate vaktuṃ saṃkhyā vatsarakoṭibhiḥ //
1.37.d:
तेन पापान्यनेकानि कृतानि सुमहान्ति च ।
न तेषां शक्यते वक्तुं संख्या वत्सरकोटिभिः ॥
1.37.m: Countless and very great sins were committed by him; / their number cannot be told even in tens of millions of years.

1.37.s:
sa kadā cinmahāpāpo jatṛnāmantakopamaḥ /
sauvīrarājño nagaraṃ sarvaiśvaryasamanvitam //
1.37.d:
स कदा चिन्महापापो जतृनामन्तकोपमः ।
सौवीरराज्ञो नगरं सर्वैश्वर्यसमन्वितम् ॥
1.37.m: Once, that great sinner, who was like the god of death to living beings, / [went to] the city of the king of Sauvīra, endowed with all opulence,

1.37.s:
yoṣiddhirbhūṣitārbhiśca sarobhinirmalodakaiḥ /
alaṅkṛtaṃ vipaṇibhiryayo devapuropamam //
1.37.d:
योषिद्धिर्भूषितार्भिश्च सरोभिनिर्मलोदकैः ।
अलङ्कृतं विपणिभिर्ययो देवपुरोपमम् ॥
1.37.m: adorned with women and lakes of clear water, / and decorated with market-streets, resembling the city of the gods.

1.37.s:
tasyopavanamadhyasthaṃ ramyaṃ keśavamandiram /
chaditaṃ hemakalaśairdṛṣṭvā vyādho mudaṃ yayau //
1.37.d:
तस्योपवनमध्यस्थं रम्यं केशवमन्दिरम् ।
छदितं हेमकलशैर्दृष्ट्वा व्याधो मुदं ययौ ॥
1.37.m: Seeing a delightful temple of Keśava situated in the midst of its park, / covered with golden water-pitchers, the hunter felt great joy.

1.37.s:
harāmyatra suvarṇāni bahūnīti viniścitam /
jagāmābhyantaraṃ tasya kīnāśaścauryalolupaḥ //
1.37.d:
हराम्यत्र सुवर्णानि बहूनीति विनिश्चितम् ।
जगामाभ्यन्तरं तस्य कीनाशश्चौर्यलोलुपः ॥
1.37.m: Firmly resolving, “I will steal many gold pieces here,” / the thief, greedy for theft, went inside it.

1.37.s:
tatrāpaśyaddvijavaraṃ śāntaṃ tattvārthakovidam /
paricaryāparaṃ viṣṇoruttaṅkaṃ tapasāṃ nidhim //
1.37.d:
तत्रापश्यद्द्विजवरं शान्तं तत्त्वार्थकोविदम् ।
परिचर्यापरं विष्णोरुत्तङ्कं तपसां निधिम् ॥
1.37.m: There he saw the best of brahmins, peaceful, knowing the truth of reality, / devoted to the service of Viṣṇu—Uttaṅka, a treasure of austerities,

1.37.s:
ekākinaṃ dayāsuṃ ca nispṛhaṃ dhyānalolupam /
cauryāntarāyakartāraṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā lubdhako mune //
1.37.d:
एकाकिनं दयासुं च निस्पृहं ध्यानलोलुपम् ।
चौर्यान्तरायकर्तारं तं दृष्ट्वा लुब्धको मुने ॥
1.37.m: solitary, compassionate, devoid of desires, eager for meditation. / Seeing him, who was an obstacle to his theft, O sage,

1.37.s:
dravyajātaṃ tu devasya hartukāmo 'tisāhasī /
uttaṅkaṃ hṝntumārebhe vidhṛtāsirmadoddhataḥ //
1.37.d:
द्रव्यजातं तु देवस्य हर्तुकामो ऽतिसाहसी ।
उत्तङ्कं हॄन्तुमारेभे विधृतासिर्मदोद्धतः ॥
1.37.m: desiring to steal the collection of wealth of the deity, the extremely reckless one / began to slay Uttaṅka, raising his sword, arrogant with pride.

1.37.s:
pādenākramya tadvakṣo jaṭāḥ saṃgṛhya pāṇinā /
hṝntuṃ kṛtamatiṃ vyādhamuttaṅkaḥ prekṣya cābravīt //
1.37.d:
पादेनाक्रम्य तद्वक्षो जटाः संगृह्य पाणिना ।
हॄन्तुं कृतमतिं व्याधमुत्तङ्कः प्रेक्ष्य चाब्रवीत् ॥
1.37.m: Pressing his chest with his foot and seizing his matted locks with his hand, / seeing the hunter resolved to kill him, Uttaṅka spoke:

1.37.s:
uttaṅka uvāca
bho bho sādho vṛthā māṃ tvaṃ haniṣyasi nirāgasam /
mayā kimaparāddhaṃ te tadvadasva mahāmatte //
1.37.d:
उत्तङ्क उवाच
भो भो साधो वृथा मां त्वं हनिष्यसि निरागसम् ।
मया किमपराद्धं ते तद्वदस्व महामत्ते ॥
1.37.m: Uttaṅka said: / “O good sir, in vain will you slay me, innocent as I am. / What wrong have I done to you? Tell me that, O very intelligent one!

1.37.s:
kṛtāparādhināṃ loke śaktāḥ śikṣāṃ prakurvate /
nahi saumya vṛthā ghnanti sajjanā api pāpinaḥ //
1.37.d:
कृतापराधिनां लोके शक्ताः शिक्षां प्रकुर्वते ।
नहि सौम्य वृथा घ्नन्ति सज्जना अपि पापिनः ॥
1.37.m: In this world, capable men mete out punishment to wrongdoers; / virtuous men do not kill even sinners in vain, O gentle one.

1.37.s:
virodhiṣvapi mūrkheṣu nirīkṣyāvasthitān guṇān /
virodhaṃ nahi kurvanti sajjanāḥ śāntacetasaḥ //
1.37.d:
विरोधिष्वपि मूर्खेषु निरीक्ष्यावस्थितान् गुणान् ।
विरोधं नहि कुर्वन्ति सज्जनाः शान्तचेतसः ॥
1.37.m: Even among foolish adversaries, having perceived their existing virtues, / peaceful-minded virtuous men do not practice hostility.

1.37.s:
bahudhā bodhyamāno 'pi yo naraḥ kṣamayānvitaḥ /
tamuttamaṃ naraṃ prāhurviṣṇoḥ priyataraṃ sadā //
1.37.d:
बहुधा बोध्यमानो ऽपि यो नरः क्षमयान्वितः ।
तमुत्तमं नरं प्राहुर्विष्णोः प्रियतरं सदा ॥
1.37.m: The man who is endowed with patience, even though provoked in many ways, / him they declare the best of men, always most dear to Viṣṇu.

1.37.s:
sujano na yāti vairaṃ parahitabuddhirvanāśakāle 'pi /
chede 'pi candanataruḥ surabhayati mukhaṃ kuṭhārasya //
1.37.d:
सुजनो न याति वैरं परहितबुद्धिर्वनाशकाले ऽपि ।
छेदे ऽपि चन्दनतरुः सुरभयति मुखं कुठारस्य ॥
1.37.m: A virtuous person whose mind is intent on the welfare of others does not foster enmity even at the time of death; / even when being cut, the sandalwood tree perfumes the edge of the axe.

1.37.s:
aho vidhiḥ subalavānbā dhate bahudhā janān /
sarvasaṃgavihīno 'pi bādhyate hi durātmanā //
1.37.d:
अहो विधिः सुबलवान्बा धते बहुधा जनान् ।
सर्वसंगविहीनो ऽपि बाध्यते हि दुरात्मना ॥
1.37.m: Alas, destiny is very powerful and afflicts people in many ways; / even one devoid of all attachment is indeed tormented by an evil-minded person.

1.37.s:
aho niṣkāraṇaṃ loke bādhante bahudhā janān /
sarvasaṃgavihīno 'pi bādhyate piśunairjanaiḥ /
tatrāpi sādhūnbādhante na samānānkadācana //
1.37.d:
अहो निष्कारणं लोके बाधन्ते बहुधा जनान् ।
सर्वसंगविहीनो ऽपि बाध्यते पिशुनैर्जनैः ।
तत्रापि साधून्बाधन्ते न समानान्कदाचन ॥
1.37.m: Alas, in this world they afflict people in many ways without cause; / even one devoid of all attachment is afflicted by slanderous men; / even there, they torment the virtuous, never their equals.

1.37.s:
mṛgamīnasajjanānāṃ tṛṇajalasaṃtoṣavihitavṛttānām /
lubdhakadhīvarapiśunā niṣkāraṇavairiṇo jagati //
1.37.d:
मृगमीनसज्जनानां तृणजलसंतोषविहितवृत्तानाम् ।
लुब्धकधीवरपिशुना निष्कारणवैरिणो जगति ॥
1.37.m: For the deer, the fish, and the virtuous, who subsist contentedly on grass, water, and contentment, / the hunter, the fisherman, and the slanderer are unprovoked enemies in this world.

1.37.s:
aho balavatī māyā mohayatyakhilaṃ jagat /
putramitrakalatrārthaṃ sarvaṃ duḥkhena yojayet //
1.37.d:
अहो बलवती माया मोहयत्यखिलं जगत् ।
पुत्रमित्रकलत्रार्थं सर्वं दुःखेन योजयेत् ॥
1.37.m: Alas, powerful illusion bewitches the entire universe; / for the sake of son, friend, and wife, it yokes everything to sorrow.

1.37.s:
paradravyāpahāreṇa kalatraṃ poṣitaṃ tvayā /
ante tatsarvamutsṛjya eka eva prayati vai //
1.37.d:
परद्रव्यापहारेण कलत्रं पोषितं त्वया ।
अन्ते तत्सर्वमुत्सृज्य एक एव प्रयति वै ॥
1.37.m: By stealing others' wealth, a wife was nourished by you; / in the end, having abandoned all that, one goes forth truly alone.

1.37.s:
mama mātā mama pitā mama bhāryā mamātmajāḥ /
mamedamiti jantūnāṃ mamatā bādhate vṛthā //
1.37.d:
मम माता मम पिता मम भार्या ममात्मजाः ।
ममेदमिति जन्तूनां ममता बाधते वृथा ॥
1.37.m: ‘My mother, my father, my wife, my sons, / this is mine’—thus possessiveness torments creatures in vain.

1.37.s:
yāvadarjayati dravyaṃ bāndhavāstāvadeva hi /
dharmādharmauṃ sahaivāstāmihāmutra na cāparaḥ //
1.37.d:
यावदर्जयति द्रव्यं बान्धवास्तावदेव हि ।
धर्माधर्मौं सहैवास्तामिहामुत्र न चापरः ॥
1.37.m: Only as long as one earns wealth do kinsmen exist; / righteousness and unrighteousness alone stay together here and in the hereafter, and nothing else.

1.37.s:
dharmādharmārjitairdravyaiḥ poṣitā yena ye narāḥ /
mṛtamagnimukhe hutvā ghṛtānnaṃ bhuñjate hi te //
1.37.d:
धर्माधर्मार्जितैर्द्रव्यैः पोषिता येन ये नराः ।
मृतमग्निमुखे हुत्वा घृतान्नं भुञ्जते हि ते ॥
1.37.m: The people who were nourished by someone with wealth acquired by righteousness or unrighteousness / offer him into the mouth of the fire when dead, and feast on food cooked with ghee.

1.37.s:
gacchantaṃ paralokaṃ ca naraṃ tu hyanutiṣṭataḥ /
dharmādharmauṃ na ca dhanaṃ na putrā na ca bāndhavāḥ //
1.37.d:
गच्छन्तं परलोकं च नरं तु ह्यनुतिष्टतः ।
धर्माधर्मौं न च धनं न पुत्रा न च बान्धवाः ॥
1.37.m: And as a man departs for the other world, / only righteousness and unrighteousness follow him—neither wealth, nor sons, nor kinsmen.

1.37.s:
kāmaḥ samṛddhimāyāti narāṇāṃ pāpakarmiṇām /
kāmaḥ saṃkṣayamāyāti narāṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām //
1.37.d:
कामः समृद्धिमायाति नराणां पापकर्मिणाम् ।
कामः संक्षयमायाति नराणां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥
1.37.m: Desire increases in men of sinful actions; / desire dwindles away in men of meritorious actions.

1.37.s: vṛthaiva vyākulā lokā dhanādānāṃ sadārjane //
1.37.d: वृथैव व्याकुला लोका धनादानां सदार्जने ॥
1.37.m: In vain indeed are people distressed constantly in the acquisition of wealth.

1.37.s:
yadbhāvi tadbhavatyeva yadabhāvyaṃ na tadbhavet /
iti niścitabuddhīnāṃ na cintā bādhate kvacit //
1.37.d:
यद्भावि तद्भवत्येव यदभाव्यं न तद्भवेत् ।
इति निश्चितबुद्धीनां न चिन्ता बाधते क्वचित् ॥
1.37.m: What is to be, certainly happens; what is not to be, does not happen; / for those of such resolved intellect, anxiety never causes distress anywhere.

1.37.s:
rdavādhīnamidaṃ sarvaṃ jagatsthāvarajaṅgamam /
tasmājjanma ca mṛtyuṃ ca daivaṃ jānāti nāparaḥ //
1.37.d:
र्दवाधीनमिदं सर्वं जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् ।
तस्माज्जन्म च मृत्युं च दैवं जानाति नापरः ॥
1.37.m: All this world, mobile and immobile, is under the control of fate; / therefore, fate alone knows birth and death, and no one else.”

1.37.s:
yatra kutra sthitasyāpi yadbhāvyaṃ tadbhaved dhruvam /
lokastu tatra vijñāya vṛthāyāsaṃ karoti hi //
1.37.d:
यत्र कुत्र स्थितस्यापि यद्भाव्यं तद्भवेद् ध्रुवम् ।
लोकस्तु तत्र विज्ञाय वृथायासं करोति हि ॥
1.37.m: "Wherever one is situated, that which is destined to happen will surely happen. / Yet worldly people, understanding that, indeed make effort in vain.

1.37.s:
aho duḥkhaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ mamatākulacetasām /
mahāpāpāni kṛtvāpi parānpuṣyānti yatnataḥ //
1.37.d:
अहो दुःखं मनुष्याणां ममताकुलचेतसाम् ।
महापापानि कृत्वापि परान्पुष्यान्ति यत्नतः ॥
1.37.m: Alas, the misery of humans whose minds are confounded by possessiveness! / Even having committed great sins, they diligently nourish others.

1.37.s:
arjitaṃ ca dhanaṃ sarvaṃ bhuñjate bāndhavāḥ sadā /
svayamekatamo mūḍhastatpāpaphalamaśnute //
1.37.d:
अर्जितं च धनं सर्वं भुञ्जते बान्धवाः सदा ।
स्वयमेकतमो मूढस्तत्पापफलमश्नुते ॥
1.37.m: Relatives always enjoy all the accumulated wealth, / while that solitary fool alone experiences the fruit of that sin."

1.37.s:
iti bravāṇaṃ tamṛṣiṃ vimucya bhayavihvalaḥ /
gulikaḥ prāñjaliḥ prāha kṣamasveti punaḥ punaḥ //
1.37.d:
इति ब्रवाणं तमृषिं विमुच्य भयविह्वलः ।
गुलिकः प्राञ्जलिः प्राह क्षमस्वेति पुनः पुनः ॥
1.37.m: As the sage was speaking thus, Gulika, agitated by fear, released him, / and with folded hands said repeatedly, "Forgive me!"

1.37.s:
satsaṃgasya prabhāveṇa harisannidhimātrataḥ /
gatapāpo lubagdakaśca hyanutāpīdamabravīt //
1.37.d:
सत्संगस्य प्रभावेण हरिसन्निधिमात्रतः ।
गतपापो लुबग्दकश्च ह्यनुतापीदमब्रवीत् ॥
1.37.m: By the power of the company of the virtuous, merely through the presence of Hari's [devotee], / the hunter, his sins gone and feeling remorse, spoke thus:

1.37.s:
mayā kṛtā ni pāpāni mahānti subahūni ca /
tāni sarvāṇi naṣṭāni viprendra tava darśanāt //
1.37.d:
मया कृता नि पापानि महान्ति सुबहूनि च ।
तानि सर्वाणि नष्टानि विप्रेन्द्र तव दर्शनात् ॥
1.37.m: "Great and very numerous sins have been committed by me; / they have all been destroyed, O best of brahmins, by the sight of you.

1.37.s:
aho 'haṃ pāpadhīrnityaṃ mahāpāpamupācaram /
kathaṃ me niṣkṛtir bhūyo yāmi kaṃ śaraṇaṃ vibhoḥ //
1.37.d:
अहो ऽहं पापधीर्नित्यं महापापमुपाचरम् ।
कथं मे निष्कृतिर् भूयो यामि कं शरणं विभोः ॥
1.37.m: Alas, I of sinful intellect have constantly committed great sin! / How will my atonement be accomplished again? To whose refuge among the lord's [servants] do I go?

1.37.s:
pūrvajanmārjitaiḥ pāpairlubdhakatvamavāptavān /
atrāpi pāpajālāni kṛtvā kāṃ gatimāpnuyām //
1.37.d:
पूर्वजन्मार्जितैः पापैर्लुब्धकत्वमवाप्तवान् ।
अत्रापि पापजालानि कृत्वा कां गतिमाप्नुयाम् ॥
1.37.m: By the sins accumulated in previous lives, I attained the state of a hunter. / Having made a web of sins here too, what destination will I attain?

1.37.s:
aho mamāyuḥ kṣayameti śīghraṃ pāpānyanekāni samarjjitāni /
prātikriyā naiva kṛtā mayaiṣāṃ gatiśca kā syānmamajanma kiṃ vā //
1.37.d:
अहो ममायुः क्षयमेति शीघ्रं पापान्यनेकानि समर्ज्जितानि ।
प्रातिक्रिया नैव कृता मयैषां गतिश्च का स्यान्ममजन्म किं वा ॥
1.37.m: Alas, my life quickly comes to an end; many sins have been accumulated, / and no counter-action has been taken by me for these! What will my destination be, or what my rebirth?

1.37.s:
aho vidhiḥ pāpaśatā kulaṃ māṃ kiṃ sṛṣṭavānpāpataraṃ ca śaśvat /
kathaṃ ca yatpāpaphalaṃ hi bhokṣye kiyatsu janmasvahamugrakarmā //
1.37.d:
अहो विधिः पापशता कुलं मां किं सृष्टवान्पापतरं च शश्वत् ।
कथं च यत्पापफलं हि भोक्ष्ये कियत्सु जन्मस्वहमुग्रकर्मा ॥
1.37.m: Alas, why did the Creator make me afflicted with hundreds of sins and ever more sinful? / And how, in how many births, will I, of terrible deeds, indeed experience the fruit of that sin?"

1.37.s:
evaṃ vinindannātmānamātmanā lubdhakastadā /
antastāpāgnisaṃtaptaḥ sadyaḥ pañcatvamāgataḥ //
1.37.d:
एवं विनिन्दन्नात्मानमात्मना लुब्धकस्तदा ।
अन्तस्तापाग्निसंतप्तः सद्यः पञ्चत्वमागतः ॥
1.37.m: Thus reproaching himself by himself at that time, / scorched by the fire of inner torment, the hunter instantly met his death.

1.37.s:
uttaṅkaḥ patitaṃ prekṣya lubagdhakaṃ taṃ dayāparaḥ /
viṣṇupādodakenaivamabhyaṣiñcanmahāmatiḥ //
1.37.d:
उत्तङ्कः पतितं प्रेक्ष्य लुबग्धकं तं दयापरः ।
विष्णुपादोदकेनैवमभ्यषिञ्चन्महामतिः ॥
1.37.m: Seeing that hunter fallen, compassionate Uttaṅka, / highly intelligent, sprinkled him with the water from Viṣṇu's feet.

1.37.s:
haripādodakasparśāllubdhako gatakalmaṣaḥ /
divyaṃ vimānamāruhya munimetadathābravīt //
1.37.d:
हरिपादोदकस्पर्शाल्लुब्धको गतकल्मषः ।
दिव्यं विमानमारुह्य मुनिमेतदथाब्रवीत् ॥
1.37.m: From the touch of the water from Hari's feet, the hunter, freed from taint, / ascended a celestial chariot and then said this to the sage:

1.37.s:
gulika uvāca
uttaṅka muniśārdūla gurustvaṃ mama suvrata /
vimuktastvatprasādena mahāpātakakañcukāt //
1.37.d:
गुलिक उवाच
उत्तङ्क मुनिशार्दूल गुरुस्त्वं मम सुव्रत ।
विमुक्तस्त्वत्प्रसादेन महापातककञ्चुकात् ॥
1.37.m: Gulika said: / "Uttaṅka, tiger among sages, you are my guru, O one of good vows! / By your grace, I am released from the slough of mortal sin.

1.37.s:
gatastvadupadeśānme saṃtāpo munipuṅgava /
tathaiva sarvapāpāni vinaṣṭānyativegataḥ //
1.37.d:
गतस्त्वदुपदेशान्मे संतापो मुनिपुङ्गव ।
तथैव सर्वपापानि विनष्टान्यतिवेगतः ॥
1.37.m: From your instruction, O bull among sages, my torment has vanished; / likewise, all my sins have perished with great speed.

1.37.s:
haripādodakaṃ yasmānmayi tvaṃ siktavānmune /
prāpito 'smi tvayā tasmāttadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam //
1.37.d:
हरिपादोदकं यस्मान्मयि त्वं सिक्तवान्मुने ।
प्रापितो ऽस्मि त्वया तस्मात्तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
1.37.m: Because you sprinkled the water from Hari's feet upon me, O sage, / I have therefore been brought by you to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

1.37.s:
tvayāhaṃ tārito vipra pāpādasmāccharīrataḥ /
tasmānnato 'smi te vidvanmatkṛtaṃ tatkṣamasva ca //
1.37.d:
त्वयाहं तारितो विप्र पापादस्माच्छरीरतः ।
तस्मान्नतो ऽस्मि ते विद्वन्मत्कृतं तत्क्षमस्व च ॥
1.37.m: By you I have been delivered, O brahmin, from this sinful body; / therefore, I bow to you, O wise one, and forgive what was done by me!"

1.37.s:
ityuktvā devakusumairmuniśreṣṭhaṃ samākiram /
pradakṣiṇātrayaṃ kṛtvā namaskāraṃ cakāra saḥ //
1.37.d:
इत्युक्त्वा देवकुसुमैर्मुनिश्रेष्ठं समाकिरम् ।
प्रदक्षिणात्रयं कृत्वा नमस्कारं चकार सः ॥
1.37.m: Having spoken thus, he strewed the best of sages with divine flowers, / performed three circumambulations, and bowed down.

1.37.s:
tato vimānamāruhya sarvakāmasamanvitam /
apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇaḥ prapede harimandiram //
1.37.d:
ततो विमानमारुह्य सर्वकामसमन्वितम् ।
अप्सरोगणसंकीर्णः प्रपेदे हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
1.37.m: Then, having ascended the chariot endowed with all desires / and crowded with hosts of Apsarases, he went to the temple of Hari.

1.37.s:
etaddṛṣṭvā vismito 'sau hyuttaṅkastapasāṃnidhiḥ /
śirasyañjalimādhāya tuṣṭāva kamalāpatim //
1.37.d:
एतद्दृष्ट्वा विस्मितो ऽसौ ह्युत्तङ्कस्तपसांनिधिः ।
शिरस्यञ्जलिमाधाय तुष्टाव कमलापतिम् ॥
1.37.m: Having seen this, that Uttaṅka, a treasure-house of austerities, was astonished; / placing his folded hands upon his head, he praised the Lord of Kamalā.

1.37.s:
tena stuto mahāviṣṇurdattavānvaramattamam /
vareṇa tenoktaṅko 'pi prapede paramaṃ padam //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge viṣṇumāhātmye saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.37.d:
तेन स्तुतो महाविष्णुर्दत्तवान्वरमत्तमम् ।
वरेण तेनोक्तङ्को ऽपि प्रपेदे परमं पदम् ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे विष्णुमाहात्म्ये सप्तत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.37.m:
Praised by him, Mahāviṣṇu granted an excellent boon; / and by that boon, Uttaṅka also attained the supreme abode.

Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, on the eulogy of the greatness of Viṣṇu, in the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.38.s:
nārada uvāca
kintatstotraṃ mahābhāga kathaṃ tuṣṭo janārdanaḥ /
uktaṅkaḥ puṇyapuruṣaḥ kīdṛśaṃ labdhavānvaram //
1.38.d:
नारद उवाच
किन्तत्स्तोत्रं महाभाग कथं तुष्टो जनार्दनः ।
उक्तङ्कः पुण्यपुरुषः कीदृशं लब्धवान्वरम् ॥
1.38.m: Nārada said: / "What was that praise, O blessed one? How was Janārdana pleased? / What kind of boon did the meritorious person Uttaṅka obtain?"

1.38.s:
sanaka uvāca
uttaṅkastu tadā vipro haridhyānaparāyaṇaḥ /
pādodakasya māhātmyaṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭāva bhaktitaḥ //
1.38.d:
सनक उवाच
उत्तङ्कस्तु तदा विप्रो हरिध्यानपरायणः ।
पादोदकस्य माहात्म्यं दृष्ट्वा तुष्टाव भक्तितः ॥
1.38.m: Sanaka said: / "Then the brahmin Uttaṅka, devoted to meditation on Hari, / having seen the greatness of the foot-water, praised [him] with devotion."

1.38.s:
uttaṅka uvāca
nato 'smi nārāyaṇamādidevaṃ jagannivāsaṃ jagadekabandhum /
cakrābjaśārṅgīsidharaṃ mahāntaṃ smṛtārtinighnaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye //
1.38.d:
उत्तङ्क उवाच
नतो ऽस्मि नारायणमादिदेवं जगन्निवासं जगदेकबन्धुम् ।
चक्राब्जशार्ङ्गीसिधरं महान्तं स्मृतार्तिनिघ्नं शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
1.38.m: Uttaṅka said: / "I bow to Nārāyaṇa, the primal deity, the abode of the universe, the sole friend of the universe; / holding the discus, lotus, Śārṅga bow, and sword, the great one who destroys the suffering of those who remember him, I go to him for refuge.

1.38.s:
yannibhijābja prabhavo vidhātā sṛjatyamuṃ lokasamuñcayaṃ ca /
yatkrodhajo hṝnti jagañca rudrastamādidevaṃ praṇato 'smi viṣṇum //
1.38.d:
यन्निभिजाब्ज प्रभवो विधाता सृजत्यमुं लोकसमुञ्चयं च ।
यत्क्रोधजो हॄन्ति जगञ्च रुद्रस्तमादिदेवं प्रणतो ऽस्मि विष्णुम् ॥
1.38.m: From whose navel-lotus the Creator arose and creates this collection of worlds, / and born from whose anger Rudra destroys the universe—to that primal deity Viṣṇu I bow.

1.38.s:
padmāpatiṃ padmadalāyatākṣaṃ vicitravīryaṃ nikhilaikahetum /
vedāntavedyaṃ pukuṣaṃ purāṇaṃ taijonidhiṃ viṣṇumahaṃ prapannaḥ //
1.38.d:
पद्मापतिं पद्मदलायताक्षं विचित्रवीर्यं निखिलैकहेतुम् ।
वेदान्तवेद्यं पुकुषं पुराणं तैजोनिधिं विष्णुमहं प्रपन्नः ॥
1.38.m: To the Lord of Padmā, whose eyes are long like lotus petals, of wondrous valour, the single cause of all, / knowable through the Vedānta, the ancient Puruṣa, the treasure of splendour, to Viṣṇu I have surrendered.

1.38.s:
ātmākṣaraḥ sarvagato 'cyutākhyo jñānātmako jñānavidāṃ śaraṇyaḥ /
jñānaikavedyo bhagavānanādiḥ prasīdatāṃ vyaṣṭisa praṣṭirupaḥ //
1.38.d:
आत्माक्षरः सर्वगतो ऽच्युताख्यो ज्ञानात्मको ज्ञानविदां शरण्यः ।
ज्ञानैकवेद्यो भगवाननादिः प्रसीदतां व्यष्टिस प्रष्टिरुपः ॥
1.38.m: The imperishable Self, omnipresent, named Acyuta, consisting of knowledge, the refuge of those who know knowledge, / knowable by knowledge alone, the beginningless Lord in the form of individual and cosmic manifestation, may he be pleased.

1.38.s:
anantavīyo guṇajātihīnāṃ guṇātmako jñānavidāṃ varaṣṭaḥ /
nityaḥ prapannārti haraḥ parātmā dayāṃbudhirme varadastu bhaghūyāt //
1.38.d:
अनन्तवीयो गुणजातिहीनां गुणात्मको ज्ञानविदां वरष्टः ।
नित्यः प्रपन्नार्ति हरः परात्मा दयांबुधिर्मे वरदस्तु भघूयात् ॥
1.38.m: Of endless valour, devoid of qualities and genus, consisting of qualities, the highest among those who know knowledge, / eternal, removing the distress of the surrendered, the supreme Self, the ocean of compassion—may he become the granter of boons to me!

1.38.s:
yaḥ sthūlasūkṣmādiviśeṣabhedaurjagadyathāvatsvakṛtaṃ praviṣṭaḥ /
tvameva tatsarvamanantasāraṃ tvattaḥ paraṃ nāsti yataḥ parātman //
1.38.d:
यः स्थूलसूक्ष्मादिविशेषभेदौर्जगद्यथावत्स्वकृतं प्रविष्टः ।
त्वमेव तत्सर्वमनन्तसारं त्वत्तः परं नास्ति यतः परात्मन् ॥
1.38.m: He who, by distinct variations such as gross and subtle, entered the world properly as his own creation—/ you alone are all that, the endless essence, since there is nothing beyond you, O supreme Self.

1.38.s:
agocaraṃ yattava śuddharūraṃ māyāvihīnaṃ guṇajātihīnam /
nirañjanaṃ nirmalamaprameyaṃ paśyanti santaḥ paramārthasaṃjñam //
1.38.d:
अगोचरं यत्तव शुद्धरूरं मायाविहीनं गुणजातिहीनम् ।
निरञ्जनं निर्मलमप्रमेयं पश्यन्ति सन्तः परमार्थसंज्ञम् ॥
1.38.m: Your pure form, beyond the senses, free from māyā, devoid of qualities and genus, / untainted, spotless, immeasurable, designated as the supreme truth, the good perceive.

1.38.s:
ekena hemraiva vibhūṣaṇāni yātāni bhedatvamupādhibhedāt /
tathaiva sarveṣvara eka eva pradṛśyate bhinna ivārivalātmā //
1.38.d:
एकेन हेम्रैव विभूषणानि यातानि भेदत्वमुपाधिभेदात् ।
तथैव सर्वेष्वर एक एव प्रदृश्यते भिन्न इवारिवलात्मा ॥
1.38.m: Just as ornaments made from gold alone attain diversity through difference of conditions, / even so the one Lord of all, the Self of all, appears as if divided.

1.38.s:
yanmāyayā mohitacetasastaṃ paśyanti nātmānamapi prasiddham /
ta eva māyārahitāstadeva pasaayanti sarvātmakamātmarupam //
1.38.d:
यन्मायया मोहितचेतसस्तं पश्यन्ति नात्मानमपि प्रसिद्धम् ।
त एव मायारहितास्तदेव पसअयन्ति सर्वात्मकमात्मरुपम् ॥
1.38.m: Those whose minds are deluded by his māyā do not see him, nor even the well-known Self; / but those very ones, freed from māyā, see that Self whose form is the Self of all.

1.38.s:
vibhuṃ jyotiranaupamyaṃ viṣṇusaṃjñaṃ namāmyaham /
samastametadudbhūtaṃ yato yatra pratiṣṭitam //
1.38.d:
विभुं ज्योतिरनौपम्यं विष्णुसंज्ञं नमाम्यहम् ।
समस्तमेतदुद्भूतं यतो यत्र प्रतिष्टितम् ॥
1.38.m: I bow to the all-pervading light, peerless, bearing the name Viṣṇu, / from whom all this has arisen and in whom it is established.

1.38.s:
yataścaitanyamāyātaṃ yadrūpaṃ tasya vai namaḥ /
aprameyamanādāramādhārādheyarūpakam //
1.38.d:
यतश्चैतन्यमायातं यद्रूपं तस्य वै नमः ।
अप्रमेयमनादारमाधाराधेयरूपकम् ॥
1.38.m: From whom consciousness has come, whose form is that—to him indeed be homage! / The immeasurable, without support, who has the form of both support and supported,

1.38.s:
paramānandacinmātraṃ vāsudevaṃ nato 'smyaham /
hṛdguhānilayaṃ devaṃ yogibhiḥ parisevitam //
1.38.d:
परमानन्दचिन्मात्रं वासुदेवं नतो ऽस्म्यहम् ।
हृद्गुहानिलयं देवं योगिभिः परिसेवितम् ॥
1.38.m: supreme bliss, pure consciousness—to Vāsudeva I bow; / the god who dwells in the cave of the heart, attended upon by yogins.

1.38.s:
yogānāmādibhūtaṃ taṃ namāmi praṇavasthitam /
nādātmakaṃ nādabījaṃ praṇavātmakamavyayam //
1.38.d:
योगानामादिभूतं तं नमामि प्रणवस्थितम् ।
नादात्मकं नादबीजं प्रणवात्मकमव्ययम् ॥
1.38.m: To him who is the beginning of yogas, dwelling in the praṇava, I bow; / consisting of sound, the seed of sound, consisting of the praṇava, imperishable.

1.38.s:
sadbhaghāvaṃ sañcidānandaṃ taṃ vande tigmacakriṇam /
ajaraṃ sākṣiṇaṃ tvasya hyavāṅmanasagocaram //
1.38.d:
सद्भघावं सञ्चिदानन्दं तं वन्दे तिग्मचक्रिणम् ।
अजरं साक्षिणं त्वस्य ह्यवाङ्मनसगोचरम् ॥
1.38.m: I praise him whose nature is being, consciousness, and bliss, bearer of the sharp discus, / unaging, the witness of this [world], beyond the reach of speech and mind.

1.38.s:
nirañjanamanantākhyaṃ viṣṇurupaṃ nato 'smyaham /
indriyāṇi mano buddhiḥ sattvaṃ tejo balaṃ dhṛtiḥ //
1.38.d:
निरञ्जनमनन्ताख्यं विष्णुरुपं नतो ऽस्म्यहम् ।
इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिः सत्त्वं तेजो बलं धृतिः ॥
1.38.m: To the untainted one named Ananta, who is Viṣṇu's form, I bow: / the senses, mind, intellect, sattva, splendour, strength, and resolve."

1.38.s:
vāsudevātmakānyāhuḥ kṣetraṃ kṣetra jñameva ca /
vidyāvidyātmakaṃ prāhuḥ parātparataraṃ tathā //
1.38.d:
वासुदेवात्मकान्याहुः क्षेत्रं क्षेत्र ज्ञमेव च ।
विद्याविद्यात्मकं प्राहुः परात्परतरं तथा ॥
1.38.m: They declare that [all these] consist of Vāsudeva, as do the field and the knower of the field; / and they declare that he consists of knowledge and ignorance, higher than the highest.

1.38.s:
anādinidhanaṃ śāntaṃ sarvadhātāramacyutam /
ye prapannā mahātmānasteṣāṃ muktirhi śāśvatī //
1.38.d:
अनादिनिधनं शान्तं सर्वधातारमच्युतम् ।
ये प्रपन्ना महात्मानस्तेषां मुक्तिर्हि शाश्वती ॥
1.38.m: Those great-souled ones who have taken refuge in Acyuta, the beginningless and endless, tranquil supporter of all, / attain indeed eternal liberation.

1.38.s:
varaṃ vareṇyaṃ varadaṃ purāṇaṃ sanātanaṃ sarvagataṃ samastam /
nato 'smi bhūyo 'pi nato 'smi bhūyo 'pi nato 'smi bhūyaḥ //
1.38.d:
वरं वरेण्यं वरदं पुराणं सनातनं सर्वगतं समस्तम् ।
नतो ऽस्मि भूयो ऽपि नतो ऽस्मि भूयो ऽपि नतो ऽस्मि भूयः ॥
1.38.m: To the excellent, the worthy of choice, the giver of boons, the ancient, eternal, all-pervading, and all-comprising, / I bow again and again; I bow again and again; I bow once more.

1.38.s:
yatpāda toyaṃ bhaghavarogavaidyo yatpādapāṃśurvimalatvasiddhyai /
yannāma duṣkarmanivāraṇāyacaya tamaprameyaṃ puruṣaṃ bhajāmi //
1.38.d:
यत्पाद तोयं भघवरोगवैद्यो यत्पादपांशुर्विमलत्वसिद्ध्यै ।
यन्नाम दुष्कर्मनिवारणायचय तमप्रमेयं पुरुषं भजामि ॥
1.38.m: The water from whose feet is a physician for the disease of worldly existence, the dust from whose feet brings about purity, / whose name dispels evil actions—that immeasurable Puruṣa I worship.

1.38.s:
sadrūpaṃ tamasadrūpaṃ sadasadrūpamavyayam /
tattadvilakṣaṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhācchraṣṭhataraṃ bhaje //
1.38.d:
सद्रूपं तमसद्रूपं सदसद्रूपमव्ययम् ।
तत्तद्विलक्षणं श्रेष्ठं श्रेष्ठाच्छ्रष्ठतरं भजे ॥
1.38.m: His form is being, non-being, and both being and non-being; immutable, / distinct from both, supreme: I worship him who is greater than the greatest.

1.38.s:
nirañjanaṃ nirākāraṃ pūrṇamākāśamadhyagam /
paraṃ ca vidyāvidyābhyāṃ hṛdaṃbujanivāsinam //
1.38.d:
निरञ्जनं निराकारं पूर्णमाकाशमध्यगम् ।
परं च विद्याविद्याभ्यां हृदंबुजनिवासिनम् ॥
1.38.m: Free from stain, formless, complete, abiding in the midst of space, / beyond knowledge and ignorance, dwelling in the lotus of the heart;

1.38.s:
svaprakāśamanirdeṣyaṃ mahatāṃ ca mahattaram /
aṇoraṇīyāṃsamajaṃ sarvopādhivivarjitam //
1.38.d:
स्वप्रकाशमनिर्देष्यं महतां च महत्तरम् ।
अणोरणीयांसमजं सर्वोपाधिविवर्जितम् ॥
1.38.m: Self-luminous, indefinable, greater than the great, / subtler than the subtle, unborn, devoid of all adjuncts;

1.38.s:
yannityaṃ paramānandaṃ paraṃ brahma sanātanam /
viṣṇusaṃjñaṃ jagaddhāma tamasmi śaraṇaṃ gataḥ //
1.38.d:
यन्नित्यं परमानन्दं परं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
विष्णुसंज्ञं जगद्धाम तमस्मि शरणं गतः ॥
1.38.m: That eternal supreme bliss, the eternal Supreme Brahman, / designated as Viṣṇu, the abode of the universe—in him I have taken refuge.

1.38.s:
yaṃ bhajanti kriyāniṣṭāyaṃ paśyanti ca yoginaḥ /
pūjyātpūjyataraṃ śāntaṃ gato 'smi śaraṇaṃ prabhum //
1.38.d:
यं भजन्ति क्रियानिष्टायं पश्यन्ति च योगिनः ।
पूज्यात्पूज्यतरं शान्तं गतो ऽस्मि शरणं प्रभुम् ॥
1.38.m: Whom those devoted to action worship, and whom yogins behold; / to that Lord, more worthy of worship than the venerable, tranquil, I have gone for refuge.

1.38.s:
yaṃ na paśyanti vidvāṃso ya etadvyāvya tiṣṭati /
sarvasmādadhikaṃ nityaṃ nato 'smi vibhumavyayam //
1.38.d:
यं न पश्यन्ति विद्वांसो य एतद्व्याव्य तिष्टति ।
सर्वस्मादधिकं नित्यं नतो ऽस्मि विभुमव्ययम् ॥
1.38.m: Whom the learned do not see, who remains pervading this [entire universe], / higher than all, eternal: I bow to the all-pervading, imperishable Lord.

1.38.s:
antaḥ karaṇasaṃyogājjīva ityucyate ca yaḥ /
avidyākārya rahitaḥ paramātmeti gīyate //
1.38.d:
अन्तः करणसंयोगाज्जीव इत्युच्यते च यः ।
अविद्याकार्य रहितः परमात्मेति गीयते ॥
1.38.m: He who is called the individual self through connection with the inner organ, / free from the effects of ignorance, is sung of as the Supreme Self.

1.38.s:
sarvātmakaṃ sarvahetuṃ sravakarmaphalappadam /
varaṃ vareṇyamajanaṃ praṇato 'smi parātparam //
1.38.d:
सर्वात्मकं सर्वहेतुं स्रवकर्मफलप्पदम् ।
वरं वरेण्यमजनं प्रणतो ऽस्मि परात्परम् ॥
1.38.m: Consisting of all, the cause of all, granter of the fruit of all deeds, / excellent, worthy of choice, unborn: I bow to the higher than the highest.

1.38.s:
sarvajñaṃ sarvagaṃ śāntaṃ sarvāntayā miṇaṃ harim /
jñānātmakaṃ jñānanidhiṃ jñānasaṃsthaṃ vibhuṃ bhaje //
1.38.d:
सर्वज्ञं सर्वगं शान्तं सर्वान्तया मिणं हरिम् ।
ज्ञानात्मकं ज्ञाननिधिं ज्ञानसंस्थं विभुं भजे ॥
1.38.m: Omniscient, all-pervading, tranquil, the inner ruler of all, Hari, / consisting of knowledge, a treasure of knowledge, abiding in knowledge: I worship the all-pervading Lord.

1.38.s:
namāmyahaṃ vedanidhiṃ murāriṃ vedānta vijñānasuniścitārtham /
sūryeduvatprojjvalane tramindraṃ ravagasvarupaṃ vapatisvarūpam //
1.38.d:
नमाम्यहं वेदनिधिं मुरारिं वेदान्त विज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थम् ।
सूर्येदुवत्प्रोज्ज्वलने त्रमिन्द्रं रवगस्वरुपं वपतिस्वरूपम् ॥
1.38.m: I bow to Murāri, the treasure of the Vedas, whose meaning is firmly established by the wisdom of the Vedānta, / whose eyes are ablaze like the sun and moon, Indra, having the nature of the sun, embodied as the universe.

1.38.s:
sarveśvaraṃ sarvagataṃ mahāntaṃ vedātmakaṃ vedavidāṃvariṣṭam /
taṃvāṅmano 'cintyamanantaśaktiṃ jñānaikavedyaṃ puruṣaṃ bhajāmi //
1.38.d:
सर्वेश्वरं सर्वगतं महान्तं वेदात्मकं वेदविदांवरिष्टम् ।
तंवाङ्मनो ऽचिन्त्यमनन्तशक्तिं ज्ञानैकवेद्यं पुरुषं भजामि ॥
1.38.m: Lord of all, all-pervading, the Great One, consisting of the Vedas, foremost among knowers of the Vedas, / unthinkable by speech or mind, of infinite power, knowable through knowledge alone: I worship the Puruṣa.

1.38.s:
indrāgnikālāsurapāśivāyusomeṣamārttaṇḍapurandarādyaiḥ /
yaḥ pāti lokānparipūrṇabhāvastamaprameyaṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye //
1.38.d:
इन्द्राग्निकालासुरपाशिवायुसोमेषमार्त्तण्डपुरन्दराद्यैः ।
यः पाति लोकान्परिपूर्णभावस्तमप्रमेयं शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
1.38.m: He who, having a complete nature, protects the worlds through Indra, Agni, Kāla, Varuṇa, Vāyu, Soma, Īśa, Sūrya, Purandara, and others— / in that immeasurable one I take refuge.

1.38.s:
sahasraśīrṣaṃ ca sahasrapādaṃ sahasrabāhuḥ ca sahasranetram /
samastayajñaiḥ parijuṣṭamādyaṃ nato 'smi tuṣṭipradamugravīryam //
1.38.d:
सहस्रशीर्षं च सहस्रपादं सहस्रबाहुः च सहस्रनेत्रम् ।
समस्तयज्ञैः परिजुष्टमाद्यं नतो ऽस्मि तुष्टिप्रदमुग्रवीर्यम् ॥
1.38.m: Having a thousand heads, a thousand feet, a thousand arms, and a thousand eyes, / worshipped through all sacrifices, the primeval one, granter of satisfaction, of fierce valour: to him I bow.

1.38.s:
kālātmakaṃ kālavibhāgahetuṃ guṇatrayātītamahaṃ guṇajñam /
guṇapriyaṃ kāmadamastasaṃgamatīndriyaṃ viśvabhaghujaṃ vitṛṣṇam //
1.38.d:
कालात्मकं कालविभागहेतुं गुणत्रयातीतमहं गुणज्ञम् ।
गुणप्रियं कामदमस्तसंगमतीन्द्रियं विश्वभघुजं वितृष्णम् ॥
1.38.m: Consisting of time, the cause of the divisions of time, transcending the three guṇas, knower of qualities, / lover of virtues, granter of desires, free of attachment, beyond the senses, enjoyer of the universe, free of thirst;

1.38.s:
nirīhamagryaṃ manasāpyagamyaṃ manomayaṃ cānnamayaṃ nirūḍham /
vijñānabhedaṃ pratipannakalpaṃ na vāṅmayaṃ prāṇamayaṃ bhajāmi //
1.38.d:
निरीहमग्र्यं मनसाप्यगम्यं मनोमयं चान्नमयं निरूढम् ।
विज्ञानभेदं प्रतिपन्नकल्पं न वाङ्मयं प्राणमयं भजामि ॥
1.38.m: Free of desire, the foremost, ungraspable even by the mind, made of mind and firmly rooted as made of food, / possessing distinctions of consciousness, assuming all forms, not made of speech, made of breath: [him] I worship.

1.38.s:
na yasya rūpaṃ na balaprabhāvo na yasya karmāṇi na yatpramāṇam /
jānanti devā kamalodbhavādyastoṣyāmyahaṃ taṃ kathamātmarūpam //
1.38.d:
न यस्य रूपं न बलप्रभावो न यस्य कर्माणि न यत्प्रमाणम् ।
जानन्ति देवा कमलोद्भवाद्यस्तोष्याम्यहं तं कथमात्मरूपम् ॥
1.38.m: Whose form, strength, majesty, deeds, and measure / the gods beginning with the lotus-born [Brahmā] do not know—how shall I praise him whose nature is the Self?

1.38.s:
saṃsārasidhau patitaṃ kadaryaṃ mohākulaṃ kāmaśatena baddham /
akīrtibhājaṃ piśunaṃ kṛtaghnaṃ sadāśuciṃ pāparataṃ pramanyum /
dayāṃbudhe pāhi bhayākulaṃ māṃ punaḥ punastvāṃ śaraṇaṃ prapadye //
1.38.d:
संसारसिधौ पतितं कदर्यं मोहाकुलं कामशतेन बद्धम् ।
अकीर्तिभाजं पिशुनं कृतघ्नं सदाशुचिं पापरतं प्रमन्युम् ।
दयांबुधे पाहि भयाकुलं मां पुनः पुनस्त्वां शरणं प्रपद्ये ॥
1.38.m: Fallen into the ocean of saṃsāra, wretched, bewildered by delusion, bound by hundreds of desires, / bearing ill fame, malicious, ungrateful, ever impure, devoted to sin, enraged— / O ocean of compassion, protect me, bewildered by fear; again and again I take refuge in you!

1.38.s:
iti prasāditastena dayālasuḥ kamalāpatiḥ /
pratyakṣatāmagāttasya bhagavāṃstejasāṃ nidhiḥ //
1.38.d:
इति प्रसादितस्तेन दयालसुः कमलापतिः ।
प्रत्यक्षतामगात्तस्य भगवांस्तेजसां निधिः ॥
1.38.m: Thus propitiated by him, the compassionate Lord of Kamalā, / the Blessed Lord, a treasure of splendours, became visible to him.

1.38.s:
atasī puṣpasaṃkāśaṃ phullapaṅkajalocanan /
kirīṭinaṃ kuṇḍalinaṃ hārakeyūrabhūṣitam //
1.38.d:
अतसी पुष्पसंकाशं फुल्लपङ्कजलोचनन् ।
किरीटिनं कुण्डलिनं हारकेयूरभूषितम् ॥
1.38.m: [Resembling] the flax flower, with eyes like blooming lotuses, / wearing a diadem, adorned with earrings, necklaces, and armlets,

1.38.s:
śrīvatsakaustubhadharaṃ hemayajñopavītinanam /
nāsāvinyastamuktā bhavardhamānatanucchavim //
1.38.d:
श्रीवत्सकौस्तुभधरं हेमयज्ञोपवीतिननम् ।
नासाविन्यस्तमुक्ता भवर्धमानतनुच्छविम् ॥
1.38.m: Bearing the Śrīvatsa and the Kaustubha, wearing a golden sacred thread, / the radiance of his body enhanced by a pearl placed on his nose,

1.38.s:
pītāṃbaradharaṃ devaṃ vanamālāvibhūṣimat /
tulasīkomaladalairarcitāṅghniṃ mahādyutim //
1.38.d:
पीतांबरधरं देवं वनमालाविभूषिमत् ।
तुलसीकोमलदलैरर्चिताङ्घ्निं महाद्युतिम् ॥
1.38.m: Wearing yellow garments, the god adorned with a garland of forest flowers, / his feet worshipped with tender tulasī leaves, possessed of great splendour,

1.38.s:
kiṅkiṇīnūpurā dyaiśca śobhitaṃ garuḍadhvajam /
dṛṣṭvā nānāma viprendro daṇḍavatkṣitimaṇḍale //
1.38.d:
किङ्किणीनूपुरा द्यैश्च शोभितं गरुडध्वजम् ।
दृष्ट्वा नानाम विप्रेन्द्रो दण्डवत्क्षितिमण्डले ॥
1.38.m: Adorned with bells, anklets, and the like, with the emblem of Garuḍa— / seeing him, the foremost of brāhmaṇas fell prostrate like a stick upon the circle of the earth.

1.38.s:
abhyaṣiñcaddhareḥ pādāvuttaṅko harṣavāribhiḥ /
murāre rakṣa rakṣeti vyāharannānyadhīstadā //
1.38.d:
अभ्यषिञ्चद्धरेः पादावुत्तङ्को हर्षवारिभिः ।
मुरारे रक्ष रक्षेति व्याहरन्नान्यधीस्तदा ॥
1.38.m: Uttaṅka bathed Hari's feet with tears of joy, / crying, 'O Murāri, protect me, protect me!' with a single-pointed mind.

1.38.s:
tamutthāpya mahāviṣṇurāliliṅga dayāparaḥ /
varaṃ vṛṇuṣva vatseti provāca munipuṅgavam //
1.38.d:
तमुत्थाप्य महाविष्णुरालिलिङ्ग दयापरः ।
वरं वृणुष्व वत्सेति प्रोवाच मुनिपुङ्गवम् ॥
1.38.m: Lifting him up, Mahāviṣṇu, filled with compassion, embraced him, / and said to that best of sages: 'Choose a boon, my child!'

1.38.s:
asādhyaṃ nāsti kiñcitte prasanne mayi sattama /
itīritaṃ samākarṇya hyuttaṅkaścakrapāṇinā /
punaḥ praṇamya taṃ prāha devadevaṃ janārddanam //
1.38.d:
असाध्यं नास्ति किञ्चित्ते प्रसन्ने मयि सत्तम ।
इतीरितं समाकर्ण्य ह्युत्तङ्कश्चक्रपाणिना ।
पुनः प्रणम्य तं प्राह देवदेवं जनार्द्दनम् ॥
1.38.m: Hearing this spoken by the Discus-Bearer: 'There is nothing unachievable for you when I am pleased, O best of men,' / Uttaṅka bowed once more to that God of gods, Janārdana, and said:

1.38.s:
kiṃ māṃ mohayasīśa tvaṃ kimanyairdeva me varaiḥ /
tvayi bhaktirdṛḍhā me 'stu janmajanmāntareṣvapi //
1.38.d:
किं मां मोहयसीश त्वं किमन्यैर्देव मे वरैः ।
त्वयि भक्तिर्दृढा मे ऽस्तु जन्मजन्मान्तरेष्वपि ॥
1.38.m: 'Why do you bewilder me, O Lord? What use have I for other boons, O God? / May I have steadfast devotion to you, even in birth after birth!

1.38.s: kīṭeṣu pakṣiṣu mṛgeṣu sarīsṛpeṣu rakṣaḥ piśācamanujeṣvapi yatra tatrajajātasya me bhavatu keśava te prasāddāttvayyeva bhaktiracalāvyabhicāraṇī ca //
1.38.d: कीटेषु पक्षिषु मृगेषु सरीसृपेषु रक्षः पिशाचमनुजेष्वपि यत्र तत्रजजातस्य मे भवतु केशव ते प्रसाद्दात्त्वय्येव भक्तिरचलाव्यभिचारणी च ॥
1.38.m: Among insects, birds, beasts, reptiles, rākṣasas, piśācas, or men—wherever I may be born, / O Keśava, by your grace, may I have unswerving and unwavering devotion to you alone!'

1.38.s: evamastviti lokeśaḥ śaṅkhaprāntena saṃspṛśan divyajñānaṃ dadau tasmai yogināmapidurlamabhagham //
1.38.d: एवमस्त्विति लोकेशः शङ्खप्रान्तेन संस्पृशन् दिव्यज्ञानं ददौ तस्मै योगिनामपिदुर्लमभघम् ॥
1.38.m: Saying 'So be it,' the Lord of the world, touching him with the tip of his conch, / gave him divine knowledge, difficult of attainment even for yogins.

1.38.s: puḥ stuvantaṃ viprendraṃ devadevo janārddanaḥ idamāha smitamukho hastaṃ tacchirasi nyasan //
1.38.d: पुः स्तुवन्तं विप्रेन्द्रं देवदेवो जनार्द्दनः इदमाह स्मितमुखो हस्तं तच्छिरसि न्यसन् ॥
1.38.m: To that foremost of brāhmaṇas who praised him again, the God of gods, Janārdana, / with a smiling face, placing his hand upon his head, spoke these words:

1.38.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca ārādhaya kriyāyogairmāṃ sadā dvijasattam /
naranārāyaṇasthānaṃ vraja mokṣaṃ gamiṣyasi //
1.38.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच आराधय क्रियायोगैर्मां सदा द्विजसत्तम् ।
नरनारायणस्थानं व्रज मोक्षं गमिष्यसि ॥
1.38.m: The Blessed Lord said: / 'Worship me constantly through kriyāyoga, O best of the twice-born; / go to the abode of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, and you shall attain liberation.

1.38.s:
tvayā kṛtamidaṃ stotraṃ yaḥ paṭhetsatataṃ naraḥ /
sarvānkāmānavāpyānte mokṣabhāgī bhavettataḥ //
1.38.d:
त्वया कृतमिदं स्तोत्रं यः पठेत्सततं नरः ।
सर्वान्कामानवाप्यान्ते मोक्षभागी भवेत्ततः ॥
1.38.m: The person who continually recites this hymn composed by you / will obtain all desires and thereafter become an enjoyer of liberation.'

1.38.s:
ityuktvā bhādhavo vipraṃ tatraivāntardadhe mune /
naranarāyaṇasthānamuttaṅko 'pi tato yayau //
1.38.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भाधवो विप्रं तत्रैवान्तर्दधे मुने ।
नरनरायणस्थानमुत्तङ्को ऽपि ततो ययौ ॥
1.38.m: Having spoken thus to the brāhmaṇa, O sage, Mādhava disappeared right there; / and Uttaṅka also then departed for the abode of Nara and Nārāyaṇa.

1.38.s:
kasmādbhaktiḥ sadā kāryā devadevasya cakriṇaḥ /
haribhaktiḥ parā proktā sarvakāmapalapradā //
1.38.d:
कस्माद्भक्तिः सदा कार्या देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ।
हरिभक्तिः परा प्रोक्ता सर्वकामपलप्रदा ॥
1.38.m: Therefore, devotion should ever be offered to the Discus-Bearer, the God of gods; / devotion to Hari is declared to be supreme, granting the fruits of all desires.

1.38.s:
utaṅko bhāktibhāvena kriyāyogaparo mune /
pūjayanmādhayavaṃ nityaṃ naranārāyaṇāśrame //
1.38.d:
उतङ्को भाक्तिभावेन क्रियायोगपरो मुने ।
पूजयन्माधयवं नित्यं नरनारायणाश्रमे ॥
1.38.m: Uttaṅka, with a spirit of devotion, intent on kriyāyoga, O sage, / constantly worshipped Mādhava in the hermitage of Nara and Nārāyaṇa;

1.38.s:
jñānavijñānasaṃpannaḥ saṃcchinnadvaitasaṃśayaḥ /
āvāpa duravāpaṃ vai tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam //
1.38.d:
ज्ञानविज्ञानसंपन्नः संच्छिन्नद्वैतसंशयः ।
आवाप दुरवापं वै तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥
1.38.m: Endowed with knowledge and realization, his doubts regarding duality severed, / he truly attained that difficult-to-attain supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

1.38.s:
pūjito namito vāpi saṃsmṛto vāpi mokṣadaḥ /
nārāyaṇo jagannātho bhaktānāṃ mānavarddhanaḥ //
1.38.d:
पूजितो नमितो वापि संस्मृतो वापि मोक्षदः ।
नारायणो जगन्नाथो भक्तानां मानवर्द्धनः ॥
1.38.m: Worshipped, bowed to, or remembered, he grants liberation: / Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the universe, who increases the honour of his devotees.

1.38.s:
tasmānnārāyaṇaṃ devamanantamaparājitam /
ihāmutra sukhaprepsuḥ pūjayedbhaktisaṃyutaḥ //
1.38.d:
तस्मान्नारायणं देवमनन्तमपराजितम् ।
इहामुत्र सुखप्रेप्सुः पूजयेद्भक्तिसंयुतः ॥
1.38.m: Therefore, desiring happiness in this world and the next, one should, endowed with devotion, / worship the god Nārāyaṇa, the infinite, the unconquered.

1.38.s:
yaḥ paṭhedidamākhyānaṃ śṛṇuyādvāsamāhitaḥ /
so 'pi sarvāghanirmuktaḥ prayāti bhavanaṃ hareḥ //
iti śrībṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathamapāde viṣṇumāhātmyaṃ nāmāṣṭatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.38.d:
यः पठेदिदमाख्यानं शृणुयाद्वासमाहितः ।
सो ऽपि सर्वाघनिर्मुक्तः प्रयाति भवनं हरेः ॥
इति श्रीबृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथमपादे विष्णुमाहात्म्यं नामाष्टत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.38.m:
Whoever reads or hears this narrative with a concentrated mind / is also freed from all sins and goes to the abode of Hari.

Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, named 'The Eulogy of Viṣṇu's Greatness', in the first quarter of the first part of the venerable Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.39.s:
sanaka uvāca
bhūyaḥ śṛṇuṣva viprendra māhātmyaṃ parameṣṭinaḥ /
sarvapāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ bhuktimuktipradaṃ nṛṇām //
1.39.d:
सनक उवाच
भूयः शृणुष्व विप्रेन्द्र माहात्म्यं परमेष्टिनः ।
सर्वपापहरं पुण्यं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं नृणाम् ॥
1.39.m:
Sanaka said:
Listen again, O best of Brahmins, to the eulogy of greatness of the supreme lord,
which removes all sins, is holy, and grants enjoyment and liberation to men.

1.39.s:
aho harikathā loke pāpaghnī puṇyadāyinī /
śṛṇvatāṃ vadatāṃ caiva tadbhaktānāṃ viśeṣataḥ //
1.39.d:
अहो हरिकथा लोके पापघ्नी पुण्यदायिनी ।
शृण्वतां वदतां चैव तद्भक्तानां विशेषतः ॥
1.39.m:
Ah, the discourse about Hari in the world destroys sins and bestows merit,
especially for those who hear it and speak it, and for his devotees!

1.39.s:
haribhaktirasāsvādamuditā ye narottamāḥ /
namaskaromyahaṃ tebhyo yatsaṃgānmukti bhāgnaraḥ //
1.39.d:
हरिभक्तिरसास्वादमुदिता ये नरोत्तमाः ।
नमस्करोम्यहं तेभ्यो यत्संगान्मुक्ति भाग्नरः ॥
1.39.m:
To those best among men who rejoice in savoring the nectar of devotion to Hari,
I bow down to them, by contact with whom a man attains liberation.

1.39.s:
haribhaktiparā ye tu harināmaparāyaṇāḥ /
durvṛttā vā suvṛttā vā tebhyo nityaṃ namonamaḥ //
1.39.d:
हरिभक्तिपरा ये तु हरिनामपरायणाः ।
दुर्वृत्ता वा सुवृत्ता वा तेभ्यो नित्यं नमोनमः ॥
1.39.m:
Those devoted to devotion to Hari and dedicated to the name of Hari,
whether ill-conducted or well-conducted, to them be homage again and again forever!

1.39.s:
saṃsārasāgaraṃ tartuṃ ya icchenmu nipuṅgava /
sa bhajeddharibhaktānāṃ bhaktānvai pāpahāriṇaḥ //
1.39.d:
संसारसागरं तर्तुं य इच्छेन्मु निपुङ्गव ।
स भजेद्धरिभक्तानां भक्तान्वै पापहारिणः ॥
1.39.m:
Whoever desires to cross the ocean of mundane existence, O foremost sage,
should revere the devotees of Hari's devotees, who remove sins.

1.39.s:
dṛṣṭaḥ smṛtaḥ pūjito vā dhyātaḥ praṇamito 'pi vā /
samuddharati govindo dustarādbhava sāgarāt //
1.39.d:
दृष्टः स्मृतः पूजितो वा ध्यातः प्रणमितो ऽपि वा ।
समुद्धरति गोविन्दो दुस्तराद्भव सागरात् ॥
1.39.m:
Seen, remembered, worshiped, meditated upon, or bowed to,
Govinda delivers [one] from the difficult-to-cross ocean of existence.

1.39.s:
svapanbhuñjan vrajaṃstiṣṭannatiṣṭaśca vadaṃstathā /
cintayedyo harernāma tasmai nityaṃ namo namaḥ //
1.39.d:
स्वपन्भुञ्जन् व्रजंस्तिष्टन्नतिष्टश्च वदंस्तथा ।
चिन्तयेद्यो हरेर्नाम तस्मै नित्यं नमो नमः ॥
1.39.m:
Sleeping, eating, walking, standing, sitting, or speaking,
whoever contemplates the name of Hari—to him be homage, homage forever!

1.39.s:
aho bhāgyamaho bhāgyaṃ viṣṇu bhaktiratātmanām /
yeṣāṃ muktiḥ karasthaiva yogināmapi durlabhā //
1.39.d:
अहो भाग्यमहो भाग्यं विष्णु भक्तिरतात्मनाम् ।
येषां मुक्तिः करस्थैव योगिनामपि दुर्लभा ॥
1.39.m:
Oh, what good fortune! Oh, what good fortune of those souls devoted to devotion to Viṣṇu,
for whom liberation, difficult to attain even for yogins, is right in hand!

1.39.s:
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam /
vadatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvapāpa praṇāśanam //
1.39.d:
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
वदतां शृण्वतां चैव सर्वपाप प्रणाशनम् ॥
1.39.m:
In this regard also they relate this ancient narrative,
which destroys all sins for both the tellers and the listeners:

1.39.s:
āsītpurā mahīpālaḥ somavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ /
jayadhvaja iti khyāto nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.39.d:
आसीत्पुरा महीपालः सोमवंशसमुद्भवः ।
जयध्वज इति ख्यातो नारायणपरायणः ॥
1.39.m:
Formerly there was an earth-protector born of the Lunar lineage,
known as Jayadhvaja, devoted to Nārāyaṇa.

1.39.s:
viṣṇordevālaye nityaṃ saṃmār janaparāyaṇaḥ /
dīpadānarataścaiva sarvabhūtadayāparaḥ //
1.39.d:
विष्णोर्देवालये नित्यं संमार् जनपरायणः ।
दीपदानरतश्चैव सर्वभूतदयापरः ॥
1.39.m:
He was constantly engaged in sweeping the temple of Viṣṇu,
devoted to offering lamps, and intent on compassion toward all beings.

1.39.s:
sa kadācinmahīpālo revātīre manorame /
vicitrakusumopetaṃ kṛtavānviṣṇumandiram //
1.39.d:
स कदाचिन्महीपालो रेवातीरे मनोरमे ।
विचित्रकुसुमोपेतं कृतवान्विष्णुमन्दिरम् ॥
1.39.m:
Once that earth-protector built on the delightful bank of the Revā
a temple of Viṣṇu furnished with various flowers.

1.39.s:
sa tatra nṛpaśārdūlaḥ sadā saṃmārjane rataḥ /
dīpadānaparaścaiva viśeṣeṇa haripriyaḥ //
1.39.d:
स तत्र नृपशार्दूलः सदा संमार्जने रतः ।
दीपदानपरश्चैव विशेषेण हरिप्रियः ॥
1.39.m:
There that tiger among kings was always engaged in sweeping
and dedicated to offering lamps, especially dear to Hari.

1.39.s:
harināmaparo nityaṃ harisaṃsaktamānasaḥ /
paripraṇāmanirato haribhaktajanapriyaḥ //
1.39.d:
हरिनामपरो नित्यं हरिसंसक्तमानसः ।
परिप्रणामनिरतो हरिभक्तजनप्रियः ॥
1.39.m:
Constantly devoted to the name of Hari, his mind fixed on Hari,
intent on offering prostrations, dear to the devotees of Hari.

1.39.s:
vītihotra iti khyāto hyāsīttasya purohitaḥ /
jayadhvajasya caritaṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayamāgataḥ //
1.39.d:
वीतिहोत्र इति ख्यातो ह्यासीत्तस्य पुरोहितः ।
जयध्वजस्य चरितं दृष्ट्वा विस्मयमागतः ॥
1.39.m:
There was his royal priest, known as Vītihotra,
who, seeing the conduct of Jayadhvaja, was struck with wonder.

1.39.s:
kadācidupaviṣṭaṃ taṃ rājānaṃ viṣṇutatparam /
apṛcchadvītihotrastu vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ //
1.39.d:
कदाचिदुपविष्टं तं राजानं विष्णुतत्परम् ।
अपृच्छद्वीतिहोत्रस्तु वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ॥
1.39.m:
Once Vītihotra, who had mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences,
asked that king who was seated and devoted to Viṣṇu:

1.39.s:
vītihotra uvāca
rājanparamadharmajña haribhaktiparāyaṇa /
viṣṇubhaktimatāṃ puṃsāṃ śreṣṭho 'si bharatarṣabha //
1.39.d:
वीतिहोत्र उवाच
राजन्परमधर्मज्ञ हरिभक्तिपरायण ।
विष्णुभक्तिमतां पुंसां श्रेष्ठो ऽसि भरतर्षभ ॥
1.39.m:
Vītihotra said:
O king, knower of the highest dharma, devoted to devotion to Hari,
you are the best among men possessing devotion to Viṣṇu, O bull of the Bharatas!

1.39.s:
saṃmārjanaparo nityaṃ dīpadānaratastathā /
tanme vada mahābhāga kiṃ tvayā viditaṃ phalam //
1.39.d:
संमार्जनपरो नित्यं दीपदानरतस्तथा ।
तन्मे वद महाभाग किं त्वया विदितं फलम् ॥
1.39.m:
You are constantly intent on sweeping and devoted to offering lamps;
tell me that, O fortunate one: what fruit has been realized by you?

1.39.s:
saṃpādanena varttīnāṃ tailasaṃpalādanena ca /
saṃyukto 'si sadā bhadrayadviṣṇorgṛhamārjane //
1.39.d:
संपादनेन वर्त्तीनां तैलसंपलादनेन च ।
संयुक्तो ऽसि सदा भद्रयद्विष्णोर्गृहमार्जने ॥
1.39.m:
By preparing wicks and supplying oil,
you are always occupied, O good one, in sweeping the temple of Viṣṇu.

1.39.s:
karmāṇyanyāni saṃtyeva viṣṇoḥ prītikarāṇi ca /
tathāpi kiṃ mahābhāga etayoḥ satatodyataḥ //
1.39.d:
कर्माण्यन्यानि संत्येव विष्णोः प्रीतिकराणि च ।
तथापि किं महाभाग एतयोः सततोद्यतः ॥
1.39.m:
There are indeed other deeds that please Viṣṇu;
nevertheless, O fortunate one, why are you constantly engaged in these two?

1.39.s:
sarvātmanā mahāpuṇyaṃ nareśa vidita ca yat /
tad brūhi me guhyatamaṃ prītirmayi tavāsti cet //
1.39.d:
सर्वात्मना महापुण्यं नरेश विदित च यत् ।
तद् ब्रूहि मे गुह्यतमं प्रीतिर्मयि तवास्ति चेत् ॥
1.39.m:
What great merit is known [to you] wholeheartedly, O lord of men,
tell me that most secret thing, if you have affection for me.

1.39.s:
purodhasaivamuktastu prahasansa jayadhvajaḥ /
vinayāvanato bhūtvā provācejaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ //
1.39.d:
पुरोधसैवमुक्तस्तु प्रहसन्स जयध्वजः ।
विनयावनतो भूत्वा प्रोवाचेजं कृताञ्जलिः ॥
1.39.m:
Thus addressed by the royal priest, that Jayadhvaja, laughing softly
and having bent low with modesty, said this with folded hands:

1.39.s:
jayadhvaja uvāca
śṛṇuṣva vipraśārdūla mayaivācaritaṃ purā /
jātismaratvājjānāmi śrotṝṇāṃ vismayapradam //
1.39.d:
जयध्वज उवाच
शृणुष्व विप्रशार्दूल मयैवाचरितं पुरा ।
जातिस्मरत्वाज्जानामि श्रोतॄणां विस्मयप्रदम् ॥

1.39.s:
āsītpurā kṛtayuge brahmansvārociṣeṃ'tare /
raivato nāma viprendro vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ //
1.39.d:
आसीत्पुरा कृतयुगे ब्रह्मन्स्वारोचिषेंऽतरे ।
रैवतो नाम विप्रेन्द्रो वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ॥
1.39.m:
Formerly in the Kṛta age, O Brahmin, during the Svārociṣa interval,
there was a best of Brahmins named Raivata, who had mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences.

1.39.s:
ayājyayājakaścaiva sadaiva grāmayojakaḥ /
piśuno niṣṭhuraścaiva hyapaṇyānāṃ ca vikrayī //
1.39.d:
अयाज्ययाजकश्चैव सदैव ग्रामयोजकः ।
पिशुनो निष्ठुरश्चैव ह्यपण्यानां च विक्रयी ॥
1.39.m:
He sacrificed for those not entitled to sacrifice, always caused dissension in villages,
was malicious, harsh, and a seller of prohibited goods.

1.39.s:
niṣiddhakarmācaraṇātparityaktaḥ sa bandhubhiḥ /
daridro duḥkhitaścaiva śīrṇāṅgo vyādhito 'bhavat //
1.39.d:
निषिद्धकर्माचरणात्परित्यक्तः स बन्धुभिः ।
दरिद्रो दुःखितश्चैव शीर्णाङ्गो व्याधितो ऽभवत् ॥
1.39.m:
Because of performing forbidden actions, he was abandoned by his kinsmen;
he became poor, wretched, emaciated, and diseased.

1.39.s:
sa kadāciddharthaṃ tu pṛthivyāṃ paryaṭan dvijaḥ /
mamāra narmadātīre śvāsakāsaprapīḍitaḥ //
1.39.d:
स कदाचिद्धर्थं तु पृथिव्यां पर्यटन् द्विजः ।
ममार नर्मदातीरे श्वासकासप्रपीडितः ॥
1.39.m:
Once, wandering the earth for wealth, that twice-born man
died on the bank of the Narmadā, afflicted by asthma and cough.

1.39.s:
tasminmṛte tasya bhāryā nāmnā bandhumatī mune /
kāmacāraparā sā tu parityaktā ca bandhubhiḥ //
1.39.d:
तस्मिन्मृते तस्य भार्या नाम्ना बन्धुमती मुने ।
कामचारपरा सा तु परित्यक्ता च बन्धुभिः ॥
1.39.m:
When he died, his wife, named Bandhumatī, O sage,
followed her wanton desires and was abandoned by her kinsmen.

1.39.s:
tasyāṃ jāto 'smi caṇḍālo daṇḍaketuriti śrutaḥ /
mahāpāparato nityaṃ brahmadveṣaparāyaṇaḥ //
1.39.d:
तस्यां जातो ऽस्मि चण्डालो दण्डकेतुरिति श्रुतः ।
महापापरतो नित्यं ब्रह्मद्वेषपरायणः ॥
1.39.m:
From her I was born as an outcaste, known as Daṇḍaketu,
constantly devoted to great sin, intent on hatred of Brahmins.

1.39.s:
paradāraparadravyalolupo jantuhiṃsakaḥ /
gāvaśca viprā bahavo nihatā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ //
1.39.d:
परदारपरद्रव्यलोलुपो जन्तुहिंसकः ।
गावश्च विप्रा बहवो निहता मृगपक्षिणः ॥
1.39.m:
Covetous of other men's wives and other men's property, an injurer of living beings,
by whom many cows, Brahmins, deer, and birds were killed.

1.39.s:
merutulyasuvarṇāni bahūnyapahṛtāni ca /
madyapānarato nityaṃ bahuśo mārgarodhakṛt //
1.39.d:
मेरुतुल्यसुवर्णानि बहून्यपहृतानि च ।
मद्यपानरतो नित्यं बहुशो मार्गरोधकृत् ॥
1.39.m:
Much gold equal to Mount Meru was stolen [by me];
constantly addicted to drinking liquor, frequently a blocker of the road.

1.39.s:
paśupakṣimṛgādīnāṃ jantūnāmantakopamaḥ /
kadācitkāmasaṃtapto gantu kāmo ratiṃ striyaḥ //
1.39.d:
पशुपक्षिमृगादीनां जन्तूनामन्तकोपमः ।
कदाचित्कामसंतप्तो गन्तु कामो रतिं स्त्रियः ॥
1.39.m:
Like the God of Death to beasts, birds, deer, and other living creatures;
once, tormented by lust, wishing to engage in sexual union with a woman,

1.39.s:
śūnyaṃ viṣṇugṛhaṃ dṛṣṭvā praviṣṭaśca striyā saha /
niśi rāmopabhogārthaṃ śayitaṃ tatra kāminā //
1.39.d:
शून्यं विष्णुगृहं दृष्ट्वा प्रविष्टश्च स्त्रिया सह ।
निशि रामोपभोगार्थं शयितं तत्र कामिना ॥
1.39.m:
and seeing a deserted house of Viṣṇu, I entered with the woman;
at night, in order to enjoy the lovely woman, [I] lay there as a passionate lover.

1.39.s:
brahmansvavastraprāntena kiyaddeśaḥ pramārjitaḥ /
yāvantyaḥ pāṃśukaṇikāstatra saṃmārjitā dvija //
1.39.d:
ब्रह्मन्स्ववस्त्रप्रान्तेन कियद्देशः प्रमार्जितः ।
यावन्त्यः पांशुकणिकास्तत्र संमार्जिता द्विज ॥
1.39.m:
O Brahmin, with the hem of my garment some space was wiped clean;
as many specks of dust as were swept away there, O twice-born one,

1.39.s:
tāvajjanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tadaiva kṣayamāgatam /
pradīpaḥ sthāpitastatra suratārthaṃ dvijottama //
1.39.d:
तावज्जन्मकृतं पापं तदैव क्षयमागतम् ।
प्रदीपः स्थापितस्तत्र सुरतार्थं द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.39.m:
the sin committed over that many births was wiped out right then!
A lamp was set up there for the sake of sexual intercourse, O best of the twice-born;

1.39.s:
tenāpi mama duṣkarma niḥśeṣaṃ kṣayamāgatam /
evaṃ sthite viṣṇugṛhe hyāgatāḥ purapālakāḥ //
1.39.d:
तेनापि मम दुष्कर्म निःशेषं क्षयमागतम् ।
एवं स्थिते विष्णुगृहे ह्यागताः पुरपालकाः ॥
1.39.m:
by that too, my evil deeds were completely brought to an end.
While we were thus staying in the house of Viṣṇu, the city-guards arrived.

1.39.s:
jāro 'yamiti māṃ tāṃ ca hatavantaḥ prasahya vai /
āvāṃ nihatya te sarve nivṛttāḥ purakṣakāḥ //
1.39.d:
जारो ऽयमिति मां तां च हतवन्तः प्रसह्य वै ।
आवां निहत्य ते सर्वे निवृत्ताः पुरक्षकाः ॥
1.39.m:
Saying, ‘This is an adulterer!’ they forcefully killed me and her;
having killed the two of us, all those city-guards turned back.

1.39.s:
yadā tadaiva saṃprāptā viṣṇudūtāścaturbhujāḥ /
kirīṭakuṇḍaladharā vanamālāvibhūṣitāḥ //
1.39.d:
यदा तदैव संप्राप्ता विष्णुदूताश्चतुर्भुजाः ।
किरीटकुण्डलधरा वनमालाविभूषिताः ॥
1.39.m:
Just then the four-armed messengers of Viṣṇu arrived,
wearing crowns and earrings, and adorned with forest-flower garlands.

1.39.s:
taistu saṃpreritāvāvāṃ viṣṇudūtairakalmaṣaiḥ /
divyaṃ vimānamāruhya sarvabhogasamanvitam //
1.39.d:
तैस्तु संप्रेरितावावां विष्णुदूतैरकल्मषैः ।
दिव्यं विमानमारुह्य सर्वभोगसमन्वितम् ॥
1.39.m:
Impelled by those spotless messengers of Viṣṇu,
having mounted a divine aerial chariot equipped with all enjoyments,

1.39.s:
divyadehadharau bhūtvā viṣṇulokamupāgatau /
tatra sthitvā brahmakalpaśataṃ sāgraṃ dvijottama //
1.39.d:
दिव्यदेहधरौ भूत्वा विष्णुलोकमुपागतौ ।
तत्र स्थित्वा ब्रह्मकल्पशतं साग्रं द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.39.m:
assuming divine bodies, we reached the world of Viṣṇu.
Having stayed there for fully a hundred Kalpas of Brahmā, O best of the twice-born,

1.39.s:
divyabhogasamāyuktau tāvatkālaṃ divi sthitau /
tataśca bhūmibhāgeṣu devayogeṣu vai kramāt //
1.39.d:
दिव्यभोगसमायुक्तौ तावत्कालं दिवि स्थितौ ।
ततश्च भूमिभागेषु देवयोगेषु वै क्रमात् ॥
1.39.m:
accompanied by divine enjoyments, we dwelt in heaven for so long a time;
and then, gradually in various parts of the earth among connections with the gods,

1.39.s:
tena puṇyaprabhāveṇa yadūnāṃ vaṃśasaṃbhavaḥ /
tenaiva me 'cyutā saṃpattathā rājyamakaṇṭakam //
1.39.d:
तेन पुण्यप्रभावेण यदूनां वंशसंभवः ।
तेनैव मे ऽच्युता संपत्तथा राज्यमकण्टकम् ॥
1.39.m:
by the power of that merit, [I had] birth in the lineage of the Yadus;
by that very [merit] I gained unfailing prosperity as well as an unthreatened kingdom.

1.39.s:
brahmankṛtvopabhogārthamevaṃ śreyo hyavāptavān /
bhaktyā kurvanti ye saṃtasteṣāṃ puṇyaṃ na vedyaham //
1.39.d:
ब्रह्मन्कृत्वोपभोगार्थमेवं श्रेयो ह्यवाप्तवान् ।
भक्त्या कुर्वन्ति ये संतस्तेषां पुण्यं न वेद्यहम् ॥
1.39.m:
O Brahmin, having done [that] merely for enjoyment, I attained such welfare!
I do not even know the merit of those good people who perform [it] with devotion.

1.39.s:
tasmātsaṃmārjane nityaṃ dīpadāne ca sattama /
yatiṣye parayā bhaktyā hyahaṃ jātismaro yataḥ //
1.39.d:
तस्मात्संमार्जने नित्यं दीपदाने च सत्तम ।
यतिष्ये परया भक्त्या ह्यहं जातिस्मरो यतः ॥
1.39.m:
Therefore, O best of men, I will constantly strive in sweeping
and in offering lamps with supreme devotion, since I remember my past lives.

1.39.s:
yaḥ pūjayejjagannāthamekākī vigataspṛhaḥ /
sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ prayāti paramaṃ padam //
1.39.d:
यः पूजयेज्जगन्नाथमेकाकी विगतस्पृहः ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तः प्रयाति परमं पदम् ॥
1.39.m:
Whoever worships the Lord of the Universe alone, free from desire,
is liberated from all sins and goes to the supreme abode.

1.39.s:
avaśenāpi yatkarma kṛtvemāṃ śriyamāgataḥ /
bhaktibhadbhiḥ praśāntaiśca kiṃ punaḥ samyagarcanāt //
1.39.d:
अवशेनापि यत्कर्म कृत्वेमां श्रियमागतः ।
भक्तिभद्भिः प्रशान्तैश्च किं पुनः सम्यगर्चनात् ॥
1.39.m:
When by an act done even involuntarily I attained this glory,
what need be said of [the result] from proper worship by peaceful people endowed with devotion?

1.39.s:
iti bhūpavacaḥ śrutvā vītihotro dvijottamaḥ /
anantatuṣṭimāpanno haripūjāparo 'bhavat //
1.39.d:
इति भूपवचः श्रुत्वा वीतिहोत्रो द्विजोत्तमः ।
अनन्ततुष्टिमापन्नो हरिपूजापरो ऽभवत् ॥
1.39.m:
Having heard this speech of the king, Vītihotra, best of the twice-born,
attained boundless satisfaction and became devoted to the worship of Hari.

1.39.s:
tasmācchṛṇuṣva viprendra devo nārāyaṇo 'vyayaḥ /
jñānato 'jñānato vāpi pūjakānāṃ vimuktidaḥ //
1.39.d:
तस्माच्छृणुष्व विप्रेन्द्र देवो नारायणो ऽव्ययः ।
ज्ञानतो ऽज्ञानतो वापि पूजकानां विमुक्तिदः ॥
1.39.m:
Therefore listen, O best of Brahmins: the imperishable god Nārāyaṇa
grants liberation to his worshipers, whether [done] knowingly or unknowingly.

1.39.s:
anityā bāndhavāḥ sarve vibhavo naiva śāśvataḥ /
nityaṃ sannihito mṛtyuḥ kartavyo dharmasaṃgrahaḥ //
1.39.d:
अनित्या बान्धवाः सर्वे विभवो नैव शाश्वतः ।
नित्यं सन्निहितो मृत्युः कर्तव्यो धर्मसंग्रहः ॥
1.39.m:
All kinsmen are impermanent, wealth is by no means eternal,
death is ever at hand; an accumulation of dharma must be made.

1.39.s:
ajño loko vṛthā garvaṃ kariṣyati mahoddhataḥ /
kāyaḥ saṃnihitāpāyo dhānādīnāṃ kimucyate //
1.39.d:
अज्ञो लोको वृथा गर्वं करिष्यति महोद्धतः ।
कायः संनिहितापायो धानादीनां किमुच्यते ॥
1.39.m:
An ignorant person, exceedingly arrogant, will take pride in vain;
the body is subject to imminent ruin—what need be said of grain and other possessions?

1.39.s:
janmakoṭisahasreṣu puṇyaṃ yaiḥ samupārjitam /
teṣāṃ bhaktirbhavecchuddhā devadeve janārdane //
1.39.d:
जन्मकोटिसहस्रेषु पुण्यं यैः समुपार्जितम् ।
तेषां भक्तिर्भवेच्छुद्धा देवदेवे जनार्दने ॥
1.39.m:
Only those who have accumulated merit through thousands of crores of births
possess pure devotion toward the god of gods, Janārdana.

1.39.s:
sulabhaṃ jāhnavī snānaṃ tathevātithipūjanam /
sulabhāḥ sarvayajñāśca viṣṇubhaktiḥ sudurlabhā //
1.39.d:
सुलभं जाह्नवी स्नानं तथेवातिथिपूजनम् ।
सुलभाः सर्वयज्ञाश्च विष्णुभक्तिः सुदुर्लभा ॥
1.39.m:
Bathing in the Gaṅgā is easily attained, and likewise the honoring of guests;
all sacrifices are easily performed, but devotion to Viṣṇu is very difficult to attain.

1.39.s:
durlabhā tulasīsevā durlabhaḥ saṃgamaḥ satām /
sarvabhūtadayā vāpi sulabhā yasya kasya cit //
1.39.d:
दुर्लभा तुलसीसेवा दुर्लभः संगमः सताम् ।
सर्वभूतदया वापि सुलभा यस्य कस्य चित् ॥
1.39.m: Rare is service to tulasī; rare is company of the good; / or compassion for all beings is easy only for some rare person.

1.39.s: satsaṃgastulasīsebā haribhaktiśca durlabhā //
1.39.d: सत्संगस्तुलसीसेबा हरिभक्तिश्च दुर्लभा ॥
1.39.m: Company of the good, service to tulasī, and devotion to Hari are rare.

1.39.s:
durlabhaṃ prāpyaṃ mānuṣyaṃ na tathā gamayed budhaḥ /
arcayeddhi jagannāthaṃ sārametaddvijottama //
1.39.d:
दुर्लभं प्राप्यं मानुष्यं न तथा गमयेद् बुधः ।
अर्चयेद्धि जगन्नाथं सारमेतद्द्विजोत्तम ॥
1.39.m: Having obtained human birth, which is rare, a wise person should not waste it so; / rather, he should worship the Lord of the Universe, for this is the essence, O best of the twice-born.

1.39.s:
tarttuṃ yadīcchati jano dustaraṃ bhavasāgaram /
haribhaktiparo bhūyādetadeva rasāyanam //
1.39.d:
तर्त्तुं यदीच्छति जनो दुस्तरं भवसागरम् ।
हरिभक्तिपरो भूयादेतदेव रसायनम् ॥
1.39.m: If a person wishes to cross the ocean of mundane existence, difficult to cross, / he should become devoted to devotion to Hari; this alone is the elixir.

1.39.s:
bhrātarāśraya govindaṃ mā vilaṃbaṃ kuru priya /
āsannameva nagaraṃ kṛtāntasya hi dṛśyate //
1.39.d:
भ्रातराश्रय गोविन्दं मा विलंबं कुरु प्रिय ।
आसन्नमेव नगरं कृतान्तस्य हि दृश्यते ॥
1.39.m: O brother, take refuge in Govinda! Do not delay, dear one! / For the city of the Ender of Life [Yama] is already seen nearby.

1.39.s:
nārāyaṇaṃ jagadyoniṃ sarvakāraṇakāraṇam /
samarcayasva viprendra yadi bhuktimabhīpsasi //
1.39.d:
नारायणं जगद्योनिं सर्वकारणकारणम् ।
समर्चयस्व विप्रेन्द्र यदि भुक्तिमभीप्ससि ॥
1.39.m: Nārāyaṇa, the origin of the world, the cause of all causes— / worship Him, O leader of Brahmins, if you desire worldly enjoyment [and liberation].

1.39.s:
sarvādhāra sarvayoniṃ sarvāntaryāmiṇaṃ vibhum /
ye prapannā mahātmānaste kṛtārthā na saṃśayaḥ //
1.39.d:
सर्वाधार सर्वयोनिं सर्वान्तर्यामिणं विभुम् ।
ये प्रपन्ना महात्मानस्ते कृतार्था न संशयः ॥
1.39.m: The support of all, the source of all, the inner ruler of all, the omnipresent Lord— / those great-souled ones who have surrendered to Him have achieved their aim; there is no doubt.

1.39.s:
te vandyāste prapūjyāśca namaskāryā viśeṣataḥ /
yer'cayanti mahāviṣṇuṃ praṇatārtipraṇāśanam //
1.39.d:
ते वन्द्यास्ते प्रपूज्याश्च नमस्कार्या विशेषतः ।
येर्ऽचयन्ति महाविष्णुं प्रणतार्तिप्रणाशनम् ॥
1.39.m: They are to be praised, they are to be revered, and especially to be saluted, / who worship Mahāviṣṇu, the destroyer of the distress of those who bow to Him.

1.39.s:
ye viṣṇubhaktā niṣkāmā yañjati parameśvaram /
triḥsaptakulasaṃyuktā ste yānti harimandiram //
1.39.d:
ये विष्णुभक्ता निष्कामा यञ्जति परमेश्वरम् ।
त्रिःसप्तकुलसंयुक्ता स्ते यान्ति हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
1.39.m: The devotees of Viṣṇu who worship the supreme Lord without desire, / joined with twenty-one generations of their family, go to Hari's mansion.

1.39.s:
viṣṇubhaktāya yo dadyānniṣkāmāya mahātmane /
pānīyaṃ vā phalaṃ vāpi sa eva bhagavatpriyaḥ //
1.39.d:
विष्णुभक्ताय यो दद्यान्निष्कामाय महात्मने ।
पानीयं वा फलं वापि स एव भगवत्प्रियः ॥
1.39.m: Whoever gives even water or fruit to a great-souled devotee of Viṣṇu / who is free from desire, that person is dear to the Lord.

1.39.s:
viṣṇubhaktiparāṇāṃ tu śuśrūṣāṃ kurvate tu ye /
te yānti viṣṇubhuvanaṃ yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam //
1.39.d:
विष्णुभक्तिपराणां तु शुश्रूषां कुर्वते तु ये ।
ते यान्ति विष्णुभुवनं यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् ॥
1.39.m: Those who perform service to those intent on devotion to Viṣṇu / go to the world of Viṣṇu until the dissolution of all beings.

1.39.s:
ye yañjati spṛhāśūnyā haribhaktān hariṃ tathā /
ta eva bhuvanaṃ sarvaṃ puṃnati svāṅghripāṃśunā //
1.39.d:
ये यञ्जति स्पृहाशून्या हरिभक्तान् हरिं तथा ।
त एव भुवनं सर्वं पुंनति स्वाङ्घ्रिपांशुना ॥
1.39.m: Those who, free of desire, worship Hari's devotees as well as Hari, / purify the entire world with the dust of their feet.

1.39.s:
devapūjāparo yasya gṛhe vasati sarvadā /
tatraiva sarvadevāśca tiṣṭanti śrīharistathā //
1.39.d:
देवपूजापरो यस्य गृहे वसति सर्वदा ।
तत्रैव सर्वदेवाश्च तिष्टन्ति श्रीहरिस्तथा ॥
1.39.m: In whose house one devoted to the worship of God always resides, / right there dwell all the gods, and so does Śrī Hari.

1.39.s:
pūjyamānā ca tulasī yasya tiṣṭati veśmani /
tatra sarvāṇi śreyāṃsi varddhatyaharahardvija //
1.39.d:
पूज्यमाना च तुलसी यस्य तिष्टति वेश्मनि ।
तत्र सर्वाणि श्रेयांसि वर्द्धत्यहरहर्द्विज ॥
1.39.m: And in whose dwelling tulasī stays, being worshipped, / there all blessings increase day by day, O twice-born.

1.39.s:
śālagrāmaśilārūpī yatra tiṣṭati keśavaḥ /
na bādhante grahāstatra bhūtavetāla kādayaḥ //
1.39.d:
शालग्रामशिलारूपी यत्र तिष्टति केशवः ।
न बाधन्ते ग्रहास्तत्र भूतवेताल कादयः ॥
1.39.m: Where Keśava resides in the form of a śālagrāma stone, / there planets, bhūtas, vetālas, and other [evil spirits] do not torment.

1.39.s:
śālagrāmaśilā yatra tattīrthaṃ tattapovanam /
yataḥ saṃnihitastatra bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ //
1.39.d:
शालग्रामशिला यत्र तत्तीर्थं तत्तपोवनम् ।
यतः संनिहितस्तत्र भगवान्मधुसूदनः ॥
1.39.m: Where the śālagrāma stone is, that is a sacred ford, that is a penance grove, / because the blessed Madhusūdana is present there.

1.39.s:
yadgṛhe nāsti devarṣe śālagrāmaśilārcanam /
śmaśānasadṛśaṃ vidyāttada gṛhaṃ śubhavārjitam //
purāṇanyāyamīmāṃsā dharmaśāstrāṇi ca dvija //
1.39.d:
यद्गृहे नास्ति देवर्षे शालग्रामशिलार्चनम् ।
श्मशानसदृशं विद्यात्तद गृहं शुभवार्जितम् ॥
पुराणन्यायमीमांसा धर्मशास्त्राणि च द्विज ॥
1.39.m: In whose house there is no worship of the śālagrāma stone, O divine sage, / one should know that house to be like a cremation ground, devoid of auspiciousness. / Purāṇas, Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā, and Dharmaśāstras, O twice-born,

1.39.s: sāṃgā vedāstathā sarve viṣṇorūpaṃ prakīrtitam //
1.39.d: सांगा वेदास्तथा सर्वे विष्णोरूपं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
1.39.m: as well as all the Vedas with their auxiliary limbs, are proclaimed to be the form of Viṣṇu.

1.39.s:
bhaktyā kurvanti ye viṣṇoḥ pradakṣiṇacatuṣṭayam /
te 'pi yānti paraṃ sthānaṃ sarvakarmanibarhaṇam //
iti bṛhannāradīyapurāṇe pūrvabhāge prathama pāde viṣṇumāhātmyaṃ nāma ekonacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.39.d:
भक्त्या कुर्वन्ति ये विष्णोः प्रदक्षिणचतुष्टयम् ।
ते ऽपि यान्ति परं स्थानं सर्वकर्मनिबर्हणम् ॥
इति बृहन्नारदीयपुराणे पूर्वभागे प्रथम पादे विष्णुमाहात्म्यं नाम एकोनचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
1.39.m:
Those who perform four circumambulations of Viṣṇu with devotion, / they too go to the supreme abode, the destroyer of all karmic actions.

Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, named Viṣṇumāhātmya, in the first quarter of the Pūrvabhāga of the Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa.

1.40.s:
sanaka uvāca
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi vibhūtiṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ mune /
yāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ kīrtayatāṃ sadyaḥ pāpakṣayo bhavet //
1.40.d:
सनक उवाच
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि विभूतिं वैष्णवीं मुने ।
यां शृण्वतां कीर्तयतां सद्यः पापक्षयो भवेत् ॥
1.40.m: Sanaka said: / Henceforth I shall declare the Vaiṣṇava splendour, O sage, / hearing and chanting which causes the immediate destruction of sins.

1.40.s:
vaivasvateṃ'tare pūrvaṃ śakrasya ca bṛhaspateḥ /
saṃvādaḥ sumahānāsīttaṃ vakṣyāmi niśāmaya //
1.40.d:
वैवस्वतेंऽतरे पूर्वं शक्रस्य च बृहस्पतेः ।
संवादः सुमहानासीत्तं वक्ष्यामि निशामय ॥
1.40.m: Formerly, in the Vaivasvata interval, there was a great dialogue / between Śakra and Bṛhaspati; I shall relate it, listen.

1.40.s:
ekadā sarvabhogāḍhyo vibudhaiḥ parivāritaḥ /
apsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇo bṛhaspatimabhāṣata //
1.40.d:
एकदा सर्वभोगाढ्यो विबुधैः परिवारितः ।
अप्सरोगणसंकीर्णो बृहस्पतिमभाषत ॥
1.40.m: Once, rich in all enjoyments, surrounded by the gods, / crowded by crowds of apsarases, he spoke to Bṛhaspati.

1.40.s:
indra uvāca
bṛhaspate mahābhāga sarvatattvārthakovida /
atītabrahmaṇaḥ kalpe sṛṣṭiḥ kīdṛgvidhā prabho //
1.40.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
बृहस्पते महाभाग सर्वतत्त्वार्थकोविद ।
अतीतब्रह्मणः कल्पे सृष्टिः कीदृग्विधा प्रभो ॥
1.40.m: Indra said: / O fortunate Bṛhaspati, knower of all true principles, / what was the creation like in the kalpa of the past Brahmā, O Lord?

1.40.s:
indrastu kīdṛśaḥ prokto vivudhāḥ kīdṛśāḥ smṛtāḥ /
teṣāṃ ca kīdṛśaṃ karma yathāvadvaktumarhasi //
1.40.d:
इन्द्रस्तु कीदृशः प्रोक्तो विवुधाः कीदृशाः स्मृताः ।
तेषां च कीदृशं कर्म यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
1.40.m: What kind of Indra was described? What kind were the gods said to be? / And what was their action like? You ought to speak accurately.

1.40.s:
bṛhaspatiruvāca
na jñāyate mayā śakra pūrvedyuścaritaṃ vidheḥ /
vartamānadinasyāpi durjñeyaṃ pratibhāti me //
1.40.d:
बृहस्पतिरुवाच
न ज्ञायते मया शक्र पूर्वेद्युश्चरितं विधेः ।
वर्तमानदिनस्यापि दुर्ज्ञेयं प्रतिभाति मे ॥
1.40.m: Bṛhaspati said: / The conduct of Brahmā on former days is not known by me, O Śakra; / even that of the present day appears difficult for me to know.

1.40.s:
manavaḥ samatītāśca tānvaktumapi na kṣamaḥ /
yo vijānāti taṃ te 'dya kathayāmi niśāmaya //
1.40.d:
मनवः समतीताश्च तान्वक्तुमपि न क्षमः ।
यो विजानाति तं ते ऽद्य कथयामि निशामय ॥
1.40.m: Nor am I capable of describing the Manus who have passed away. / Who knows it, that person I will tell you today; listen.

1.40.s:
sudharma iti vikhyātaḥ kaścidāste pure tava /
bhuñjāno divyabhogāṃśca brahmalokādihāgataḥ //
1.40.d:
सुधर्म इति विख्यातः कश्चिदास्ते पुरे तव ।
भुञ्जानो दिव्यभोगांश्च ब्रह्मलोकादिहागतः ॥
1.40.m: Renowned as Sudharmā, a certain one lives in your city, / enjoying divine pleasures, having come here from the world of Brahmā.

1.40.s:
sa vā eta dvijānāti kathayāmi niśāmaya /
evamuktastu guruṇā śakrastena samanvitaḥ //
1.40.d:
स वा एत द्विजानाति कथयामि निशामय ।
एवमुक्तस्तु गुरुणा शक्रस्तेन समन्वितः ॥
1.40.m: He indeed knows this; I shall speak, listen. / Having been thus addressed by the preceptor, Śakra, accompanied by him,

1.40.s: devatāgaṇasaṃkīrṇaḥ sudharmanilayaṃ yayau //
1.40.d: देवतागणसंकीर्णः सुधर्मनिलयं ययौ ॥
1.40.m: surrounded by the hosts of deities, went to the abode of Sudharmā.

1.40.s:
samāgataṃ devapatiṃ bṛhaspatisamanvitam /
dṛṣṭvā yathārhaṃ devarṣe pūjayāmāsa sādaram //
1.40.d:
समागतं देवपतिं बृहस्पतिसमन्वितम् ।
दृष्ट्वा यथार्हं देवर्षे पूजयामास सादरम् ॥
1.40.m: Seeing the lord of the gods arrived, accompanied by Bṛhaspati, / he worshipped them with respect according to their worth, O divine sage.

1.40.s:
sudharmeṇārcitaḥ śaṅkro dṛṣṭvā tacchriyamuttamām /
manasā vismayāviṣṭaḥ provāca vinayānvitaḥ //
1.40.d:
सुधर्मेणार्चितः शङ्क्रो दृष्ट्वा तच्छ्रियमुत्तमाम् ।
मनसा विस्मयाविष्टः प्रोवाच विनयान्वितः ॥
1.40.m: Śakra, worshipped by Sudharmā, seeing his excellent splendour, / was seized with wonder in his mind and spoke, filled with humility.

1.40.s:
indra uvāca
atītabrahmakalpasya vṛttāntaṃ vetsi cedbudha /
tadākhyāhi samāyāta etatpraṣṭuṃ sayājakaḥ //
1.40.d:
इन्द्र उवाच
अतीतब्रह्मकल्पस्य वृत्तान्तं वेत्सि चेद्बुध ।
तदाख्याहि समायात एतत्प्रष्टुं सयाजकः ॥
1.40.m: Indra said: / If you know the account of the past Brahmā-kalpa, O wise one, / then relate it; I have come together with my priest to ask this.

1.40.s:
gatanidrāṃśca devāṃśca yena jānāsi suvrata /
tadvadasvādhikaḥ kasmādasmadbhyo 'pi divi sthitaḥ //
1.40.d:
गतनिद्रांश्च देवांश्च येन जानासि सुव्रत ।
तद्वदस्वाधिकः कस्मादस्मद्भ्यो ऽपि दिवि स्थितः ॥
1.40.m: And how you know the gods who are sleepless, O you of noble vows, / tell that: why do you abide in heaven superior even to us,

1.40.s:
tejasāyaśasā kīrtyā jñānena ca parantapa /
dānena vā tapobhirvā kathametādṛśaḥ prabho //
1.40.d:
तेजसायशसा कीर्त्या ज्ञानेन च परन्तप ।
दानेन वा तपोभिर्वा कथमेतादृशः प्रभो ॥
1.40.m: in splendour, in fame, in renown, and in knowledge, O scorcher of foes, / or by gifts or by austerities? How is it such, O Lord?

1.40.s:
ityukto devarājena sudharmā prahasaṃstadā /
provāca vinayāviṣṭaḥ pūrvavṛttaṃ yathāvidhi //
1.40.d:
इत्युक्तो देवराजेन सुधर्मा प्रहसंस्तदा ।
प्रोवाच विनयाविष्टः पूर्ववृत्तं यथाविधि ॥
1.40.m: Thus addressed by the king of the gods, Sudharmā, smiling then, / filled with humility, properly related the past event.

1.40.s:
sudharma uvāca
caturyugasahasrāṇi brahmaṇo dinamucyate /
ekasmin divase śakra manavaśca caturdaśa //
1.40.d:
सुधर्म उवाच
चतुर्युगसहस्राणि ब्रह्मणो दिनमुच्यते ।
एकस्मिन् दिवसे शक्र मनवश्च चतुर्दश ॥
1.40.m: Sudharmā said: / A day of Brahmā is said to be four thousand yugas. / In a single day, O Śakra, there are fourteen Manus.

1.40.s:
indrāścaturdaśa proktā devāśca vividhāḥ pṛthak /
indrāṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ manvādīnāṃ ca vāsava //
1.40.d:
इन्द्राश्चतुर्दश प्रोक्ता देवाश्च विविधाः पृथक् ।
इन्द्राणां चैव सर्वेषां मन्वादीनां च वासव ॥
1.40.m: Fourteen Indras are proclaimed, and various gods separately. / And among all the Indras and the Manus and the others, O Vāsava,

1.40.s:
tulyatā tejasā lakṣmyā prabhāveṇa balena ca /
teṣāṃ nāmāni vakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣva susamāhitaḥ //
1.40.d:
तुल्यता तेजसा लक्ष्म्या प्रभावेण बलेन च ।
